title: Utilizing light energy transformation in nanostructures for targeted diagnostic and therapeutic applications.
abstract: Theranostics, a combination of therapy and diagnostics, represents a paradigm change in precision medicine with the ability to monitor diseases in real time and deliver targeted treatment. Nanomaterials are state-of-the-art technology for photo-energy conversion-based therapeutic action and diagnostic imaging; note the remarkable temporal and spatial precision that uses light as a driving force. This review highlights recent advances in the design and application of such nanomaterials for converting light into demand responses via mechanisms including photoluminescence (PL), photothermal conversion for photothermal therapy (PTT), photoacoustic imaging (PAI), photoelectric effect, SERS-based detection, and photodynamic therapy (PDT). Such light-activated systems are versatile platforms for the treatment of various diseases like arthritis, cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, and retinal degeneration. By integrating multiple therapeutic and diagnostic modalities into a single nanoscale system, photoactive nanomaterials hold the potential to achieve enhanced treatment efficacy with minimal side effects. However, rapid advances are still hindered by challenges related to maximizing tissue penetration and biocompatibility, as well as activation in physiological settings. Nevertheless, the synergy of light-based science and nanotechnology is enabling next-generation precision theranostics and dynamic tools for personalized medicine for physicians. For these intelligent nanoplatforms to reach their full potential in practical healthcare applications, more interdisciplinary research and clinical translation are required.

title: Association Between Glenohumeral Bony Morphology and Anterior Shoulder Instability: An Advanced Three-Dimensional Analysis.
abstract: Background Glenohumeral bony morphology plays an important role in anterior shoulder instability (ASI), but the specific acquired and constitutional anatomical features associated with ASI remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate and compare glenohumeral bony morphological characteristics between patients with ASI and controls using three-dimensional (3D) computed tomography (CT) imaging analysis. Methods A total of 210 participants were included, comprising 105 patients with unilateral ASI and at least one recurrence and 105 controls. Bilateral shoulder CT scans were obtained for the ASI group, whereas unilateral CT scans were obtained for the control group. The following parameters were measured on 3D models: glenoid index (GI), glenoid version angle, glenoid inclination angle, glenoid depth, humeral head containment angle, and the humeral head-to-glenoid diameter ratio. Within-patient comparisons were performed between affected and contralateral unaffected shoulders, and the contralateral unaffected shoulders were further compared with control shoulders. Sex-based subgroup analyses were also performed. Results The affected shoulders had a greater GI than the contralateral unaffected shoulders, with a mean paired difference of 0.19 (95% CI, 0.16-0.23; Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). The humeral head containment angle was nominally smaller on the affected side, but the difference did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons (raw P = 0.013; Holm-adjusted P = 0.067). Compared with control shoulders, the contralateral unaffected shoulders demonstrated a greater GI (1.39 ± 0.11 vs. 1.32 ± 0.10; mean difference, 0.07; 95% CI, 0.04-0.09; Holm-adjusted P < 0.001) and reduced glenoid depth (2.9 ± 0.8 mm vs. 3.6 ± 0.9 mm; Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in the remaining morphological parameters after Holm correction. In the exploratory sex-stratified analyses, greater GI and reduced glenoid depth remained significant among male participants, whereas no parameter differed significantly among female participants after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion ASI was associated with distinct glenohumeral bony morphological characteristics on 3D analysis. A greater glenoid index and reduced glenoid depth were the most consistent features, including in the contralateral unaffected shoulders of patients with ASI, suggesting a possible anatomical association. Level of evidence Level III, Cross-Sectional Design, Prognosis Study.

title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: the definition of Shoulder Periprosthetic Joint infection.
abstract: Background Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the greatest diagnostic and treatment challenges facing shoulder surgeons and their patients. A definition for shoulder PJI was established by the 2018 International Consensus Meeting (ICM) on Orthopedic Infections, but the selection and weighting of its minor criteria relied largely on expert opinion. The purpose of this study was to present an updated, evidence-based definition of shoulder PJI generated by the 2025 ICM Shoulder Group. Methods The 2025 ICM Shoulder Group, an international panel of shoulder surgeons and infectious disease specialists, used a modified Delphi process informed by 86 systematic reviews and by a predictive statistical model derived from the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) Multicenter Revision Arthroplasty and PJI Group dataset to reconsider the 2018 ICM definition of shoulder PJI, including its major criteria, minor criteria, and diagnostic categories. Results The delegates voted to eliminate organism virulence from the definition and to retain gross intra-articular purulence and presence of a sinus tract as the two criteria defining Definite PJI. The Minor Criteria were revised to include erythema, unexpected wound drainage, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP), elevated synovial neutrophil percentage, positive frozen section, radiographic humeral osteolysis, intraoperative humeral loosening, and positive culture, each statistically weighted using the predictive model. Non-definite PJI was categorized by summed minor criteria score as High likelihood (≥13 points), Moderate likelihood (7-12 points), Unknown (1-6 points), or No PJI (0 points). The final definition achieved unanimous delegate consensus (51 of 51 delegates; 100% agreement; super majority, strong consensus). Conclusions The 2025 ICM definition of shoulder PJI represents an evidence-informed evolution of the 2018 definition, combining statistical modeling of prospective multicenter data with structured expert consensus. The definition is expected to continue to evolve as further shoulder-specific data become available.

title: Preoperative Pseudoparesis Is Not Associated With Inferior Outcomes After Anterior Latissimus Dorsi and Teres Major Transfer for Irreparable Anterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
abstract: Background The prognostic relevance of preoperative pseudoparesis after combined anterior latissimus dorsi and teres major transfer (aLDTM) for irreparable anterosuperior rotator cuff tears (IASRCTs) has not been examined in a matched comparison. We hypothesized that, after propensity score matching, final outcomes would not differ significantly between groups. Methods This retrospective comparative cohort study reviewed patients undergoing aLDTM for IASRCT between April 2015 and January 2024. Pseudoparesis was defined a priori as active forward elevation ≥45° and <90° with preserved passive elevation after local anesthetic injection and without neurologic deficit (n=57); active forward elevation ≥90° defined the comparator group (n=183). True pseudoparalysis (<45°) and advanced arthropathy (Hamada grade >2) were excluded. One-to-one propensity score matching on age, sex, body mass index, diabetes, hypertension, previous cuff repair, acromiohumeral distance (AHD), Hamada grade, intraoperative reparable infraspinatus tear, and fatty infiltration of the four rotator cuff muscles produced 57 pairs (all absolute standardized mean differences <0.10). Outcomes included clinical scores (VAS, ADLIR, Constant, UCLA, ASES), range of motion, strength, subscapularis-specific tests, and tendon integrity on 2-year postoperative MRI. Mean follow-up was 57.0 ± 20.0 months. Results Both groups improved in clinical scores, forward elevation, abduction, internal rotation, and most strength measures (all adjusted P < .001); external rotation range of motion did not change significantly. Final clinical scores, range of motion, and strength showed no significant between-group differences (all adjusted P ≥ .569). The pseudoparesis group showed larger gains in forward elevation (69° ± 26° vs 35° ± 28°, adjusted P < .001) and abduction (48° ± 29° vs 29° ± 27°, adjusted P = .007). Subscapularis-specific tests and AHD did not differ between groups. Retear on 2-year postoperative MRI occurred in 3/57 (5.3%) and 4/57 (7.0%) (adjusted P = 1.000). Conclusion In this propensity score-matched analysis, the pseudoparesis group had lower baseline elevation by definition, whereas final clinical, range-of-motion, strength, and structural outcomes did not differ between groups after aLDTM for IASRCT. These findings should not be extrapolated to true pseudoparalysis or advanced arthropathy.

title: Predictive Modeling of Clinically Apparent Shoulder Periprosthetic Joint Infection (PJI).
abstract: Introduction The first International Consensus Meeting (ICM) definition of shoulder periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) introduced a tiered framework of PJI categories based on weighting of minor criteria for those cases not having major criteria of Definite infection. The selection of minor criteria and weightings was based on expert opinion and limited available evidence. The purpose of this study was to use prospective, multicenter data to develop a predictive model for clinically apparent shoulder PJI to inform a more evidence-based understanding of minor criteria and PJI categories. Methods Prospective data were collected on 861 consecutive revision shoulder arthroplasty cases within the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) Revision Shoulder Arthroplasty and PJI Multicenter Research Group. Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis and intra-articular purulence were identified as pathognomonic indicators of infection (major criteria) and used as the primary outcome for multivariable analysis. Logistic regression modeling was performed, with model specification guided by information criteria. Variable selection emphasized optimal model fit while balancing complexity, focusing on: (1) markers of host inflammatory response, (2) universally available and commonly utilized diagnostic tests, (3) minimizing the total number of variables, and (4) preserving model usability despite missing data. Results Among 861 cases, 97 shoulders (11%) met the outcome of interest (sinus tract or intra-articular purulence). The final model incorporated seven variables spanning clinical findings, laboratory values, imaging, intraoperative assessment, and microbiology. These variables were erythema, unexpected wound drainage, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) or C-reactive protein (CRP), radiographic humeral osteolysis, synovial neutrophils ≥70% or positive frozen section (≥5 polymorphonuclear cells in ≥5 high-powered fields), intraoperative humeral loosening, and ≥2 positive cultures with the same organism. The apparent concordance statistic in the development cohort was 0.90 (95% CI 0.87-0.94). A nomogram was subsequently developed to estimate the probability of PJI, defined by the presence of a sinus tract or intra-articular purulence. Conclusion Using prospective, multicenter data, this study proposes a seven-factor nomogram to estimate the probability of clinically apparent shoulder PJI. The model showed strong apparent discrimination for clinically apparent infection in the development cohort. External validation will be necessary to confirm performance, and consensus will be required to establish weighting and diagnostic thresholds for tiers of non-definite shoulder PJI.

title: The medial collapse sign is associated with cubitus varus after pediatric supracondylar humeral fracture fixation: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Cubitus varus deformity is a common complication following pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures and rarely remodels spontaneously. However, surgeons lack a reliable intraoperative radiographic sign that directly reflects inadequate medial column reduction. This study aimed to evaluate whether the medial collapse sign (MCS) on immediate postoperative anteroposterior radiographs is associated with postoperative cubitus varus. Methods A retrospective cohort study included pediatric patients who underwent surgical treatment for supracondylar humeral fractures consecutively between January 2016 and March 2024. Fifty-two patients treated with reduction and cross pinning and followed for at least 6 months were included. Patients were categorized according to the presence or absence of cubitus varus at final follow-up (n = 20 and n = 32, respectively), which was radiographically defined as a side-to-side carrying-angle difference ≥5° on standing anteroposterior radiographs. Univariable and multivariable analyses were performed using Firth's penalized logistic regression. Results Presence of the MCS was strongly associated with cubitus varus (OR 155.4, 95% CI 24.8-1965.5; Holm-adjusted P < .001). MCS remained associated after adjustment for medial cortical comminution (OR 47.5, 95% CI 6.6-590.4, Holm-adjusted P < .001). The large effect size should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size. Sensitivity and specificity were 90.0% and 96.9%, respectively. Interobserver reliability was almost perfect (κ = 0.919). Conclusion The medial collapse sign is strongly associated with postoperative cubitus varus and may reflect inadequate medial column reduction. Recognition of the same medial cortical morphology on intraoperative fluoroscopy may prompt reassessment of alignment and reduction. Level of evidence Level III, Retrospective cohort comparison, prognosis study.

title: Idiopathic Granulomatous Mastitis in Mexican Women: 11-Year Clinical, Imaging, and Pathology Review.
abstract: Introduction Idiopathic granulomatous mastitis (IGM) is a rare chronic inflammatory breast disease that mimics malignancy, often leading to delayed diagnosis and mismanagement. Data on IGM in Latin American populations are scarce. Materials and methods We conducted a retrospective study of 39 women diagnosed with IGM between 2013 and 2024 at a specialized breast center in Mexico. Clinical, radiological, pathological, and treatment data were extracted from records. All patients provided informed consent for participation in the study. Patient confidentiality was maintained throughout the study, and all data were analyzed in a deidentified manner. Results The mean age was 35 y; 91.9% were premenopausal and 79.5% had a history of pregnancy. Palpable mass (66.7%), pain (61.5%), and fistulas (33.3%) were common. Ultrasound revealed hypoechoic tubular lesions in 70.8%. Histology confirmed non-necrotizing granulomas in 92.3%, with frequent squamous metaplasia and plasmacytic infiltration. Corticosteroids were used in 94.9%; surgery in 5.1%. At 12 mo, 87.1% showed remission; 51.3% had residual breast deformity. Conclusions IGM in Mexican women presented with hallmark histological features but often at advanced stages. Early diagnosis is key to reducing long-term cosmetic sequelae.

title: Management of Brachial Plexus Neurogenic Tumors: A Retrospective Study of 25 Cases.
abstract: Introduction To investigate the clinical characteristics of cervical brachial plexus neurogenic tumors and enhance the diagnostic and therapeutic management of this condition. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 25 patients diagnosed with brachial plexus neurogenic tumors who were treated at a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Clinical manifestations, treatment strategies, and follow-up outcomes were systematically summarized. Results A total of 25 patients were included, treated across multiple departments: otorhinolaryngology-head and neck surgery, neurosurgery, orthopedics, thyroid surgery, and vascular surgery. There were 13 male and 12 female patients, aged 16-76 y, with a disease duration ranging from 1 wk to 2 y, defined as the interval from symptom onset to initial clinical evaluation. The primary presenting symptom was a neck root mass in 21 patients, among whom seven experienced ipsilateral upper limb numbness, soreness, or electric shock-like pain upon palpation and four reported sensory disturbances in the upper extremity or shoulder-back pain. All patients underwent cervical contrast-enhanced computed tomography, and 18 additionally received 3.0 T magnetic resonance imaging. Preoperative ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration cytology was performed in all cases, revealing spindle cell tumors with morphological features suggestive of schwannoma. Of the 25 patients, 23 underwent surgical resection, while two with small tumors (<2 cm), no neurological symptoms, and cytologically benign findings opted for conservative management with close observation. Surgical approaches included the anterior supraclavicular approach, the posterior cervical paravertebral approach, and clavicle-splitting (transclavicular) approach. Postoperative pathological examination confirmed benign schwannoma in 22 cases and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor in one case. Follow-up duration ranged from 12 to 60 mo. Transient postoperative neurological dysfunction occurred in five patients, manifesting as limited shoulder abduction, reduced wrist extensor strength, or limb numbness; all deficits resolved within 6 mo following structured rehabilitation programs. Conclusions Brachial plexus neurogenic tumors commonly present as a mass in the neck root, with a subset of cases accompanied by neurological symptoms. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are valuable modalities for tumor localization and qualitative characterization. Preoperative fine needle aspiration cytology enables a preliminary assessment of tumor histology. The selection of an appropriate surgical approach should be guided by tumor location and anatomical involvement. Intralesional enucleation is a key strategy for preserving neurological function, and when combined with microsurgical techniques and intraoperative nerve monitoring, even transient postoperative neurological deficits can be effectively managed through structured rehabilitation programs.

title: Histological Stages of Appendicitis Associated With Imaging Characteristics: A Computed Tomography and Ultrasound-Based Comparative Study.
abstract: Introduction Appendicitis diagnosis relies heavily on medical imaging procedure studies; however, a definite diagnosis is obtained through histological assessment. Understanding the imaging characteristics and their relation to various histological phases enhance the quality of treatment recommendations. This study analyzed imaging characteristics of acute appendicitis in relation to its histological severity. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted using data from a third-level hospital. Appendectomy specimens from patients with prior computed tomography (CT) scans or ultrasound (US) imaging were included. Histological stages were categorized into simple, suppurative, abscessed, and perforated phases, depending the presence of edema, vascular congestion, neutrophilic infiltrate into the muscular layer, microabscess formation, mucosal ulceration, purulent exudate, macroscopic pus, and perforation with transmural inflammation. Imaging features as fat stranding, presence of free fluid, contrast enhancement within the appendix, appendicolith detection, reactive lymph nodes in the vicinity, appendix diameter itself, increased echogenicity, and detecting heightened perfusion via Doppler imaging were compared across these stages. Results Among 760 patients included (51.4% women, mean age 30.1 ± 5.3), 196 (25.8%) had CT scans and 361 (47.5%) had US. CT confirmed appendicitis in 59.2% of cases, yielded a negative result in 19.4%, and provided an inconclusive diagnosis in 21.4% of cases, commonly identifying fat stranding, free liquid, and contrast enhancement. US diagnosed appendicitis in 67.6% of cases, whereas 32.4% were reported as negative, with findings including increased echogenicity, Doppler perfusion, appendix identification, and free liquid in the right parietocolic gutter. All imaging characteristics were less prevalent in early stages compared to advanced stages, with a higher negativity rate in earlier stages. Conclusions Imaging findings are associated with the histopathological severity of appendicitis. Increased histopathological severity is associated with greater frequency of CT and US findings. These relations suggest the potential for managing appendicitis based on the histological phase suspected from imaging findings. Further research is warranted.

title: Understanding Colorectal Cancer Screening Gaps Among Adults Aged 45-49.
abstract: Introduction The United States Preventative Task Force recommends initiating colorectal cancer (CRC) screening at age 45, but screening rates among 45-49 y-olds has been lower than older age groups. Reasons for low screening rates among younger individuals are not clear. Methods Using Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 2022 to 2024, we investigated factors associated with CRC screening among adults aged 45-49; stratified analyses were conducted among the insured and uninsured. Among screened individuals, associations with undergoing endoscopy versus another screening modality were studied. We characterized preventative care behaviors including seeking primary care, time since last checkup, and completion of other age-appropriate cancer screening. Results Of 50,132 individuals, 21,566 (42.6%) underwent CRC screening. Those with primary care physicians had higher odds of screening (odds ratio = 1.71; 95% confidence interval = 1.47-1.98, ref: no primary care physician), but increasing time since one's last visit was associated with decreasing odds of screening at all time intervals (5+ y ago: odds ratio = 0.29; 95% confidence interval = 0.23-0.38, ref: <1 y). Lower income, rural residence, no insurance, and lower educational attainment were associated with lower odds of screening. CRC screening was completed in only 41.3% of women who had mammograms and 48% who were screened for cervical cancer. Conclusions Uptake of CRC screening lags in adults aged 45-49, with differences in socioeconomic factors and preventative care utilization. A majority of eligible but unscreened individuals accessed other age-appropriate cancer screening tests, directing focus to patient- and provider-specific factors as potential targets for intervention.

title: Trends in Retraction of Vascular and Interventional Radiology Research.
abstract: Retractions play an important role in maintaining the integrity of vascular and interventional radiology (VIR) literature, yet their causes and trends remain uncharacterized. A search of PubMed, Embase, and the Retraction Watch Database in April 2026 identified 142 retracted VIR articles published since 2000. The leading reasons for retraction were peer-review manipulation (21.1%), intrinsic study errors (14.8%), and submission duplication (11.3%), although 40% of notices did not specify a reason. Most articles originated from China (69%) and addressed interventional oncology (35.2%). Retractions rose sharply in recent years, with 64.7% occurring between 2023 and 2026. The median time from publication to retraction was 14.8 months, and most articles were retracted within two years. Journal impact factor ranged widely (0.60-78.50) and was not associated with time to retraction. These findings highlight peer-review manipulation as a prominent mechanism of misconduct and reaffirm the importance of rigorous peer review and editorial screening.

title: Synchronous Percutaneous Biopsy and Cryoablation for Suspicious Solitary Pulmonary Nodules.
abstract: To evaluate the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and safety of synchronous CT-guided core needle biopsy and cryoablation for highly suspicious 1-2 cm pulmonary nodules MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 102 consecutive patients undergoing synchronous CT-guided core needle biopsy and cryoablation between August 2020 and October 2025. Treatment was undertaken on the basis of clinical and imaging suspicion before final histopathologic diagnosis. A cryoprobe was placed before biopsy to provide an intraprocedural landmark. Technical success, diagnostic yield, and adverse events were evaluated in all 102 patients; local tumor progression and overall survival were evaluated separately in 81 patients with pathology-confirmed NSCLC. Cryoablation technical success was 100% (102/102), and concurrent biopsy diagnostic yield was 87.3% (89/102). Biopsy identified 86 malignant diagnoses, including 81 NSCLCs. Mean nodule diameter was 1.52 ± 0.30 cm. Median follow-up in the NSCLC cohort was 34.5 months (IQR, 18.4-49.4 months). The cumulative incidence of recorded local tumor progression was 8.8% at both 1 and 3 years, and overall survival was 100% and 90.8%, respectively. Pneumothorax requiring chest tube drainage occurred in 20.6% (21/102), and no procedure-related deaths were reported. The synchronous biopsy and cryoablation approach was technically feasible and provided a specific histopathologic diagnosis in 87.3% of selected patients with highly suspicious 1.0-2.0-cm pulmonary nodules. Among patients with pathology-confirmed NSCLC, local-control outcomes were within the range reported in similar cryoablation-only series.

title: Pediatric Laryngeal Tumors: A Systematic Review of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms.
abstract: Background Pediatric laryngeal tumors are exceptionally rare and encompass a heterogeneous spectrum of benign and malignant neoplasms. Evidence remains largely limited to case reports and small case series. Objective To systematically characterize the histopathology, clinical presentation, treatment, recurrence, and outcomes of benign and malignant laryngeal tumors in children. Methods A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE, Embase, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from January 2000 to July 2026 involving patients aged ≤18 years with histologically confirmed primary laryngeal tumors. Results Eighty-six studies were included. Among 52 patients with benign tumors, granular cell tumor was the most frequent diagnosis, followed by neurofibroma and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor. Hoarseness was the predominant symptom, and surgery, particularly endoscopic resection, was the principal treatment. Recurrence occurred in 7/44 patients (15.9%) with available outcome data. Among 69 patients with malignant or intermediate tumors, squamous cell carcinoma predominated, followed by sarcomas and lymphomas. Treatment included surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy according to histology and disease extent. Total laryngectomy was performed in nine patients, and 12 deaths were reported. Conclusions Pediatric laryngeal tumors are rare, but should be considered in children with persistent or progressive hoarseness, dyspnea, dysphagia, or other unexplained upper airway symptoms. Granular cell tumor and neurofibroma were the predominant benign lesions, whereas squamous cell carcinoma was the most frequently reported malignant neoplasm. Given the rarity of these tumors and the current reliance on case-based evidence, the establishment of international multicenter registries is warranted to generate higher-quality data and inform standardized diagnostic and therapeutic algorithms for pediatric laryngeal neoplasms.

title: Fingerprinting the polycystic kidney: radiomics of the noncystic parenchyma for earlier ADPKD detection.
abstract: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease risk stratification relies on total kidney volume, a validated marker of cyst burden and progression. Kremer et al.'s pilot study used rapid breath-hold magnetic resonance fingerprinting with radiomics to evaluate noncystic renal parenchyma in children and young adults. Quantitative T1/T2 texture features distinguished autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease from controls independently of total kidney volume, cyst fraction, age, or body size, suggesting early tissue changes. Small, cross-sectional, unmatched data require longitudinal validation of reproducibility, prognostic value, and clinical utility.

title: Development and validation of a deep learning-based automated Notch Width Index measurement system from anteroposterior knee radiographs.
abstract: Background The Notch Width Index (NWI), a radiographic marker of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury risk, is poorly reproducible when measured manually. We developed a fully automated NWI system combining deep learning segmentation with geometric analysis. Methods A segmentation model (U-Net++/EfficientNet-B5) and a YOLOv8 laterality classifier were trained on 384 public images. Thirty-three anteroposterior knee radiographs were each measured twice by each of two surgeons. The fully automated method (D) was compared with both surgeons, and two semi-automated methods (B, C) with Surgeon 1 to isolate each processing stage, using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman analysis. The models were also applied without retraining to 500 external radiographs to assess feasibility and failure modes. Results Single-reading manual reliability was poor to moderate (ICC 0.475 and 0.562). The deterministic automated method agreed with both surgeons at ICC 0.525-0.756 (moderate to good); the semi-automated methods performed comparably (ICC 0.734 and 0.753). Segmentation reached a mean Dice coefficient of 0.975 ± 0.003, and processing was about 540 times faster than manual measurement. On the external dataset, segmentation degraded on osteoarthritic and low-quality images, so plausible values did not guarantee correct segmentation. Conclusion The method achieved moderate-to-good agreement with expert measurement while ensuring deterministic, examiner-independent reproducibility. Because it was never trained on surgeons' readings, this reflects reproduction of the geometric definition rather than overfitting. The principal barrier is segmentation under domain shift, not the algorithm; the method is best regarded as a reproducible standardization tool for routine anteroposterior views.

title: Comparative accuracy of large language models and orthopaedic clinicians in knee osteoarthritis and tibial plateau fracture classification systems.
abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) can process radiographic images, but their accuracy across orthopaedic classification systems requires further evaluation. This study compared the classification accuracy of four LLMs with that of orthopaedic surgeons and residents. This cross-sectional study included 100 cases obtained from Radiopaedia, with 20 cases each for the Kellgren-Lawrence, Ahlback, Schatzker, Hohl and Moore, and AO Foundation/Orthopaedic Trauma Association (AO/OTA) classifications. Each case comprised anteroposterior and lateral radiographs. Five orthopaedic surgeons, five residents, and four LLMs assessed the same cases, yielding 1400 classification assessments. Three independent senior orthopaedic surgeons established the consensus reference standard. AI evaluations were conducted in April 2026 using a standardized Turkish-language prompt, without classification definitions or examples. Only the first response was recorded. Analyses were descriptive because paired case-level classifications were unavailable. Overall accuracy was 91.2% (456/500) for orthopaedic surgeons, 70.2% (351/500) for residents, and 51.0% (204/400) for LLMs. LLM accuracy was 70.0% for Kellgren-Lawrence, 68.8% for Ahlback, 67.5% for AO/OTA, 28.8% for Hohl and Moore, and 20.0% for Schatzker. Model-specific accuracy was 58.0% for Claude Opus 4.1, 57.0% for GPT-5.5, 45.0% for Gemini 2.5 Pro, and 44.0% for DeepSeek-VL2. Orthopaedic surgeons achieved the highest observed accuracy across all five classification systems. LLM classification accuracy varied across systems and was lower overall than that of orthopaedic surgeons and residents. These findings are limited to the selected educational dataset and evaluation conditions. They do not establish educational or clinical utility; validation in larger, representative datasets is required.

title: Artificial intelligence-supported diabetic retinopathy screening in Tanzania: a randomised controlled trial.
abstract: Background Non-attendance after referral from screening is one of the major challenges for diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa. Artificial intelligence (AI) systems for the identification of diabetic retinopathy can provide point-of-screening results and therefore enable immediate counselling. We aimed to investigate whether AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy who attended the central ophthalmology referral clinic when compared with standard diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human grading and telephone counselling. Methods This two-arm, parallel-group, individually randomised controlled trial was conducted at non-communicable disease or diabetic clinics in 24 hospitals in the Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions of Tanzania. Eligible participants (aged ≥18 years) had diabetes and attended diabetic retinopathy screening. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling (the AI-intervention group) or standard-of-care diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human retinal image assessment and telephone counselling (the standard-of-care group). Participants had retinal photographs taken of both eyes. Images from the AI-intervention group were submitted to the AI software, and these participants were given their screening result (non-referable, referable, or ungradable) plus face-to-face counselling before leaving the photography room, with a referral to the central ophthalmology clinic if the AI output was referable or ungradable. Participants in the standard-of-care group received their screening result, along with appropriate counselling, by telephone a few weeks later. The primary outcome was attendance at the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks of screening among participants classified by masked UK-certified graders as having true referable diabetic retinopathy. This trial was registered with the ISRCTN Registry, ISRCTN18317152, and is complete. Findings Between March 8, 2023, and Aug 31, 2024, 2439 participants were assessed for eligibility and 2378 were enrolled, of whom 1192 were randomly assigned to the AI-intervention group and 1186 to the standard-of-care group. 904 participants had true referable diabetic retinopathy, comprising 437 in the AI-intervention group and 467 in the standard-of-care group. Of the participants in the AI-intervention group, 157 (35·9%) of 437 attended the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks, compared with 85 (18·2%) of 467 in the standard-of-care group, an absolute difference of 17·7 percentage points (95% CI 12·0-23·4; odds ratio 2·52 [95% CI 1·86-3·42]; p<0·0001). Interpretation AI-supported screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy that attended the central ophthalmology clinic after screening compared with the standard of care in Tanzania. Such AI-enabled screening pathways have the potential to improve diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa. title: Symptom-agnostic endpoints in tuberculosis vaccine efficacy trials.
abstract: Tuberculosis vaccine prevention-of-disease efficacy trials traditionally rely on symptom-triggered case detection. This approach captures only a subset of bacteriologically confirmed disease and can miss cases that occur between scheduled trial visits or outside trial procedures, slowing endpoint accrual and complicating interpretation of results. At the same time, the diagnostic landscape for tuberculosis is changing rapidly. Advances, including near point-of-care (NPOC) molecular assays using sputum and non-sputum specimens, portable chest radiography with computer-aided detection, and digital tools for decentralised monitoring, now make symptom-agnostic screening strategies increasingly feasible in large clinical trials. A 2026 WHO policy recommending the use of NPOC molecular diagnostics for tuberculosis further highlights the relevance of these approaches. In this Health Policy paper, we outlined a framework for integrating symptom-agnostic screening into tuberculosis vaccine efficacy trials and reviewed emerging diagnostic technologies that could enable this transition. Using parameters informed by the placebo arm of the M72/AS01 E phase 2b trial, we present a worked example illustrating a possible effect on endpoint detection and case-verification burden. In this illustrative scenario, an NPOC-based symptom-agnostic screening strategy was estimated to increase detection of bacteriologically confirmed tuberculosis endpoints by approximately 1·4-fold, as compared with that by symptom-based screening alone, although this finding should not be interpreted as a direct estimate of overall trial efficiency. Realising these benefits will require analytical validation of diagnostic tools, clinical qualification for trial use, and early alignment with regulators and policy bodies. If evaluated through staged evidence generation and implemented with stringent confirmation algorithms, then symptom-agnostic screening could support more interpretable assessments of vaccine impact across the bacteriological spectrum of tuberculosis disease while preserving endpoint specificity.

title: Multi-omics liquid biopsy for leptomeningeal metastases in lung cancer: from molecular mechanisms to precision diagnosis and treatment.
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM), a serious complication of advanced lung cancer, poses significant challenges in both clinical diagnosis and treatment monitoring, and is associated with a poor prognosis. Conventional diagnostic methods include magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology; however, their sensitivity is limited, particularly in the early stages of the disease. Against this backdrop, liquid biopsy has emerged as a minimally invasive and practical approach for molecular assessment and longitudinal monitoring of LM. Recent studies have reported that, in selected cohorts of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and LM, CSF-derived circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) detects driver and resistance-associated alterations more frequently than paired plasma, while epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM)-based CSF circulating tumor cell (CTC) assays have reported sensitivities of 76%-100% and specificities of 84%-100%, compared with a first-lumbar-puncture sensitivity of 44%-67% for conventional CSF cytology. These performance estimates should be interpreted in the context of selected cohorts and heterogeneous reference frameworks. Furthermore, cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumor cell (CSF-CTC) burden holds prognostic value, with higher CTC levels associated with poorer survival outcomes. This review summarizes recent advances in liquid biopsy biomarkers including ctDNA, DNA methylation, microRNA (miRNA), proteins, and circulating tumor cells (CTCs), focusing on their applications in the diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and prognostic assessment of lung cancer-associated LM, and provides a comparative discussion of liquid biopsy based on plasma and cerebrospinal fluid specimens. It further explores the potential, current challenges, and directions for clinical translation of multi-omics integration in the personalized management of LM.

It further explores the potential, current challenges, and directions for clinical translation of multi-omics integration in the personalized management of LM.

title: Serum extracellular vesicle-associated SNORD54 adds diagnostic information to CEA and CYFRA21-1 in non-small cell lung cancer: a case-control development study.
abstract: Background Blood-based biomarkers that complement established serum markers may improve molecular classification of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We evaluated whether SNORD54 and SNORD41 measured in a serum extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and cytokeratin 19 fragment 21-1 (CYFRA21-1). Methods This single-center case-control biomarker-development study included serum samples from patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC and contemporaneous healthy controls. Supporting expression evidence was assessed in paired lung adenocarcinoma and lung squamous cell carcinoma datasets and in 48 paired formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded NSCLC specimens. Serum analyses included gene-specific cohorts and a common complete-case cohort with SNORD54, SNORD41, CEA, and CYFRA21-1 measurements. Logistic regression models were compared using paired DeLong tests. Model parsimony, adjustment for age, sex, and smoking, locked Stage I-II and Stage I subgroup analyses, U6-normalization sensitivity analyses, and 2000-resample bootstrap internal validation were performed. Results The complete-case cohort comprised 98 patients with NSCLC and 79 healthy controls. Adding SNORD54 to CEA and CYFRA21-1 increased the AUC from 0.851(95% confidence interval [CI], 0.795-0.907) to 0.951 (95% CI, 0.920-0.982; ΔAUC, 0.100; 95% CI, 0.050-0.150; P < 0.001). At the development-derived cutoff, the three-marker model achieved 85.7% sensitivity and 94.9% specificity. SNORD41 did not improve the SNORD54-containing model (ΔAUC, 0.0003; P = 0.480; likelihood-ratio P = 0.953) and increased both Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. With coefficients and the cutoff fixed from the overall cohort, the three-marker model achieved AUCs of 0.904 (95% CI, 0.843-0.964) for Stage I-II disease and 0.882 (95% CI, 0.804-0.960) for Stage I disease. SNORD54 remained informative after adjustment for age, sex, and smoking. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.948. U6 Ct values differed between diagnostic groups; associations of both snoRNAs with case status persisted in sensitivity models accounting for U6 Ct. Conclusions SNORD54 measured in a serum EV-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond CEA and CYFRA21-1 in this NSCLC case-control cohort. The parsimonious SNORD54 + CEA + CYFRA21-1 model retained discrimination in locked early-stage subgroup analyses and showed limited apparent optimism after bootstrap correction. Independent validation in cohorts that include benign pulmonary nodules and other relevant lung diseases, together with standardized EV processing and validated RNA normalization, will define the clinical transportability of this three-marker panel.

title: Advanced neuroimaging in rare diseases: The paradigm of quantification in the era of personalized medicine.
abstract: Rare diseases frequently involve the central nervous system, posing significant diagnostic and monitoring challenges. Recent advances in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and neuroradiology have expanded the tools available for RD assessment, encompassing improvements in image acquisition, postprocessing techniques, and functional MRI sequences. Advanced postprocessing methods allow radiologists to derive additional quantitative information from conventional morphological images, including the segmentation and volumetric analysis of brain structures such as gray matter. Functional MRI techniques, such as Diffusion Weighted Imaging, Perfusion Weighted Imaging, or Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy, further contribute objective metrics reflecting underlying pathophysiological processes, including water diffusion and tissue perfusion. Within the framework of personalized medicine, integrating these advanced neuroimaging approaches may improve diagnostic precision and support treatment monitoring, follow-up, and disease surveillance. This review highlights the application of advanced neuroimaging tools across a range of clinical scenarios relevant to rare diseases, including cranial and structural abnormalities, white matter disorders, tumor assessment, and vascular conditions.

title: A clinical evaluation of spiral 4DCT and intelligent 4DCT sequence scanning.
abstract: Accurate 4DCT imaging is essential for radiotherapy planning but is often degraded by breathing irregularities. Phantom studies show that intelligent four-dimensional computed tomography (Direct i4D) sequence scanning can significantly reduce artifacts related to breathing irregularity compared to traditional spiral 4DCT. Direct i4D is a sequence-based acquisition mode in which beam-on time is adapted in real time to an individual patient's breathing pattern to optimize projection data coverage. In this study, we compared Direct i4D and spiral 4DCT scan image quality between Direct i4D and spiral 4DCT in a paired design, with both scans acquired for the same patient during a single simulation session. Spiral 4DCT and Direct i4D scans from 33 patients with pre-identified irregular breathing patterns were collected retrospectively. Breathing irregularities included variations in amplitude, frequency, or both. Spiral 4DCT scans were used for motion evaluation, while the Direct i4D scans were acquired for treatment planning. To compare the internal target volume (ITV) on both 4DCT datasets, a radiation oncologist manually contoured all ITVs de novo. Residual sorting artifacts were visually evaluated and scored by a radiation oncologist and medical physicist on a scale of 1 to 5 (where higher scores indicate lower presence of artifacts and better image quality). Visual evaluation of 4DCT phases showed that 36% of spiral 4DCT and 3% of Direct i4D scans would require resimulation. Meanwhile, 18% and of spiral 4DCT and 27% of Direct i4D scans were artifact-free (p-value < 0.1). The ITV comparison between the 2 4DCT techniques revealed mean and standard deviation (STD) Dice similarity coefficients of 0.59 and 0.18, respectively. ITV mean CT value difference varies between 0.80 HU and 158.41 HU (Mean ± STD: 39.41HU ± 40.02 HU). Real-time adaptation of the scan time and rebinning by Direct i4D enhanced the image quality for individual 4DCT phases. Irregular breathing patterns can degrade spiral 4DCT image quality and tumor delineation. The novel Direct i4D technique provides a reliable solution to reduce such artifacts significantly.

title: Mind the Gap: A survey of chronic wound datasets, methods, and clinical translation.
abstract: Chronic wounds, including diabetic foot ulcers, venous ulcers, arterial ulcers and pressure ulcers, represent a growing global health challenge with significant morbidity, mortality, and economic burden. Advancements in medical image analysis have shown promise in automating wound detection, segmentation, and measurement. However, translation of these research advances into clinical practice through mobile applications remains limited. This survey presents systematic analysis of the relationship between chronic wound datasets, deep learning methods, and mobile wound assessment applications. We analyse 20 datasets (14 public/partially public and 6 private), including iterative challenge datasets that extend image pool through synthetic augmentation. We review 50 deep learning methods spanning encoder-decoder architectures to self-supervised learning approaches, and evaluate 13 mobile applications (commercially deployed clinical tools and research prototypes). We examine the alignment between publicly available chronic wound datasets and the documented capabilities of mobile wound assessment mobile applications. Our analysis reveals critical misalignments between datasets, algorithms and mobile applications. Existing datasets are typically designed for algorithm benchmarking rather than clinical deployment, and therefore lack standardised acquisition protocols, scale calibration markers, depth information, detailed tissue composition annotations, and representation of diverse skin types. Conversely, reviewed mobile applications report capabilities, including automatic tissue classification, calibrated wound measurement and depth estimation, for which publicly available data is insufficient. We map documented dataset characteristics to capabilities reported among reviewed mobile applications, identify unresolved methodological challenges, and outline key priorities for the field. Based on these insights, we propose actionable recommendations for developing clinically translatable computer vision system for wound assessment. This survey is intended to serve as a reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to bridge the gap between medical imaging methodologies and practical demands of clinical wound care.

title: A self-navigated framework for motion detection and spoke-reordering musculoskeletal dynamic reconstruction in 3D radial MRI.
abstract: Motion remains a major challenge and active research focus in MRI, as both involuntary (e.g., head movement) and voluntary (e.g., joint motion) motion can degrade image quality or, alternatively, provide opportunities for dynamic assessment. Existing motion sensing approaches - such as external tracking or navigator sequences - often require additional hardware, increase SAR, or necessitate sequence modifications, thereby limiting clinical flexibility. In this work, we propose a self-navigated motion sensing framework for 3D radial MRI. Motion surrogates are first extracted directly from multi-coil k-space data. A sliding-window summation is then applied to enhance robustness, followed by a second principal component (PC2)-based strategy to derive a 1D motion-sensitive signal that reflects subject position over time. Beyond conventional head motion correction, we demonstrate the utility of the proposed framework in improving dynamic 4D MRI of the ankle and knee under both stepwise and continuous motion protocols. By reordering spokes based on motion-derived position rather than acquisition time, the method enables motion-resolved reconstructions with improved anatomical clarity. Overall, this approach facilitates efficient motion detection and supports broader adoption of motion-aware dynamic MRI. The source code of this framework is available at https://github.com/EricLin1993/SpEMSK.

title: A unified and domain-robust framework enables controllable multimodal brain MRI synthesis.
abstract: Multimodal magnetic resonance image (MRI) synthesis can shorten examinations, reduce cost, and furnish contrasts that are difficult or impossible to acquire, but current models remain hard to control and brittle to shifts in scanner, protocol, and pathology. We present a unified, domain-robust synthesis framework that modulates spatial carriers with physically informed, domain-stable statistical guidance. A balanced soft-plus-hard conditioning scheme enables a single model to perform diverse contrast mapping, while allowing smooth user adjustment of contrast weighting. Evaluated on 991 test subjects from five public and three private datasets spanning cross-dataset, cross-protocol, and related cross-pathology scenarios, our approach matches or outperforms advanced baselines for both in-domain synthesis and inference under unseen domains without finetuning. Clinician Turing test and downstream glioma grading experiments further indicate realistic appearance, preservation of pathology-relevant information, and potential practical value under clinically heterogeneous conditions. By jointly delivering controllability, robustness to real-world variability, and physically informed, domain-stable guidance within one architecture, this work advances MRI synthesis toward deployment in heterogeneous clinical environments.

Evaluated on 991 test subjects from five public and three private datasets spanning cross-dataset, cross-protocol, and related cross-pathology scenarios, our approach matches or outperforms advanced baselines for both in-domain synthesis and inference under unseen domains without finetuning. Clinician Turing test and downstream glioma grading experiments further indicate realistic appearance, preservation of pathology-relevant information, and potential practical value under clinically heterogeneous conditions. By jointly delivering controllability, robustness to real-world variability, and physically informed, domain-stable guidance within one architecture, this work advances MRI synthesis toward deployment in heterogeneous clinical environments.

title: Performance uncertainty in medical image analysis: A large-scale investigation of confidence intervals.
abstract: Performance uncertainty quantification is essential for reliable validation and eventual clinical translation of medical imaging artificial intelligence (AI). Confidence intervals (CIs) play a central role in this process by indicating how precise a reported performance estimate is. Yet, due to the limited amount of work examining CI behavior in medical imaging, the community remains largely unaware of how many diverse CI methods exist and how they behave in specific settings. The purpose of this study is to close this gap. To this end, we conducted a large-scale empirical analysis across a total of 24 segmentation and classification tasks, using 19 trained models per task group, a broad spectrum of commonly used performance metrics, multiple aggregation strategies, and several widely adopted CI methods. Reliability (coverage) and precision (width) of each CI method were estimated across all settings to characterize their dependence on study characteristics. Our analysis revealed five principal findings: (1) the sample size required for reliable CIs varies from a few dozens to several thousands of cases depending on study parameters; (2) CI behavior is strongly affected by the choice of performance metric; (3) aggregation strategy substantially influences the reliability of CIs, e.g. they require more observations for macro than for micro; (4) the machine learning problem (segmentation versus classification) modulates these effects; (5) different CI methods are not equally reliable and precise depending on the use case. Finally, we derived practical implications of this study in the form of a decision tree which shall prove useful to the community. This paves the way for future consensus guidelines on reporting performance uncertainty.

title: Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation.
abstract: Foundation models (FM) have transformed computational pathology but remain computationally prohibitive for clinical deployment due to their massive parameter counts and high-magnification processing requirements. Here, we introduce XMAG, a lightweight FM developed through cross-magnification distillation that transfers knowledge from a state-of-the-art 20x magnification teacher to an efficient 5x magnification student architecture. XMAG employs a compact backbone and operates entirely at 5x, requiring 11.3 times fewer patches per whole slide image (WSI) compared to existing approaches. Our novel distillation framework incorporates dual-level knowledge transfer, aligning both global image representations and local spatial features across magnification levels through carefully designed projection heads and spatial token mapping. We trained XMAG on 3.49 million images curated from publicly available datasets and evaluated performance across seven clinically relevant histopathology analysis tasks spanning multiple cancer types. Across four WSI-level classification tasks, XMAG achieved an average AUC within 1% of substantially larger foundation models while delivering up to 29.5-fold faster encoder-level processing, corresponding to an encoder throughput of 8.8 WSIs per minute in a controlled patch-encoding benchmark. We also found that performance differences remained task-dependent, with larger gaps observed for fine-grained tasks such as ISUP grading and patch-level phenotyping. We further explore end-to-end XMAG training as a direction for task-specific adaptation of the compact model. These results suggest that cross-magnification distillation is a promising strategy for developing efficient low-magnification pathology foundation models and may support more scalable WSI analysis in computationally constrained research and translational settings.

title: ROI-SSIM guided framework for 3D knee MRI reconstruction under artifact degradation.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction is highly sensitive to undersampling and acquisition artifacts. Although deep learning-based approaches have significantly improved reconstruction quality, they are typically optimized using global fidelity metrics that may not fully reflect reconstruction quality within clinically important structures such as the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), meniscus, and articular cartilage. This study proposes a region-aware MRI reconstruction framework based on a Vision Transformer autoencoder (ViT-AE) guided by an ROI Structural Similarity (ROI-SSIM) loss. The method leverages fastMRI+ bounding-box annotations and incorporates a hybrid artifact simulation framework spanning k-space and image-domain degradations. Experiments on the fastMRI knee single-coil validation set (PD contrast, R=4) show that the proposed ViT-AE achieves reconstruction fidelity competitive with established baselines (SSIM 0.823, Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) 32.4dB , Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE) 0.0147), while ROI-SSIM supervision improves structural fidelity within clinically relevant annotated regions. Under mixed artifact conditions, region-specific structural similarity decreased by only 2.9% , compared with a 6.8% decrease in global SSIM. These findings support the use of region-aware supervision for artifact-robust MRI reconstruction. Overall, the method presented in this paper:Introduces ROI-SSIM supervision for region-aware MRI reconstruction.Develops a hybrid artifact simulation framework spanning k-space and image-domain degradations.Demonstrates improved anatomical preservation under artifact conditions.

title: Ex vivo fluorescence confocal microscopy for real-time margin assessment of nonmelanoma skin cancer in Mohs surgery: A prospective interventional study.
abstract: New-generation ex vivo fluorescence confocal microscopy (EVFCM) generates hematoxylin-eosin-like images directly comparable to conventional histopathology. Its interobserver performance with a novel acquisition mode in non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC) micrographically controlled surgery remains to be defined. In this prospective interventional study, 42 tumors from 39 patients undergoing Mohs surgery between January and October 2025 were examined with EVFCM. Specimens were orthogonally sectioned, stained, and acquired in digital-stain mode. Peripheral and deep margins were independently and blindly reviewed by a dermatologist and a pathologist, both trained in EVFCM interpretation. Concordant negative margins were considered tumor-free, whereas positive, discordant, or equivocal findings prompted re-excision and re-evaluation. Diagnostic agreement with histopathology was assessed using Cohen's κ statistic. A total of 261 margins were evaluated. Inter-reader agreement between the dermatologist and pathologist was almost perfect for both margin assessment (κ=0.863; SE 0.067; p<0.001; observed agreement 98.6%) and histotype assessment (κ=0.882; SE 0.031; p<0.001; observed agreement 97.6%). Compared with histopathology, EVFCM showed high performance, with an overall diagnostic accuracy of 96.4%. The AUC for the combined assessment was 0.875 (SE 0.074; 95% CI 0.730-1.000). Only two discrepancies were observed between EVFCM and histopathology: one false-negative margin assessment and one discordance attributable to differences in sample processing. These findings support EVFCM as a reliable tool for intraoperative margin assessment in NMSC. Comparable performance between dermatologist and pathologist readers supports its potential integration into Mohs surgery workflows; however, potential workflow advantages of the standardized sample-processing approach require prospective validation using quantitative time metrics.

title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
abstract: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. Existing global deep learning super-resolution (SR) methods often incur computational overhead by ignoring regional image content. This motivates an adaptive local SR strategy to optimize efficiency and detail preservation. To address this, we developed a local SR method that adaptively allocates computational resources to information-rich regions. The proposed framework regularized an entropy-based local region processing strategy with a diffusion model fortified by frequency-domain and structural constraints. We retrospectively evaluated our method on two diverse datasets: a proprietary 7.0 T dental MRI dataset (25 T2-weighted DESS sequences from 10 beagle dogs) and a public 5.0 T brain MRI dataset (Diff5T, 50 diffusion-weighted sequences). Image quality was quantified using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID. On the 5.0 T brain test dataset (10 subjects), the method achieved a PSNR of 27.15 ± 0.10 dB, an LPIPS of 0.14 ± 0.00 and an FID of 54.01, with lower perceptual metrics than the evaluated baselines. Ablation studies indicated that the proposed frequency-domain and structural constraints reduced LPIPS and FID, with trade-offs in PSNR and SSIM. In conclusion, the evaluated framework showed improvements in perceptual metrics by integrating targeted local processing with frequency-domain and structural regularization, accompanied by a trade-off in pixel-wise fidelity metrics, supporting the technical feasibility of addressing the resolution-time trade-off in high-field MRI. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and evaluating the framework in human dental cohorts to address anatomical differences between the current canine model and human dental anatomy.

title: Multicenter external validation of a multimodal MRI deep-learning model to predict meningioma bone invasion.
abstract: Background Preoperative detection of meningioma bone invasion lacks objective biomarkers and relies on subjective radiological assessment, posing a risk of excessive bone resection or residual tumor. We therefore developed and externally validated a parsimonious six-feature DenseNet121 signature derived from multiparametric MRI across two independent institutions. Methods In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 438 consecutive patients (mean age, 53 ± 11 years; 77% women) with histologically confirmed meningioma were allocated to training (n = 182), internal validation (n = 77), and external test (n = 179) sets. Following N4 bias-field correction and isotropic resampling, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted volumes were fed into a DenseNet121 architecture to extract a six-feature signature via nested cross-validation. Discrimination (area under the ROC curve, AUC), calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision-curve analysis) were evaluated. Results In the external cohort (prevalence 11%), the signature achieved an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.73-0.91), sensitivity 75%, specificity 77% and negative predictive value 96%, with an AUC improvement of 0.155 over conventional radiomics (95% CI, 0.01-0.30; p = 0.035). At a 20% risk threshold, decision-curve analysis confirmed a positive net clinical benefit, primarily driven by the high negative predictive value. SHAP analysis demonstrated the dominant and consistent contribution of low-ADC features. Conclusion The DenseNet121-derived six-feature signature serves as a reliable rule-out aid for preoperative meningioma bone invasion, with a high negative predictive value that may safely support decisions to avoid extensive bone resection in predicted-negative cases. Positive predictions require confirmatory CT or intraoperative biopsy to mitigate false positives. This tool could assist nurses and surgeons in preoperative planning, facilitating personalized patient care and potentially reducing operative time and complications.

title: A hierarchical residual Swin transformer with dual-level locality compensation for accelerated MRI reconstruction.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides high spatial resolution, excellent soft-tissue contrast, and reliable anatomical discrimination, and is therefore widely used in clinical diagnosis. However, long acquisition time still limits imaging efficiency and clinical throughput. Although convolutional neural network (CNN)-based deep learning approaches have shown considerable promise for reconstructing images from undersampled k-space data, existing methods frequently fail to preserve fine structural details and texture continuity under aggressive undersampling conditions. In this study, we propose a novel reconstruction network based on the Swin Transformer, which integrates three key components: (i) long residual connections to facilitate the recovery of high-frequency details; (ii) a dual-level locality compensation mechanism to restore local spatial information; and (iii) a channel recalibration module to explicitly capture global dependencies among channels, thereby enhancing global feature extraction. Extensive experiments conducted on the IXI and MICCAI 2013 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms several compared generative adversarial network (GAN)-based approaches for MRI reconstruction across all undersampling mask types, achieving a PSNR improvement of approximately 0.6-1 dB over the best competing method under various settings. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/cvgjhuor/HR-SwinGAN.

title: A deep learning radiomics model based on multiparametric MRI for predicting the efficacy of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in axillary lymph nodes of breast cancer.
abstract: Objectives In this study, we developed and validated a deep learning radiomics clinical (DLRC) model integrating multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and clinical data to predict axillary pathological complete response (apCR) in cN+ breast cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). Materials and methods We retrospectively collected data from 221 eligible breast cancer patients. The DLRC model integrated radiomics features and deep learning scores (DL-Scores) derived from mpMRI, together with clinical risk factors, to predict apCR. Seven classifiers were employed for model construction, and the optimal classifier was selected based on classification performance to build the final model. Model performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, area under the curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Classification performance was assessed via the confusion matrix. Additionally, SHAP plots were utilized for interpretability analysis of the model. Results Multivariate analysis confirmed that progesterone receptor (PR), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), clinical T stage (OR = 0.258), and time-intensity curve (TIC) were significantly associated with apCR. The mpMRI based DLRC model achieved AUCs of 0.949 (95% CI, 0.912-0.986) and 0.932 (95% CI, 0.867-0.998) in the training and validation sets. SHAP analysis further revealed the interpretability of the model. The confusion matrix visually demonstrated the consistency between the predicted results and the true labels, validating the classification performance of the model. Conclusion The DLRC model effectively predicts apCR in breast cancer patients after NAC. It can serve as an auxiliary tool for clinicians in identifying potential candidates for axillary de-escalation, offering support for personalized precision treatment. We present this article in accordance with the TRIPOD-AI reporting checklist.

title: The utility of magnetic resonance imaging of the spinal cord in paediatric transverse myelitis: A systematic review.
abstract: Background Spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to the diagnosis of paediatric acute transverse myelitis (ATM), yet its true diagnostic yield, concordance with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) inflammation, and prognostic value remain unclear. Objective To quantify the diagnostic yield of spinal cord MRI in paediatric ATM, evaluate agreement with CSF inflammatory markers, and explore associations between MRI features and clinical outcomes. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and prospectively registered (CRD42024504846). MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO and CENTRAL were searched from 2006 to October 2025. Observational studies including ≥5 children (≤18 years) with monophasic ATM who underwent spinal cord MRI were eligible. The primary outcome was the proportion of clinically diagnosed ATM cases demonstrating inflammatory spinal cord lesions on MRI. Secondary outcomes included MRI-CSF concordance and associations between imaging findings and long-term outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Results Twelve studies comprising 330 children were included. The pooled diagnostic yield of spinal cord MRI was 97.6% (95% CI 92.2 to 100.0%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=71.8%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 71.2 to 99.6%, indicating that a future paediatric cohort could plausibly report a yield anywhere within that range. Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis and gadolinium enhancement were the most frequently reported features. Paired MRI-CSF data were available for 61 patients; discordance was observed in 36%, most commonly MRI-positive with normal CSF. Follow-up data (n = 237) showed 64% achieved good recovery, whereas 30% had severe residual deficits; persistent bladder dysfunction occurred in 31%. Baseline MRI positivity did not reliably predict outcome. Conclusions Spinal cord MRI demonstrates a high diagnostic yield in imaged children with clinically diagnosed ATM, but imaging was a condition of cohort entry in most included studies and the pooled estimate is strongly influenced by study design. MRI should be interpreted alongside CSF findings, and baseline imaging alone does not reliably stratify prognosis. Standardised prospective studies are required to refine the diagnostic and prognostic role of MRI in paediatric inflammatory myelopathies.

title: Histomorphometric analysis of invasive fungal infections.
abstract: Background Invasive fungal infections represent a growing global health challenge, making rapid and accurate diagnosis essential for timely initiation of appropriate therapy. Histopathology remains central to distinguishing true infection from colonization or contamination, and morphometric analysis may facilitate fungal identification. Furthermore, advances in digital pathology, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning have increased interest in morphometric approaches for fungal differentiation. However, their application requires the identification of morphometric parameters that reliably discriminate between fungal genera. Method In the present study 8772 measurements across nine morphometric parameters in 76 human and veterinary histological cases of invasive fungal infections caused by Candida, Aspergillus, and Mucorales were performed. Aim The aims were to comprehensively characterize fungal morphology, evaluate the diagnostic utility of different morphometric parameters, and develop a simple decision tree for fungal differentiation. Results Overall, the measurements made in this study demonstrated good interobserver agreement. Only minor morphometric variation was observed throughout the tissue blocks, indicating that assessment of a single histological section can be sufficient for morphometric analysis. In addition, discriminatory morphometric parameters were identified, enabling the development of a diagnostic decision tree that differentiated Mucorales from Aspergillus and Candida in 95% of the cases. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that quantitative morphometry provides reliable and clinically relevant information for fungal identification in histological sections. The identified morphometric parameters may form the basis for future image analysis and machine learning approaches, enabling faster and more accurate diagnosis of invasive fungal infections.

title: Maternal edible THC consumption alters offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in rhesus macaques.
abstract: Background Prenatal cannabis exposure is associated with adverse offspring outcomes including altered neurodevelopment. However, there is insufficient evidence to establish a direct association. We sought to determine the impact of chronic prenatal delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) exposure on offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in a translational rhesus macaque model. Methods Animals were divided into two groups, control and THC-exposed, with both groups receiving a daily edible (placebo or THC) pre-conception, throughout pregnancy, and postnatally. MRI was performed longitudinally across gestation and infancy to assess volumetric and microstructural brain development. Serial behavioral testing, including motor and emotional assessments, was performed postnatally. At 6 months of age, brain tissue was collected for histology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), whole genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS), and bulk RNA-sequencing. Findings Analysis of the MRI images showed white matter changes with higher fractional anisotropy in the corpus callosum (CC) and centrum semiovale in THC-exposed infants. However, there were no significant differences in regional brain volumes. Behavioral testing demonstrated that THC-exposed infants displayed increased vocalizations and decreased independence. originalAbstract:
Background

Prenatal cannabis exposure is associated with adverse offspring outcomes including altered neurodevelopment. However, there is insufficient evidence to establish a direct association. We sought to determine the impact of chronic prenatal delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) exposure on offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in a translational rhesus macaque model.

Methods

Animals were divided into two groups, control and THC-exposed, with both groups receiving a daily edible (placebo or THC) pre-conception, throughout pregnancy, and postnatally. MRI was performed longitudinally across gestation and infancy to assess volumetric and microstructural brain development. Serial behavioral testing, including motor and emotional assessments, was performed postnatally. At 6 months of age, brain tissue was collected for histology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), whole genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS), and bulk RNA-sequencing.

Findings

Analysis of the MRI images showed white matter changes with higher fractional anisotropy in the corpus callosum (CC) and centrum semiovale in THC-exposed infants. However, there were no significant differences in regional brain volumes. Behavioral testing demonstrated that THC-exposed infants displayed increased vocalizations and decreased independence. WGBS identified differentially methylated regions (DMRs) associated with THC exposure in the cerebellum and prefrontal cortex, annotated to genes involved in synaptic organization and brain development. RNA-sequencing confirmed differential expression of genes related to axon development and glutamatergic synapse, with expression correlating with methylation levels.

Interpretation

Chronic prenatal edible THC exposure in the rhesus macaque was associated with changes in white matter development, effects on infant behavior with signs of increased stress and anxiety, and brain DNA methylation and expression of genes involved in neurodevelopment.

title: Resting-state fMRI biomarkers of surgical outcome in temporal lobe epilepsy: Network reorganization, rsfMRI-based prediction models, and cognition - A systematic review.
abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) may provide information on brain network alterations relevant to seizure outcome and cognitive risk after epilepsy surgery. We reviewed rsfMRI studies in TLE surgical cohorts to evaluate postoperative network changes, preoperative predictors of seizure outcome, and associations between functional connectivity and cognition. This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. Fifteen studies were included, comprising 474 TLE patients who underwent resective epilepsy surgery and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Studies were reviewed for patient population, surgery, rsfMRI methodology, networks or regions, outcome definition, postoperative network changes, and cognitive assessments. Despite heterogeneity in patient selection, surgery, rsfMRI analysis, and outcome definition, studies consistently reported reduced DMN-related connectivity in TLE compared with healthy controls. Postoperative functional connectivity in seizure-free patients shifted toward healthy controls patterns in few studies. Preoperative rsfMRI-based prediction models showed promising accuracy for predicting seizure outcome but were generally developed in small cohorts and lacked external validation. Evidence relating rsfMRI to cognition was limited, but implicated thalamic, ascending reticular activating system, and thalamo-occipital connectivity in attention, language, and executive functions. RsfMRI is a promising research biomarker for network-level risk stratification in TLE surgery, particularly for seizure outcome prediction and postoperative network reorganization. Current evidence remains insufficient for clinical implementation. Future studies require larger homogeneous multicenter cohorts, standardized acquisition and preprocessing, consistent outcome definitions, systematic postoperative rsfMRI, neuropsychological assessment, and external validation of prediction models.
