title: Latent knowledge-driven unified representation learning for brain tumor segmentation with missing modalities.
abstract: Gliomas are the most common primary malignant brain tumors, characterized by high heterogeneity, diffuse infiltration, and poor prognosis. Accurate tumor segmentation plays a fundamental role in diagnosis, treatment planning, and quantitative analysis. Although multimodal MRI provides rich anatomical and functional information, missing imaging modalities are frequently encountered in real-world clinical practice. Here, we propose a Latent Knowledge-driven Unified Representation Learning (LK-URL) framework for robust glioma segmentation under missing-modality conditions. LK-URL incorporates a Dynamic Adaptive Unified Interaction Module (DAUIM) to model intra- and inter-modality interactions, enabling enhanced tumor-aware feature representation and cross-modal compensation. Furthermore, a Latent Knowledge Collaborative Learning (LKCL) strategy is introduced to transfer structural knowledge from complete to incomplete modality settings via internal full-modality supervision, thereby improving the consistency of feature representations across diverse modality combinations and enhancing segmentation robustness. Extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches under missing-modality scenarios, while exhibiting strong generalization ability in real-world clinical settings. The code is available at https://github.com/joey-AI-medical-learning/LK-URL.

title: TMRKP: Trustworthy MRI-based radiology knowledge-aware prediction framework for stroke-associated pneumonia and hemorrhagic transformation.
abstract: Prediction of stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) and hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is critical for improving the prognosis of acute ischemic stroke patients. However, current brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based models narrowly focus on generic visual patterns, and frequently overlook the radiology-informed knowledge critical for predicting SAP and HT. To address this limitation, we propose a trustworthy MRI-based radiology knowledge-aware prediction (TMRKP) framework equipped with radiology knowledge-aware masked modeling (RKMM) and evidential multi-sequence fusion (EMF). Specifically, TMRKP first organizes four MRI sequences into a 2 × 2 super-sequence configuration, mimicking the diagnostic perspective of radiologists who simultaneously analyze multiple imaging modalities. Second, to introduce radiology knowledge into representation learning, we focus on white matter hyperintensities (WMH), a well-established biomarker of chronic small-vessel disease and long-term ischemic injury that is clinically relevant to SAP and HT. During pre-training, RKMM segments WMH masks from the MRI sequence to steer the model toward WMH regions, enabling it to learn meaningful representations of these clinically relevant pathological areas. Third, for SAP and HT prediction, EMF models the predictive uncertainty using evidence derived from both the super-sequence and the WMH-aware masked super-sequence, and fuses the resulting multi-sequence evidence based on Dempster-Shafer theory (DST). Extensive experiments on the collected Jiangdu dataset, together with independent external validation on the Zhongda dataset, demonstrate the superiority and generalizability of TMRKP over the state-of-the-art models.

title: Brain volume analysis-guided basic research in psychiatry.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) volumetric analysis is among the few tools able to probe the living human brain, offering a route from clinical findings back to basic neuroscience. Here we propose a reverse-translational framework for psychiatric research that links human MRI findings to their underlying molecular mechanisms in model animals. The framework rests on three "liaisons": a species liaison, confirming that a volume change identified in humans is also observed in mice using the same imaging and analytical method; a scale liaison, in which a histological pipeline explains the macroscopic volume change in terms of cell number and cell volume; and a causal liaison, in which molecular or cell-biological intervention converts correlative histological findings into causal evidence by inducing or reversing the volume change. We further propose that unbiased, whole-brain MRI volumetric analysis in mice can serve as an exploratory region-screening method, identifying disease- or treatment-related regions without a predefined region of interest, and capturing the maintained structural outcome of an intervention rather than its immediate functional trace. Together, the three-liaison framework and the region-screening approach outline a general strategy by which MRI-guided reverse and forward translation can uncover the structural and molecular basis of psychiatric diseases and their treatments.

title: Characterizing age-dependent diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility properties in 5xFAD Alzheimer's mouse brain using high-resolution MRI.
abstract: Background and purpose Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating and progressive neurodegenerative disorder and the most common cause of dementia. This study aimed to characterize magnetic susceptibility changes associated with beta-amyloid (Aβ) plaques during AD progression using diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measurements in the 5xFAD mouse model. Methods Ex vivo multi-echo gradient-echo imaging (MGRE) with a spatial resolution of 40 × 40 × 40 μm 3 was performed in three age groups of 5xFAD mice (4, 12, and 18 months) using a 9.4T Bruker MRI scanner. Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) was reconstructed, and DECOMPOSE-QSM was applied to derive diamagnetic component susceptibility (DCS) and paramagnetic component susceptibility (PCS). Aβ plaques were automatically detected based on DCS and quantified to assess age-dependent plaque accumulation, changes in plaque burden, and associated susceptibility alterations. Cortical regions were further segmented into plaque-detected and plaque-undetected regions to assess regional susceptibility variations among the three age groups. In addition, Aβ/ferritin immunostaining was performed on the imaged murine brains. Results The results demonstrated progressive, spatially heterogeneous, age-dependent accumulation of amyloid plaques, as evidenced by significant increases in plaque burden. In plaque-detected and whole-region cortical areas, DCS consistently shifted toward more negative values (greater diamagnetic susceptibility) with disease progression, while PCS became more positive (greater paramagnetic susceptibility). The concurrent increase in plaque burden, together with progressively more negative DCS and more positive PCS within plaques, are consistent with increasing diamagnetic and paramagnetic tissue contributions associated with amyloid and iron-related pathology, respectively. Histological analysis showed colocalized Aβ aggregation and ferritin deposition within plaques, both of which increased with age. Conclusions The decomposed susceptibility components, DCS and PCS, provide complementary biophysical information beyond conventional QSM, enabling improved characterization of plaque-associated susceptibility changes during AD progression. High-resolution MRI facilitates the visualization and detection of individual plaques, allowing detailed analysis of their susceptibility properties. These findings highlight the importance of high-resolution MRI and the potential of diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measures as sensitive imaging biomarkers for monitoring neurodegenerative pathology.

title: The Visual Cortex and Beyond: Investigating Long-Term Cortical Plasticity Following Monocular Deprivation.
abstract: Aim To characterise short- and long-term plastic changes in cortical and subcortical structures induced by ultra-long (five-day) monocular deprivation (MD), and to assess the extent and regional specificity of structural changes and their reversibility following the restoration of binocular vision. Methods In this single-arm longitudinal study, 21 healthy adults underwent five structural MRI sessions: at baseline, during MD on days 1, 3 and 5, and after a seven-day recovery period (day 12). MD was induced by occluding the right eye with a translucent eye patch for five consecutive days. Grey matter volume (GMV) changes were analysed using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain effects and generalised estimating equations (GEE) to model temporal trajectories in predefined cortical and subcortical regions. Results Ultra-long MD induced dynamic GMV changes in primary and higher visual cortices, with exploratory changes also in subcortical and cerebellar structures. VBM showed cumulative volume increases in bilateral occipital cortex, including calcarine, lateral occipital and fusiform regions, and adjacent cerebellar lobules, peaking between days 3 and 5. Region-wise modelling resolved the temporal build-up of these changes across visual, subcortical and sensorimotor regions; after correction for multiple comparisons, a time-dependent effect remained in occipital and ventral occipito-temporal cortex (occipital pole, fusiform and calcarine cortex), converging with the voxel-wise result. Following binocular restoration, an exploratory GMV decrease was observed selectively in the left middle occipital gyrus, while an exploratory increase was observed in the left hippocampus, compatible with persistent plasticity in associative memory networks. Conclusion Prolonged sensory imbalance via ultra-long MD induces rapid, region-specific and possibly persistent GMV plasticity in the adult brain. These changes follow temporally stratified trajectories across visual, subcortical and integrative systems, consistent with models of homeostatic and hierarchical plasticity. Corrected evidence supports cumulative occipital plasticity during deprivation; whether the exploratory extra-visual and post-recovery changes reflect persistent adaptation requires confirmation. MD-based paradigms thus offer a controlled window on structural plasticity in both healthy individuals and clinical populations.

title: Achieving detailed medial temporal lobe segmentation with upsampled isotropic training from implicit neural representation.
abstract: Imaging biomarkers in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are important tools for diagnosing, tracking and treating Alzheimer's disease (AD). Neurofibrillary tau pathology in AD is closely linked to neurodegeneration and generally follows a pattern of spread in the brain, with early stages involving subregions of the medial temporal lobe (MTL). Accurate segmentation of MTL subregions is needed to extract granular biomarkers of AD progression. MTL subregions are often imaged using T2-weighted (T2w) MRI scans that are highly anisotropic due to constraints of MRI physics and image acquisition, making it difficult to reliably model MTL subregions geometrically and extract morphological measures, such as thickness. In this study, we propose a segmentation framework for MTL subregions in isotropic space, in which an implicit neural representation is used to construct the isotropic training atlas from the anisotropic low-resolution T2w data, with T1w MRI as an auxiliary modality to support the INR and segmentation. In an independent test set, the morphological measures extracted using this isotropic model showed stronger effect sizes than those from models trained on anisotropic data in distinguishing participants with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from cognitively unimpaired individuals. In the test-retest analysis, the morphological measures extracted using the isotropic model showed greater stability than those from the anisotropic segmentation. This study demonstrates improved reliability of MRI-derived MTL subregion biomarkers without additional atlas annotation effort, which may more accurately quantify and track the relationship between AD pathology and brain atrophy for monitoring disease progression.

title: Atlas-assisted segment anything model for fetal brain MRI (FeTal-SAM).
abstract: This paper presents FeTal-SAM, a novel adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) tailored for fetal brain MRI segmentation. Traditional deep learning methods often require large annotated datasets for a fixed set of labels, making them inflexible when clinical or research needs change. By integrating atlas-based prompts and foundation-model principles, FeTal-SAM addresses two key limitations in fetal brain MRI segmentation: (1) the need to retrain models for varying label definitions, and (2) the lack of insight into whether segmentations are driven by genuine image contrast or merely inferred by learned spatial priors. We leverage multi-atlas registration to generate spatially aligned label templates that serve as dense prompts, alongside a bounding-box prompt, for SAM's segmentation decoder. This strategy enables binary segmentation on a per-structure basis, which is subsequently fused to reconstruct the full 3D segmentation volumes. Evaluations on two datasets, the dHCP dataset and an in-house dataset demonstrate FeTal-SAM's robust performance across gestational ages. Notably, it achieves Dice scores comparable to state-of-the-art baselines which were trained for each dataset and label definition for well-contrasted structures like cortical plate and cerebellum, while maintaining the flexibility to segment anatomical structures that could be templated by compatible atlas image and label sample pairs. Although slightly lower accuracy is observed for subtle, low-contrast structures (e.g., hippocampus, amygdala), our results highlight FeTal-SAM's potential as a flexible atlas-conditioned segmentation framework without requiring a separately trained model for each supported parcellation. This method thus constitutes a promising step toward clinically adaptable fetal brain MRI analysis tools.

title: Therapeutic potential and toxicological trade-offs of nanoparticle-enhanced valproic acid in glioblastoma: Behavioral and oxidative insights.
abstract: Background Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a poor prognosis. In the current research, the therapeutic and behavioral efficacy of valproic acid (VPA) and its nanoparticles (Nano VPA) with or without temozolomide (TMZ) was investigated in the C6 glioblastoma rat model. Methods We divided eighty-four adult male Wistar rats into seven groups (n = 12/group): sham, tumor, TMZ, VPA, nano VPA, VPA + TMZ, and nano VPA + TMZ. To induce tumors, C6 cells were injected into the brains of the rats. On days 12 to 15, behavioral performance was assessed using the social interaction test, elevated plus maze, open field, rotarod, and passive avoidance. On day 18, tumor size, edema, and histopathology were examined. Oxidative stress parameters in brain tissue and serum were measured by ELISA. Results VPA and Nano VPA significantly inhibited tumor growth, either alone or with TMZ. All treatments except Nano VPA + TMZ improved survival compared with tumor controls. Treated groups showed enhanced anxiety regulation, sociability, learning, and memory. Motor coordination improved following VPA or Nano VPA therapy. Tumor induction reduced serum SOD, CAT, and TAC levels; treatments raised serum TAC and lowered brain MDA, but further reduced serum SOD. Conclusion Our results suggest that oxidative stress modulation may contribute to the neurobehavioral and antitumor effects of both VPA and nano-VPA. While nano-VPA showed greater tumor reduction, conventional VPA was more effective in improving survival. Combining VPA with TMZ may enhance outcomes, and support further study of Nano VPA as an adjuvant therapy for GBM.

title: CAG repeat length shapes bidirectional functional connectome alterations in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3: a multimodal MRI study.
abstract: The ATXN3 gene is the primary driver of brain damage in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). We aimed to elucidate the patterns of connectome alterations shaped by cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) repeat length in SCA3. Eighty-nine genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 89 age-, sex-, education-matched healthy controls underwent multimodal MRI and comprehensive clinical assessments. Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) was used to identify functional connectivity patterns associated with CAG repeat length. Structural brain damage was assessed using voxel-based morphometry. Mediation analysis was performed to examine the role of structural impairment in connectivity changes. CPM identified a positive and a negative network, whose connectivity strength increased or decreased with CAG repeat length. The positive network (r = 0.397, P < 0.001) was mainly localized within the cerebello-motor circuit and was positively associated with ataxia severity and functional disability. The negative network (r = 0.243, P = 0.022) was distributed across large-scale networks, with selective vulnerability of interhemispheric connectivity, and was associated with motor dysfunction. Besides the canonical motor pathways, limbic-related connectivity was related to motor impairment. Structural analyses revealed widespread gray matter atrophy centered on the cerebellum. Cerebellar atrophy statistically mediated the association between CAG repeat length and connectivity decreases. CAG repeat length is associated with a bidirectional connectopathy in SCA3. Cerebellar atrophy may mediate the connectivity decreases. Future longitudinal studies are required to examine the underlying causal pathway.

title: Machine learning of connectome-wide functional connectivity in spinal muscular atrophy.
abstract: While traditional view posed SMA as a pure motor neuron disorder, accumulating evidence pointed to the broader involvement of central nervous system. This study aimed to combined connectome-wide resting-state functional connectivity with machine learning algorithms to investigate the underlying brain mechanisms in SMA and capture the potential neuroimaging biomarker. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging were acquired from 43 SMA (26 SMA type 2 and 17 type 3) and 45 healthy controls (HCs). Connectome-wide functional connectivity, defined based on the Automated Anatomical Labeling 116 atlas (AAL116), combined with machine learning algorithms including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) were conducted for SMA vs HCs and SMA type 2 vs 3 classification. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm was used to quantify the contribution of individual connections. Connectome-wide functional connectivity allowed individual classification of SMA and HCs with stable performance across machine learning models. The majority of the most discriminative functional connectivity involved the high-level associative regions and cerebellum, subserving sensory and motor processing. Furthermore, the functional connectivity between right superior parietal gyrus and right inferior temporal gyrus was positively correlated with motor function. In conclusion, our study provided connectome-wide evidence that functional connectivity patterns involving high-level associative cortices and the cerebellum could distinguish SMA from HCs using machine learning. The identified connectivity features offer new insight into the distributed brain pathology of SMA beyond the traditional classical motor neuron view, and may serve as promising neuroimaging marker for this disease.

title: Dynamic multi-scale topology learning and cross-modal graph fusion for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
abstract: Multi-modal fusion methods have demonstrated potential in integrating complementary information from different data modalities. However, existing methods often rely on static fusion strategies, failing to capture the heterogeneous interactions across modalities. To address this challenge, we propose the dynamic multi-scale topology learning and cross-modal interaction graph fusion network (DMTL-Net) for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) diagnosis. The model is designed to extract distinctive and complementary features from brain functional and structural networks while capturing their dynamic topological organization. Specifically, the structural radiomics similarity network (RSN) and functional connectivity network (FCN) are constructed from structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), respectively. Multi-modal graph initialization is performed by the cross-modal inclusive integration and consensus filtering to balance sensitivity and specificity. Then we propose the dynamic topology learning mechanism that integrates multi-scale feature extraction with adaptive channel-wise and spatial-wise fusion, effectively capturing complex inter-modal interactions. Additionally, focal loss is used to reduce the contribution of easy-to-classify samples and emphasize hard examples during optimization. Evaluated on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange dataset, the proposed DMTL-Net demonstrates superior performance and consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

title: Meningioma in the modern era: Updates in stratification and therapeutic approaches.
abstract: Meningioma is the most common primary intracranial tumor in adults. Most meningiomas have an indolent growth pattern, but some can grow quickly. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification system is the gold standard for tumor grading and relies predominantly on histopathology and limited molecular alterations. It is increasingly recognized that the variability in tumor behaviour is incompletely captured using traditional systems. Contemporary advances have expanded tumor stratification beyond starting WHO grading, providing a more comprehensive framework for understanding tumor biology. Molecular profiling has identified independent biological classification systems and molecular signatures that capture important prognostic information beyond histopathology. Magnetic resonance imaging-based analyses and radiomics have enabled non-invasive characterization of tumor phenotype and growth potential. Therapeutically, surgical resection and radiation therapy remain the foundation of management, with evolving paradigms emphasizing maximal safe resection and risk-adapted radiotherapy strategies informed by integrated tumor characteristics. Systemic therapies have historically shown limited efficacy; however, recent efforts are shifting toward biomarker-driven, precision approaches guided by molecular alterations. Future directions focus on integrating multimodal data into unified, clinically actionable models that more accurately predict recurrence, progression, and treatment response. Such approaches aim to move beyond parallel classification systems toward individualized management strategies, ultimately advancing meningioma care into a precision-based paradigm.

title: Diagnostic performance and methodological heterogeneity of neuromelanin-sensitive MRI in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Parkinson's disease (PD) diagnosis remains primarily clinical and is often delayed until substantial neurodegeneration has occurred. Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI (NM-MRI) assesses the integrity of neuromelanin-rich nuclei affected in PD, the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and locus coeruleus (LC), but its diagnostic performance, technical determinants, and translational applicability remain unclear amid heterogeneity. We aimed to quantify diagnostic accuracy, determine whether performance varies across methodological approaches, and contextualise evidence from clinically relevant settings. Methods We systematically reviewed NM-MRI diagnostic studies through December 2025. QUADAS-2 assessed risk of bias. Sensitivity and specificity were jointly pooled using a bivariate model, and AUC using random-effects meta-analysis. Subgroup analyses and exploratory meta-regressions assessed methodological heterogeneity; broader clinical evidence was synthesised qualitatively. Results Thirty-nine studies were included. Across 20 PD-versus-healthy-control (HC) studies (878 PD; 690 HCs), pooled sensitivity was 89.03% (95% CI 86.01-91.45%), specificity 87.02% (95% CI 82.76-90.34%), PLR 6.86, NLR 0.126, and DOR 54.37. Across 32 studies (1411 PD; 1086 HCs), pooled AUC was 0.909 (95% CI 0.884-0.929; I 2 = 64.6%). No significant unadjusted differences emerged by sequence, dimensionality, segmentation, or measurement type. NM-MRI abnormalities were detectable across prodromal, early- and advanced-stage PD, although global measures showed limited discrimination between disease stages. Subregional measures captured phenotypic variation, genotype discrimination was limited, and PD-versus-ET/APS performance was promising but variable, within small, heterogeneous evidence bases. Conclusion NM-MRI is a promising non-invasive imaging biomarker for PD, with strong discrimination across diverse methodological approaches. Harmonised acquisition and analysis, externally validated diagnostic thresholds, and prospective multicentre studies in clinically representative populations are needed to support future clinical implementation.

title: Investigation of CardioFreeze Motion Correction for Cardiac PET/CT.
abstract: Background Cardiac imaging with positron emission tomography and computed tomography (PET/CT) is a principal technique in the diagnosis and prognostication of coronary artery disease. PET/CT image quality can be negatively impacted by patient, cardiac, and respiratory motion. Methods We evaluated images from 102 patients clinically referred for cardiac rest/stress Rb-82 PET/CT myocardial perfusion imaging. Patient images were processed with a prototype data-driven motion detection algorithm and stratified by motion severity. Images were subjected to cardiac (CS) or cardiac and respiratory (CD) motion correction via a novel reconstruction tool. Validated image quality markers including target-to-background ratio (TBR) were assessed between corrected and non-corrected images and analyzed via student's t-tests. Results The motion detection algorithm identified 36 (35.3%) patients with significant motion. Image processing via CS yielded a statistically significant increase in mean image contrast (TBR 3.65±0.07, p<0.01) and intensified when respiratory motion correction was applied (3.78±0.07, p<0.005). Motion correction is more effective when applied to images containing greater motion, improving mean TBR by 3% (p<0.05) in non-motion scans but >10% (p<0.01) in significant motion cases. Three months post-imaging, 18 patients underwent clinically indicated coronary angiography: seven patients demonstrated significant motion, and CD motion correction improved their image quality to that of patients with no motion. Conclusions Over 1/3 of patients undergoing cardiac PET/CT have detectible motion leading to potential artifacts with clinical significance. Cardiac and respiratory motion correction improves image quality and may improve diagnostic accuracy, particularly when respiratory motion is severe. Further studies are critical to investigate the clinical impacts of improved image quality.

title: Applied nutritional investigation determinants of lower quadriceps skeletal muscle measured by ultrasound at ICU admission: a cross-sectional analysis.
abstract: Background Low skeletal muscle (SM) is common at ICU admission and is associated with worse prognosis. Early identification of at-risk patients is essential, but determinants of low SM in critically ill patients remains unclear. Objective To identify sociodemographic, nutritional, and clinical characteristics associated with low SM at ICU admission. Methods This cross-sectional analysis included critically ill patients ≥18 years admitted within 24 hours. Sociodemographic and nutritional data were obtained through anamnesis, while clinical data were extracted from records. Quadriceps muscle layer thickness (QMLT) was measured using a B-mode US. Lower QMLT was defined as values below the sex-specific 25th percentile of the sample. Binary logistic regression was performed. Results 399 patients were included (age 61.4 ± 14.9 years; 56.6% male). Older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.0-1.04), previous unintentional weight loss (OR = 1.64; CI 95% 1.03-2.61), reduced food intake before admission (OR = 2.32; CI 95% 1.44-3.74), and pressure injuries (OR = 1.83; CI 95% 1.05-3.20) were associated with low QMLT. However, in multivariate analysis, only older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.00-1.04) and reduced food intake (OR = 2.26; CI 95% 1.22-4.18) remained independent determinants. Conclusion Older age and reduced food intake were independently associated with lower QMLT at ICU admission. These findings highlight the need for early screening and targeted strategies to mitigate muscle loss and improve outcomes in critically ill patients.

title: OpenMSK: A modular open-source framework for comprehensive analysis of imaging biomarkers in knee osteoarthritis.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a fully automated, extendable, open-source AI-driven pipeline capable of knee magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation and quantitative extraction of MRI and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging biomarkers. Design For model training, open-source knee MRI data from 347 knees acquired across 7 scanners using multiple gradient-echo sequences were used. An independent test set of 20 knees from 3T PET-MRI examinations were used for evaluation in this prospective reliability and agreement study. The pipeline segmented femoral, tibial, and patellar bones and cartilage, and medial and lateral menisci using three different deep learning models. Quantitative outputs included cartilage thickness and T 2 relaxation times, meniscus volume and T 2 ∗ relaxation times, bone shape scores, and static and kinetic subchondral bone PET measures. Manual segmentations from two annotators served as reference standards. Segmentation performance was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients (DSC), average symmetric surface distances, and volume differences. Quantitative outcome agreement was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Pearson correlations, and root mean square error. Results Automated segmentations demonstrated high spatial agreement with manual annotations, with DSCs ranging from 0.84 to 0.98 across all tissues. Quantitative PET-MRI biomarkers generally demonstrated high agreement, although confidence intervals were wide for several biomarkers. Conclusion OpenMSK enables multi-tissue knee segmentation and generation of quantitative MRI and PET biomarkers, with performance assessed against two independent annotators and across different U-Net-based segmentation architectures. As a freely available, modular platform, OpenMSK lowers technical barriers to whole-joint quantitative imaging and provides a standardized foundation for OA research and clinical translation.

title: Optic disc drusen as a diagnostic confounder in a child with Alice in Wonderland syndrome.
abstract: We report the case of a 10-year-old boy referred for transient visual episodes compatible with Alice in Wonderland syndrome, described as a sensation that objects were moving away. Ophthalmic examination showed preserved visual acuity and an unremarkable anterior segment, but revealed elevation of the left optic disc, prompting evaluation for true papilledema. Macular OCT was normal, whereas optic nerve head OCT demonstrated structural asymmetry consistent with pseudopapilledema. Brain and orbital MRI showed isolated enlargement of both optic nerve sheaths and mild elevation of the left optic disc, without additional findings suggestive of intracranial hypertension. Orbital ultrasonography identified a hyperechogenic focus suggestive of optic disc drusen. The stable clinical and structural course supported the diagnosis of unilateral pseudopapilledema due to optic disc drusen, probably unrelated to the perceptual symptoms.

title: Advances in precision medicine for the anterior segment: therapeutic applications using CRISPR-Cas9.
abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has emerged as one of the most promising strategies in precision medicine applied to ophthalmology. Although its initial development focused on inherited retinal diseases, recent advances have increasingly targeted anterior segment disorders, including herpetic keratitis, hereditary corneal dystrophies, and genetically associated glaucoma. The ability to modify specific DNA or RNA sequences enables direct intervention in molecular pathways involved in inflammatory, degenerative, and infectious disease progression. This review summarizes the biological basis of CRISPR-Cas systems and discusses the main preclinical and translational findings related to corneal and glaucomatous diseases. Current limitations, including off-target effects, immunogenicity, and challenges associated with molecular delivery into ocular tissues, are also addressed. Available evidence suggests that CRISPR-Cas9 may significantly transform the future management of multiple anterior segment diseases.

title: Predicting taste alteration in head and neck cancer patients using 3D transformer-based deep learning model.
abstract: Purpose Taste alteration is a common post-treatment side effect of head and neck cancer (HNC) radiotherapy. Accurate normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models can support treatment planning aimed at reducing side effects that impair quality-of-life. Deep learning (DL) offers opportunities to incorporate full 3D dose, CT, and organofinterest (OOI) data. Using a large prospective cohort, this study explores whether CNN and transformerbased DL models can outperform a conventional logistic regression model for predicting taste alteration 6 months after radiotherapy. Material/methods Data from 972 patients was used, with the endpoint being moderatetosevere patientreported taste alteration at six months (EORTC QLQH&N35). DL models were trained using 3D dose distributions, planning CT, OOI segmentations and clinical features. A conventional NTCP model using oral cavity mean dose, parotid mean dose, and age served as reference. Attention maps were evaluated for the transformer-based DL model to quantify the model attention to specific regions of the head and neck area. In addition, two cropping approaches for the 3D data were compared. Results The CNN and transformer DL models performed comparable to the reference NTCP model in the test set (Reference: AUC = 0.71; ResNet: AUC = 0.68; TransRP: AUC = 0.71), though calibration was best for the reference model. Shifting the crop improved DL performance and transformer attention focused on supraglottic and submandibular regions. Conclusion This study showed that the prediction of taste alteration can be achieved using DL models, particularly transformer-based models which, in contrast to CNNs, can account for global features of comprehensive 3D information of dose distribution, CT-images and organs-of-interest segmentations.

Using a large prospective cohort, this study explores whether CNN and transformerbased DL models can outperform a conventional logistic regression model for predicting taste alteration 6 months after radiotherapy.

title: Systematic Review of Clinical Utility of Multimodal Imaging in Infectious Posterior Uveitis. Multimodal imaging in Uveitis (MUV) Taskforce Report 12.
abstract: Topic To systematically evaluate the clinical utility of multimodal imaging (MMI) for the diagnosis, activity assessment, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications in the five most prevalent infectious posterior uveitides. Design Systematic review and evidence-based quality appraisal. Participants Original research studies published between January 2018 and September 2025(primary cohort) and 2012-2017(supplemental cohort) evaluating MMI in ocular toxoplasmosis(TOXO), cytomegalovirus retinitis(CMVR), ocular tuberculosis(TB), syphilitic uveitis(SYPH), and acute retinal necrosis(ARN). Methods MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, and Scopus were systematically searched. Independent reviewers extracted reported imaging findings and clinical utility statements for: color fundus photography (CFP), fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA), indocyanine green angiography (ICGA), and OCT angiography (OCTA). Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), and certainty of evidence was graded using a bespoke consensus-based scheme informed by GRADE principles. Main outcome measures (1)reported imaging findings for each entity and modality; and (2)statements of clinical utility for diagnosis, detection of disease activity, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications. Results Among 122 included studies (82 primary and 40 supplemental), the primary studies contributed 5,522 individual patient examinations and 574 imaging statements, while the supplemental studies provided corroborating evidence. Overall, 366 clinical utility statements were identified across the four prespecified domains, including 30 statements supporting synergistic MMI strategies. CFP, including studies using ultra-widefield imaging, achieved high certainty for diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring in four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with moderate certainty in ARN. OCT achieved high certainty across all four clinical utility domains for four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with lower certainty in ARN owing to its limited evidence base. FFA achieved high certainty for complication detection in three of five entities. FAF achieved high certainty for disease activity in four of five entities. OCTA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for two of five entities, whereas ICGA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for only one of five entities. Conclusions Substantial evidence exists regarding the imaging findings and clinical utility of MMI in infectious posterior uveitis. Combined MMI enables integrated structural, vascular, and choroidal assessment beyond conventional clinical examination.

title: Longitudinal analysis of structural biomarkers for disease progression in intermediate age-related macular degeneration: a MACUSTAR study report.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the prognostic impact of qualitative and quantitative structural biomarkers including their topographic distribution for progression to geographic atrophy (GA) or neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) in eyes with intermediate AMD (iAMD) within the longitudinal part of the MACUSTAR study (NCT03349801). Design Longitudinal, prospective low-interventional European multicenter cohort study. Subjects 577 eyes of 577 study patients with iAMD. Methods Study eyes with iAMD underwent multimodal retinal imaging at each study visit followed by a standardized grading of structural biomarkers, including presence of subretinal drusenoid deposits (SDDs), vitelliform lesion, pigmentary abnormalities (PAs), refractile deposits, pigment epithelium detachment (PED), non-exudative choroidal neovascularization (nCNV), incomplete (i) retinal pigment epithelium and outer retinal atrophy (RORA), complete (c) RORA, and hyperreflective foci presence (HRF). Automated assessment of the retinal pigment epithelium drusen complex (RPEDC) volume and HRF area including their topographic distribution based on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging was conducted using a deep-learning based algorithm. Disease progression (GA/nAMD) was assessed at each study visit up to a follow-up time of 4 years. Multivariable time-discrete hazard models were used to evaluate the biomarkers' relevance for disease progression in the entire OCT volume, the central 3 mm disk, and the central subfield of the Early Treatment Diabetes Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) Grid. Main outcome measures Disease progression to GA/nAMD, hazard ratios of structural biomarkers for disease progression RESULTS: A total of 577 study eyes of 577 iAMD study patients (mean age 72.01 ± 7.01 years, 66.1 % female, median follow-up 3 years) were included. Disease progression was detected in 82 eyes (9.01 %), 37 (6.4 %) progressed to GA, and 45 (7.7 %) to nAMD. Inside the central 3 mm presence of SDDs, PED, nCNV and cRORA conferred overall risk for progression, whereas PAs, RPEDC volume, iRORA, cRORA were associated with risk for progression to GA. Only nCNV volume increased risk for nAMD. Conclusions Structural biomarkers indicate risk for iAMD progression and may differentiate eyes progressing to GA from eyes progressing to nAMD. Biomarker topography impacts their prognostic relevance and needs to be considered in clinical trial design.

title: Accuracy of soft tissue profile predictions using WebCeph and Dolphin software in non-growing skeletal Class II cases treated with upper premolar extractions: A retrospective comparative study.
abstract: Introduction Aesthetic outcomes are a primary concern for adult orthodontic patients. Clinicians often rely on soft tissue simulation software, such as Dolphin Imaging (D-Tech) and WebCeph (D-Tech), to manage patient expectations. This study aimed to compare the accuracy of these two tools in predicting soft tissue profile changes in non-growing skeletal Class II patients treated with maxillary first premolar extractions. Methods A retrospective comparative study was conducted on patients treated by the same practitioner with bilateral maxillary first premolar extractions and maximum anchorage. From a private-practice database of 2535 patients treated between January 2015 and January 2025, 34 met the inclusion criteria after eligibility screening. Pre- and post-treatment lateral cephalometric radiographs and profile photographs were used to generate simulations. Predicted cephalometric measurements from D-Tech and W-Tech were compared with each other and with the actual post-treatment results. Statistical analyses included paired t-tests, one-sample t-tests, Bland-Altman plots, and linear regression. Results Thirty-four patients (10 males, 24 females; 35.7±3.5 years) were analysed. Both tools showed a significant discrepancy in the nasolabial angle versus actual results (P<0.001). D-Tech differed significantly in the subnasale to Holdaway-line distance (mean difference 0.81mm [95% CI 0.03 to 1.60]; P=0.042), while W-Tech differed in upper and lower lip position relative to the True Vertical Line (LL-TVL P=0.004; UL-TVL P=0.006). For the remaining parameters, both tools showed good agreement; D-Tech showed a proportional bias for lip-TVL position (greater underestimation at larger values), whereas W-Tech overestimated lower lip thickness. Conclusion Both Dolphin Imaging and WebCeph provide clinically applicable predictions for most soft tissue parameters. Several statistically significant lip-position discrepancies were within the range generally considered clinically imperceptible (=1.5-2.0mm), whereas the nasolabial angle showed a discrepancy that is both statistically and clinically relevant. Predictions should therefore be interpreted with caution, particularly for parameters prone to systematic bias.

title: Diagnostic AI tools in musculoskeletal imaging-Present and future.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as the next step in musculoskeletal (MSK) imaging, yet its translation into routine clinical care, including osteoarthritis (OA), has been selective and challenging. This Perspective summarizes where diagnostic MSK AI tools stand today and argues that the central question is not whether models perform well in benchmarks, but whether they create measurable clinical value. Based on a keynote presentation at IWOAI 2026, we relate diagnostic AI tools in MSK imaging to the theme "Linking OA Tissues" by asking whether current AI tools can connect tissue-level imaging findings with whole-joint disease, longitudinal change, and clinical context. Drawing on the regulatory landscape and peer-reviewed evidence, we show that AI tools have been selectively translated into clinical routine: radiographic morphometry and fracture detection dominate among commercially available products because they are narrow, standardized tasks with transparent, easily verifiable outputs and an obvious clinical need. By contrast, MRI, the modality on which advanced OA assessment largely depends, remains a bottleneck. OA is a particularly challenging target because it is a multi-tissue, whole-joint, longitudinal, and context-dependent disease for which binary, single-task outputs are too crude. Furthermore, we propose a deliberately non-quantitative framework in which useful AI is the product of model performance, relevant endpoints, workflow fit, and human-AI interaction; failures of translation typically reflect deficits in the latter three rather than in model performance alone. Realizing clinical value in MSK and OA imaging will require validation against patient-relevant endpoints, attention to how readers interact with AI, and reference standards that go beyond curated benchmarks.

title: Correction of lower-limb deformities by intramedullary nailing.
abstract: Background Osteotomy to correct lower-limb deformity may be necessary when residual growth precludes asymmetric epiphysiodesis. Interlocking intramedullary nailing (IMN) provides minimally invasive stable fixation, spanning fragile segments, and compatible with bone lengthening, but requires precise preoperative planning and meticulous operative technique, as the room for postoperative adjustment is very limited. Our aim here is to present practical indications, planning principles, instrumentation, operative steps and postoperative management for safe and effective correction of femoral and tibial deformities using IMN. Methods This is a narrative technique-focused synthesis drawing on the authors' surgical experience and current operative principles to guide patient selection, imaging, osteotomy level, implant selection and intraoperative strategy. Five main questions are addressed: RESULTS: Preoperative clinical examination includes assessment of the stability and range of motion of the joints adjacent to the deformed bone segment. A scaled full-length standing radiograph with patellae facing forward is necessary for preoperative planning, along with a true lateral view. Intraoperatively, the patient is placed supine on a standard table fitted with an alignment grid. Contraindications include very severe or complex deformities and current or recent bone infection. IMN is suitable for correction of most cases of valgus/varus, pro-/re-curvatum and rotational deformities, and intramedullary motorized lengthening nails can also be applied in case of limb length discrepancy. Diaphyseal and metaphyseal deformities around the knee are the best indications. Straight reamers are recommended for metaphyseal deformities. Reference Schanz screws are placed above and below the planned osteotomy level for rotation control. A tube system, introduced like a working portal into the bone, seals the joint completely and maintains the reamer at the entry point in a constant trajectory according to the preoperative plan. Holes are drilled at the osteotomy site and serve as venting holes to decrease the risk of fat embolism during reaming and to enhance bone healing, like autologous bone grafting. Blocking screws can be used to increase stability in case of a wide medullary canal and/or to allow large corrections. IMN typically allows at least partial immediate weight-bearing and free range of motion without immobilization. Patients undergoing limb lengthening should be followed up regularly in the outpatient clinic by a multidisciplinary team assessing bone formation, implant-related complications and joint contractures. Conclusion Interlocking IMN is a versatile option for acute correction of most femoral and tibial diaphyseal and metaphyseal deformities, and for simultaneous length restoration using motorized nails when indicated. Success hinges on careful patient selection, planning based on the center of rotation and angulation (CORA), precise osteotomy placement and staged reaming, frequent use of blocking screws, Schanz-pin rotation control, and adjunct fixation when necessary, with regular follow-up. When complexity or juxta-articular epiphyseal involvement precludes IMN, hexapod external fixation is an alternative.

title: Acute intra-articular calcaneal fractures: currents concepts.
abstract: Calcaneal fractures are predominantly intra-articular and most commonly involve the subtalar joint, with an estimated incidence of 11,5 per 100,000 population and a male predominance. They occur mainly after high-energy trauma and are associated with substantial functional impairment and major socio-occupational consequences. Anatomical assessment (loss of height, posterior facet collapse, lateral wall widening, and varus displacement with superior migration of the tuberosity) determines prognosis and guides management. Plain radiographs (Böhler's and Gissane's angles) remain useful, but computed tomography is the reference standard for lesion characterization and preoperative planning. The surgery-versus -conservative debate has shifted with the development of minimally invasive techniques (sinus tarsi approach, percutaneous screw fixation and intramedullary nailing), which aim to restore hindfoot alignment, articular congruence and stability while reducing soft-tissue morbidity. Displaced Sanders II-III fractures represent the main indications for osteosynthesis, whereas Sanders type IV fractures are typically discussed between ORIF and primary subtalar arthrodesis. The most frequent complications remain soft tissue compromise and infection, as well as late sequelae (subtalar osteoarthritis, lateral subfibular impingement and residual varus). Current innovations focus on improving the reproducibility of reduction (arthroscopy-assisted techniques, balloon calcaneoplasty and navigation/robotics).

title: Cerebral Schistosoma japonicum infection confirmed by histopathology and PCR: Diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in multiple parasitic coinfections.
abstract: Cerebral schistosomiasis, a rare manifestation of schistosomiasis, is challenging to diagnose due to non-specificity in the clinical and radiologic findings and cross-reactivity in serologic testing with other helminths. Coinfection with multiple parasites further complicates diagnosis and treatment. A previously healthy 32-year-old Filipino man presented with a seizure. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed multiple clustered enhancing nodules with surrounding vasogenic edema in the left frontal lobe. Serologic testing was positive for anti-Schistosoma japonicum, Strongyloides, and Toxocara IgG antibodies. Follow-up MRI performed 20 days after the initial MRI demonstrated spontaneous resolution of preexisting enhancing lesions and the appearance of new non-contiguous lesions before antiparasitic therapy. Because imaging and serology analyses could not identify the causative organism, the left frontal lobe was biopsied. Histopathologic examination demonstrated schistosome eggs surrounded by granulomatous inflammation. PCR analysis of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue confirmed Schistosoma japonicum-mediated cerebral schistosomiasis. Following treatment of concomitant strongyloidiasis with ivermectin, the patient received praziquantel and corticosteroids without developing Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome. Follow-up MRI demonstrated resolution of the cerebral lesions. To our knowledge, this case documents previously undescribed dynamic pretreatment MRI changes together with the gross intraoperative appearance of cerebral schistosomiasis. Our findings highlight the diagnostic value of histopathologic confirmation when multiple parasitic infections coexist, underscoring the importance of detecting and treating concomitant Strongyloides stercoralis infection before corticosteroid therapy.

title: Macular retinal layer thickness in patients with severe congenital ptosis with and without amblyopia.
abstract: Objective To evaluate macular retinal layer thickness in patients with severe congenital ptosis with and without amblyopia and compare the findings with those of healthy controls. Methods This cross-sectional study included 69 patients (87 eyes) with severe congenital ptosis, comprising 32 patients (40 eyes) with amblyopia and 37 patients (47 eyes) without amblyopia, together with 38 healthy controls (38 eyes). Macular retinal thickness was measured using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). Automated segmentation quantified the inner five retinal layers (IRT), outer five retinal layers (ORT), and full retinal thickness (FRT) in the fovea, parafovea, and perifovea. Group differences were analyzed using analysis of covariance with adjustment for axial length (AL). title: Aromatherapy for Anxiety and Pain in Radiologic and Interventional Procedures a Scoping Review.
abstract: Objective To describe the scope of evidence on the use and effects of aromatherapy for reducing anxiety and pain in adults undergoing radiologic and interventional procedures. Design Scoping review guided by the Arksey and O'Malley framework and reported using PRISMA‑ScR guidelines. Data sources A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, and the Cochrane Library was conducted for studies published between 2013 and 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), cohort studies, case series, or pilot studies involving adults receiving an aromatherapy intervention during a diagnostic or interventional radiology procedure, with anxiety and/or pain as outcomes. Twenty-six RCTs met inclusion criteria. Data extraction captured essential oil (EO) type, delivery method, exposure duration, outcome measures, and main findings. Results Lavender was the most frequently studied EO, followed by peppermint, rose-based oils, citrus oils, chamomile, clary sage, Osmanthus fragrans, and Cananga odorata. EO's were delivered using cotton balls, gauze, aromatherapy tabs, patches, masks, inhalers, and diffusers. Anxiety was more frequently evaluated than pain. Reductions in anxiety were commonly reported, particularly in studies using lavender-based interventions, while findings related to pain were more variable. Marked heterogeneity in EO composition, delivery approaches, procedures, and outcome measurement tools limit cross-study comparison and generalizability. Conclusions Aromatherapy, particularly lavender, may reduce procedural anxiety, while evidence supporting pain reduction remains limited. Substantial methodological variability highlights the need for standardized protocols, transparent reporting of EO composition, and rigorous study designs to clarify clinical utility. Nursing practice implications Consistent with the American Society for Pain Management Nursing's emphasis on integrative, evidence-based care, aromatherapy may serve as a safe, nonpharmacologic adjunct to support patient well-being, particularly for procedural anxiety. Safe implementation requires nursing competency in EO selection, delivery methods, contraindications, and patient screening. Continued nursing leadership and advocacy are essential to advance multimodal, patient-centered approaches to procedural pain and anxiety management across care settings.

title: Re-irradiation for recurrent high-grade glioma: current evidence and practical considerations.
abstract: Re-irradiation is an increasingly important salvage option for patients with recurrent high-grade glioma and glioblastoma, but its use is complicated by limited prospective evidence, heterogeneous treatment approaches, and concern for cumulative toxicity to the brain and critical neurologic structures. Available studies suggest that carefully selected patients may achieve meaningful local control, symptom relief, and preservation of neurologic function, although a consistent overall survival benefit has not been demonstrated. Treatment decisions therefore require individualized assessment of performance status, neurologic function, disease volume and pattern, interval from prior radiation therapy, expected prognosis, alternative salvage options, and overlap with previously irradiated organs at risk. In this expert opinion, we summarize the contemporary evidence supporting brain re-irradiation and discuss available techniques; we also describe a practical, organ-at-risk-driven framework for patient selection, target delineation, fractionation, cumulative dose assessment, and integration of systemic therapy. Re-irradiation can be delivered safely in selected patients, but treatment intensity should remain closely aligned with anatomy, prognosis, therapeutic alternatives, and patient goals.

title: Multicenter Evaluation of a Deep Learning Model for Automatic Contouring of Cardiac Substructures in Adults.
abstract: Purpose Efficient delineation of cardiac substructures is essential for assessing radiation-induced cardiac toxicity in thoracic radiotherapy. We clinically evaluated a deep learning model designed for automated segmentation of these structures. Methods and materials The model built in collaboration with XXX (XXX) generated 21 cardiac substructures (whole heart, chambers, coronary arteries, valves, and great vessels). Five radiation oncologists rated raw contours on thirty contrast-enhanced CTs from two institutions using a 4-point Likert scale (3 = no correction, 2 = minor/moderate correction, 1 = major correction, 0 = not performed) and applied corrections when needed. Dice Similarity Coefficients (DSC) and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distances (HD95) were computed to compare model versus reference contours, clinician-corrected versus reference contours, and model versus STAPLE contours. Results Of 630 structures, 93.8% were scored either 3 or ≥2, and 6.2% received 1 by at least one clinician. For the coronary arteries (210 structures), 88.5% were scored either 3 or ≥ 2. Contour generation took approximately 1 min, with a median review and correction time of 7.0 min per CT (IQR, 5.8-9.8). The median DSC between the model and reference contours was 1.0 across all structures, while it ranged from 0.92 to 1.0 for clinician-corrected versus reference contours. Overall, HD95 was below 5 mm, for both clinicians versus reference and model versus STAPLE. Conclusions The deep learning model provided satisfactory segmentation of cardiac substructures on contrast-enhanced CT, including coronary arteries. Its integration into a widely adopted treatment planning system lays the foundation for broad clinical implementation.

title: Two-Year Outcomes of the XXX Trial: Longitudinal Analysis of Safety, PSA Kinetics, and Patient-Reported Outcomes.
abstract: Purpose To assess the 2-year incidence and longitudinal trajectory of grade (G) ≥2 genitourinary (GU) and gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events (AEs) following single-dose ablative radiotherapy (SDRT) for organ-confined prostate cancer (PCa), alongside associated changes in patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and PSA kinetics. Methods XXX (XXX) is a single-institution prospective study enrolling patients with unfavorable intermediate-risk or selected high-risk organ-confined PCa treated with SDRT delivering 24 Gy in one fraction to the prostate and seminal vesicles. Treatment incorporated urethra-sparing and intrafraction motion control and was delivered on a linear accelerator using a 10-MV flattening filter-free single partial arc in combination with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). AEs were graded using CTCAE v5.0. PSA and testosterone were monitored longitudinally, and scheduled multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) were performed to assess radiological response. PROs were assessed using EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-PR25, IPSS, and IIEF questionnaires. Mixed-effects models evaluated longitudinal trajectories and associations with baseline and dosimetric factors. Results Thirty patients were treated. At 2 years, no ≥G3 AEs were observed. Cumulative G2 GU and GI AEs were 23% and 7%, respectively. Two years point prevalent G2 GU and GI AEs were 10% and 3%, respectively. Longitudinal analysis showed an overall stable safety profile, with higher baseline IPSS and bladder trigone D1cc significantly associated with higher GU AEs. PRO analyses demonstrated statistically significant changes in urinary domains, although effect sizes remained below minimal important difference thresholds, indicating no clinically meaningful deterioration. Baseline symptom burden strongly predicted long-term PROs trajectories. Biochemical relapse-free survival was 100% at 2 years, with a consistent and significant PSA decline over time and local radiological control confirmed by mpMRI. Testosterone recovery occurred in 76% of patients receiving ADT. Conclusions Single-fraction 24 Gy SDRT combined with ADT was feasible and well tolerated, with low rates of ≥G2 AEs and largely maintained quality of life at 2 years in patients with unfavorable localized prostate cancer. Early oncologic outcomes are encouraging but require confirmation with longer follow-up and comparative validation.

title: Streamlining Liver SABR: Validation and Initial Experience of Bulk Density Override Based Single-Session, Simulation-Free Adaptive Workflow.
abstract: Purpose Conventional liver stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) typically requires a CT simulation visit followed by multiple treatment fractions, which can increase patient burden and limit access. We propose an approach that consolidates imaging, planning, adaptation, and delivery into one session, utilizing an MR-guided adaptive workflow. We report here the workflow and dosimetric validation of a streamlined bulk density override (BDO) strategy and the initial clinical implementation of this simulation-free approach. Methods and materials A single-institution phase II trial was designed to deliver liver SABR (30-40 Gy in 1 fraction) in a single-session using an MR-guided Linac for patients with liver cancers using BDO strategy. To validate dosimetric accuracy, 17 previously treated single-fraction liver SABR plans were recalculated retrospectively using (1) CT-based electron density and (2) BDO-based density. DVH endpoints and 3D gamma analysis (1%/1mm) were compared. Early clinical experience from the first five trial patients is reported, including dose comparisons between BDO-based calculations and diagnostic CT-based calculations. Results For the retrospective analysis, BDO-based calculation closely matched the CT-based calculation. For the PTV and GTV, the median percent differences were close to zero for all evaluated metrics and the maximum percent differences were all within 2%. For organ-at-risk (OAR) endpoints (chest wall, bowel, liver minus GTV, spinal cord), mean and maximum dose differences were within 0.1 Gy and 0.6 Gy, respectively. The average 3D gamma pass rate was 99.2%. For the first 5 patients treated on trial, BDO- and diagnostic CT-based reference plan metrics agreed within 1.5% for PTV coverage and within 0.5 Gy for key OAR endpoints. The mean gamma pass rate was 98.8%. Conclusions The BDO strategy provides dosimetric agreement comparable to CT-based calculation and supports an efficient and patient-centric single-visit delivery model. Our results support further investigation of simulation-free, single-session MR-guided adaptive liver SABR.

title: Anxiety sensitivity, psychological vulnerability, and brain volumes in borderline personality disorder.
abstract: Aim This study compared AS, psychological vulnerability, and brain volumes in BPD and healthy controls and examined clinical-volumetric associations within BPD. Method Twenty-seven patients with BPD and 28 healthy controls completed the Anxiety Sensitivity Index-3 and the Psychological Vulnerability Scale. Three-dimensional T1-weighted images were acquired using a 1.5-Tesla MRI scanner, and regional volumes were calculated. Results In raw analyses, the BPD group had higher psychological vulnerability and total, cognitive, and social AS scores. After covariate adjustment, only social AS remained significant (p = 0.035). Bilateral putamen, anterior insula, caudate, nucleus accumbens, and total gray matter volumes were larger in the BPD group, persisting after adjustment (all p ≤ 0.018). Differences in left amygdala, posterior and total insula, posterior cingulate gyrus, and white matter volumes lost significance after adjustment. In the BPD group, posterior insula volumes were negatively correlated with total and social AS scores, remaining significant after controlling for confounders (r=-0.471 to -0.611; p = 0.004-0.036). Psychological vulnerability and cognitive AS were not associated with regional volumes. Conclusion Social AS may represent a specific dimension of BPD. Group-level differences in anterior insula and striatal volumes, together with dimensional associations between posterior insula volumes and AS, suggest distinct roles for insular subregions in BPD-related clinical and structural processes.

title: Nasopharyngeal diffuse large b-cell lymphoma in a teenage presenting with cavernous sinus syndrome: A case report.
abstract: Primary lymphoma of the nasopharynx is uncommon and is more commonly seen as an association with other primary pathologies. Nasopharyngeal lymphoma is an aggressive tumor and can affect all age groups but is more commonly seen in middle-aged and older individuals. Majority of these tumors belong to the non-Hodgkin's group. Cavernous sinus syndrome (CSS) is a rare but severe complication indicating advanced aggressive stage of disease with direct extension of tumor into the cavernous sinus. Our patient is a young teenage 18-years old presented to emergency department with the symptoms of left jaw pain (4 months), facial swelling (1 month), bilateral nasal obstruction, dysphagia (1 month), visual loss in left eye and proptosis (1 week) along with weight loss. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) face and neck with contrast performed immediately revealed a nasopharyngeal mass with extension of disease into the left cavernous sinus encasing cavernous part of the left internal carotid artery (ICA), involvement of the left orbital apex, optic chiasm and pituitary gland. Histopathology later confirmed diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Laboratory investigations were unremarkable except for an elevated ESR. The patient underwent multidisciplinary management with combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy, demonstrating an excellent response on follow-up MRI and PET-CT, and was discharged with appropriate follow-up instructions. This case highlights early recognition with MRI and histopathological confirmation enables timely chemotherapy, improving outcomes and reducing the risk of permanent neurological sequelae.

title: Delayed radiographic diagnosis of distal femoral metastases in breast cancer: A case report from Cocody University Teaching Hospital (Côte d'ivoire).
abstract: Bone metastases represent a frequent complication of breast cancer, affecting more than one third of patients. Delayed investigation of persistent focal bone pain in a breast cancer patient can lead to serious consequences. We report a case of delayed radiographic diagnosis of distal femur metastases in a breast cancer patient, where the initial standard X-ray was normal. The diagnosis of bone metastasis was established by a second X-ray 11 months later, following disease progression. This case highlights the limitations of conventional radiography and highlights the importance of using PET-CT, MRI, or bone scintigraphy imaging modalities methods for early detection of metastatic lesions to guide therapeutic management.

title: The 'Upstairs-Downstairs' heart with complete main pulmonary artery agenesis and PDA-dependent pulmonary circulation: A rare structural intersection characterized by multi detector computed tomography.
abstract: Superior-inferior ventricular arrangement is an exceedingly rare form of congenital cardiac malposition, representing fewer than 0.1% of all congenital heart diseases, and is almost invariably associated with complex intracardiac anomalies. We report a 3-year-old male who presented with persistent cyanosis, exertional dyspnea, and failure to thrive. Prospective ECG-gated CT angiography demonstrated situs solitus with levocardia. A superior-inferior ventricular arrangement was present, with the morphologic left ventricle positioned superior to the morphologic right ventricle. The great arteries were normally related, with a left-sided aortic arch. A large ventricular septal defect was identified. Pulmonary atresia was present, characterized by the absence of the right ventricular outflow tract, pulmonary valve, and main pulmonary artery. Native confluent branch pulmonary arteries were present and received pulmonary blood flow through a large patent ductus arteriosus supplying the left pulmonary artery, with additional small systemic-to-pulmonary collateral vessels. The morphologic right ventricle was dilated and hypertrophied, with associated enlargement of the right atrium. Pulmonary venous drainage was normal, and no abnormalities of the systemic venous drainage were identified. This case underscores the critical role of cardiac CT angiography in comprehensive anatomical delineation of rare and complex congenital cardiac malformations, with direct implications for surgical planning and prognostication.

title: Isolated cerebellopontine angle metastasis from breast cancer: The added value of MR spectroscopy.
abstract: Cerebellopontine angle (CPA) tumors are predominantly vestibular schwannomas and meningiomas; metastatic lesions in this location are rare, particularly in the absence of multiple brain metastases. We report the case of a 53-year-old woman with a history of invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast in HER2-positive metastatic relapse, in whom brain MRI revealed a single 28 × 24 mm mass in the right cerebellopontine angle. The lesion was isointense on T1- and T2-weighted images, contained fluid components, and showed restricted diffusion (ADC 0.64 × 10⁻³ mm²/s) with intense peripheral enhancement after gadolinium administration. MR spectroscopy demonstrated markedly elevated Cho/NAA (6.73) and Cho/Cr (5.72) ratios within the lesion, with a normal perilesional spectroscopic profile, favoring a secondary lesion and allowing the main differential diagnoses to be excluded without biopsy. The patient underwent stereotactic radiotherapy (30 Gy in 5 fractions), with significant regression of the lesion on follow-up MRI at five months. This case illustrates the role of MR spectroscopy in the non-invasive characterization of atypical cerebellopontine angle lesions.

title: Stopping too soon: Search termination and subsequent search misses in diagnostic radiography.
abstract: Introduction Diagnostic radiography requires balancing image evaluation, dose optimisation, and workflow efficiency within time-constrained clinical environments. Image acceptance depends on detecting technical issues and determining when further inspection is unnecessary and when an image is sufficient for clinical purposes. Visual search theory suggests that observers rely on internal stopping rules to guide termination decisions, yet their role in radiographic image adequacy remains underexplored. This paper develops a model of radiographic search termination. Methods A conceptual model was developed through narrative synthesis of literature from cognitive psychology, medical image perception and radiology. Relevant studies were selected to identify key constructs, including quitting rules, subsequent search misses, inattentional blindness and confidence during incomplete search. These constructs were integrated to generate a radiography-specific framework explaining search termination. Results A model is presented in which radiographic image evaluation is considered a multiple-target visual search task governed by an internal stopping threshold. This threshold reflects when the expected benefit of continued inspection falls below its perceived cost. It may be shaped by perceptual evidence, time pressure, workload, interruptions, target prevalence, patient presentation, observer confidence, experience and departmental norms. The model proposes three candidate termination patterns: global-impression termination, target-substitution termination and constraint-driven termination. It also identifies structured second-pass inspection, confidence calibration and feedback on missed secondary inadequacies as theoretically informed strategies requiring empirical investigation. Conclusion Framing image acceptance as a stopping-policy decision provides a cognitive explanation for variability in adequacy assessment and repeat imaging. Search termination reflects a dynamic balance between thoroughness and efficiency under uncertainty. Implications for practice Integrating visual search theory into education and workflow design may support better calibration of stopping thresholds, improving image quality, reducing unnecessary repeats, and supporting clinically meaningful decision-making.

title: Diagnosing endometriosis in adolescents using ultrasound and MRI: A scoping review of imaging approach and implementation considerations.
abstract: Introduction Imaging is increasingly used for adult endometriosis, but evidence supporting adolescent imaging approaches remains unclear. This scoping review mapped evidence on imaging-based diagnosis of endometriosis in adolescents and young people, including ultrasound and MRI approaches, imaging-detected disease phenotypes, consent, acceptability, and AI-assisted imaging. Methods Studies involving people with suspected or confirmed endometriosis were eligible if participants were aged 14-25 years or the population was explicitly described as adolescent, teenage, youth, or young adult. Author-defined adolescent cohorts could therefore include participants younger than 14 years. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL and Web of Science were searched, alongside grey literature and reference lists. Screening and extraction were completed independently in duplicate. Data were synthesised descriptively. Results Thirty-five evidence sources were included: nine primary studies and 26 secondary sources. The primary evidence base was limited, heterogeneous and mostly specialist-based. Ultrasound was the sole or initial modality in eight of nine primary studies; MRI was used in four. Imaging findings were most consistent for ovarian endometrioma and posterior deep endometriosis. Superficial disease was poorly captured, and normal imaging remained common in symptomatic cohorts. Secondary sources commonly described ultrasound-first approaches, with selective use of transvaginal ultrasound, transrectal ultrasound, or MRI. Acceptability, feasibility, consent and refusal were frequently discussed in secondary sources but rarely measured in primary studies. No adolescent-specific primary studies evaluated AI-assisted imaging. Conclusion Imaging is recommended in clinical guidance for adolescent endometriosis and evaluated in selected cohorts, but the evidence remains limited, heterogeneous and largely adult-derived. Implications for practice Imaging is an important component of adolescent endometriosis assessment. Modality choice and examination approach should be individualised through informed consent. Negative imaging should not be interpreted as excluding endometriosis, particularly superficial disease, when symptoms persist.

Imaging is an important component of adolescent endometriosis assessment. Modality choice and examination approach should be individualised through informed consent. Negative imaging should not be interpreted as excluding endometriosis, particularly superficial disease, when symptoms persist.

title: Doses in planning computed tomography in one radiotherapy department: Description of exposure parameters and estimation of organ doses, effective doses and typical doses.
abstract: Introduction Computed tomography (CT) used in radiotherapy (RT) planning involves complex acquisitions protocols, making it essential to evaluate doses and ensure patients' radiological safety. This study aims to evaluate organ doses based on RT planning CT scans, Effective Doses (ED), and Typical Doses, in a Portuguese RT department. Methods The sample included 151 patients who underwent planning CT using the General Electric (GE) Discovery ™ RT scanner. Dosimetric estimates were obtained with the National Cancer Institute Dosimetry System for Computed Tomography (NCICT). For each examination, acquisition parameters, patient anatomical diameters, Volume Computed Tomography Dose Index (CTDI vol ), Dose-Length Product (DLP), organ absorbed doses, and ED were analysed. Results Typical Dose values were proposed, based on the 50th percentile of CTDI vol and DLP distributions of the main RT protocols: head and neck (H&N), central nervous system (CNS), breast, breast and axilla, breast deep inspiration breath hold (DIBH), 4D lung, stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) lung and prostate. Results were compared with the literature, to assess practice and identify optimization areas. Conclusion These findings improve understanding of local practices and highlight the importance of periodic protocol evaluation. Furthermore, this study provides a basis for dose optimization strategies and supports the definition of diagnostic reference levels (DRL) in RT services. Implication for practice This study demonstrates the importance of evaluating and monitoring CT protocols in RT planning to ensure patient safety and minimize radiation exposure. The analysis of organ doses, ED, and local DRL provides concrete values reflecting current practice. These findings can guide protocol adjustments, support definition of typical dose levels and contribute to future optimisation strategies in RT.
