title: Diagnostic accuracy of musculoskeletal ultrasound in suspected polymyalgia rheumatica: a multicentre, cohort study.
abstract: Background Diagnosing polymyalgia rheumatica is challenging, and musculoskeletal ultrasound is primarily used in diagnostically difficult situations. Previous musculoskeletal ultrasound studies in patients with polymyalgia rheumatica used case-control designs or non-representative cohorts, reducing assessment of diagnostic accuracy. This study aimed to assess the diagnostic accuracy of musculoskeletal ultrasound in two independent cohorts of patients with suspected polymyalgia rheumatica. Methods This multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study included consecutive, glucocorticoid-naive patients with suspected polymyalgia rheumatica, referred for rheumatology evaluation at the University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands (retrospective cohort), between April 30, 2019, and Feb 13, 2024, and at Aarhus University Hospital, Silkeborg Regional Hospital, and Horsens Regional Hospital, Denmark (prospective cohort), between Sept 14, 2020, and June 30, 2022. The Aarhus cohort included patients older than 50 years with proximal muscle or joint pain and excluded patients with cranial symptoms suggestive of giant cell arteritis, cancer within the past 5 years, or pre-existing inflammatory rheumatic disease. No explicit referral criteria were applied in the Groningen cohort. Participants underwent protocolised clinical examination and musculoskeletal ultrasound. The reference standard was clinical diagnosis after 6 months (Groningen) or 12 months (Aarhus) of follow-up. Musculoskeletal ultrasound assessment included subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis, biceps tenosynovitis, and hip synovitis in both cohorts, plus glenohumeral synovitis and trochanteric bursitis in the Groningen cohort. A polymyalgia rheumatica ultrasound lesion count was calculated based on six (Aarhus) and ten (Groningen) sites. Diagnostic performance of individual and combined lesions was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. There was no lived experience involvement in the study design or conduct. The Aarhus cohort study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04519580. Findings The Groningen cohort included 92 patients patients with suspected polymyalgia rheumatica (41 [45%] male, 51 [55%] female, mean age 69 years [SD 9]), of whom 58 (63%) were diagnosed with polymyalgia rheumatica after 6-month follow-up. The Aarhus cohort included 93 patients (53 [57%] male, 40 [43%] female, mean age 71 years [SD 8]), 66 (71%) of whom had a diagnosis of polymyalgia rheumatica at 12 months. No single musculoskeletal ultrasound finding was pathognomonic for polymyalgia rheumatica. The combination of musculoskeletal ultrasound findings with the highest sensitivity was the presence of at least one inflammatory lesion (Groningen: 10-site polymyalgia rheumatica ultrasound lesion count 93% [95% CI 83-98]; Aarhus: 6-site polymyalgia rheumatica ultrasound lesion count 92% [83-98]). The combination with highest specificity was the presence of at least one inflammatory lesion in both the shoulder and hip girdles (Groningen: 85% [95% CI 69-95]; Aarhus: 93% [76-99]). ROC analysis showed an area under the curve of 0·779 (95% CI 0·675-0·883) for the 10-site count in Groningen and 0·769 (0·664-0·875) for the 6-site count in Aarhus. Musculoskeletal ultrasound performed better in distinguishing polymyalgia rheumatica from non-inflammatory conditions than from other inflammatory rheumatic diseases. Interpretation Absence of shoulder and hip lesions on musculoskeletal ultrasound makes a polymyalgia rheumatica diagnosis unlikely. However, their presence requires careful clinical evaluation, as similar findings occur in other inflammatory rheumatic diseases. These findings support the use of musculoskeletal ultrasound as a potential adjunct to clinical assessment when evaluating patients with suspected polymyalgia rheumatica. Funding FOREUM, Danish Rheumatism Association, Independent Research Fund Denmark, Ketty and Ejvind Lyngsbæks Foundation, Frimodt-Heineke's Foundation, Aase and Ejnar Danielsen's Foundation, AP Møller Foundation, Health Research Foundation of Central Denmark Region, and Regional Hospital Central Jutland Research Foundation.

title: Cognitive fusion-modulated structural covariance networks predict treatment response in drug-naive OCD: A multiscale neuroimaging-transcriptomic study.
abstract: Background Cognitive fusion (CF), a core maladaptive process in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), describes overidentification with intrusive thoughts. While implicated in symptom maintenance, its neuroanatomical basis and treatment prediction utility remain poorly understood. Methods We enrolled 80 first-episode, drug-naïve OCD patients and 70 matched healthy controls. All participants underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging and clinical assessment. Patients received 8-week selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors treatment with endpoint reevaluation. Using multimodal neuroimaging, we examined group differences in gray matter volume (GMV) and structural covariance network (SCN), tested whether CF levels modulated connectivity, and evaluated baseline features for predicting treatment response. Transcriptomic analysis linked the findings to the Allen Human Brain Atlas data. Results OCD patients showed GMV reductions in frontal-limbic regions and increases in parietal/inferior frontal areas. SCN analysis revealed enhanced structural covariance within fronto-parieto-cerebellar circuits. Higher CF scores were associated with stronger structural coupling between the left angular gyrus and the right middle temporal/medial superior frontal gyri. Baseline GMV in the left dorsolateral superior frontal gyrus (SFGdl) positively correlated with CF improvement, remaining significant after controlling for overall symptom reduction. Transcriptomic analysis indicated the left SFGdl GMV patterns spatially associated with glutamatergic synapse and calcium signaling pathways. Conclusions CF in OCD links to altered structural integration between large-scale networks, with the left SFGdl emerging as a potential CF-specific treatment predictor. This multiscale study highlights combining neuroimaging with psychological constructs to understand treatment-relevant changes in OCD.

Transcriptomic analysis indicated the left SFGdl GMV patterns spatially associated with glutamatergic synapse and calcium signaling pathways.

Conclusions

CF in OCD links to altered structural integration between large-scale networks, with the left SFGdl emerging as a potential CF-specific treatment predictor. This multiscale study highlights combining neuroimaging with psychological constructs to understand treatment-relevant changes in OCD.

title: Structural network alterations and peripheral immune-inflammatory dysregulation define distinct subtypes of major depressive disorder with prognostic implications.
abstract: Background Immune-inflammatory dysregulation and cortical structural vulnerability have been increasingly implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, how they interact with each other, and whether immune heterogeneity in MDD is systematically organized by structural networks, remain unclear. Methods Genome-wide association studies data of MDD, gray matter volume (GMV) phenotypes, and 19 immune-related traits were utilized to assess causal relationships. A prospective cohort comprising 122 patients with MDD and 66 healthy controls underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging and assessment of 40 inflammatory and immune-related markers. Individualized structural covariance network analysis, machine-learning approaches, and survival analyses were used to identify neurobiological subtypes and evaluate treatment outcomes. Results Genetically predicted MDD was associated with lower levels of circulating IGF-1 ( p FDR = 0.013). Levels of IL-5 and leptin were negatively associated with GMV alterations in the right cingulate gyrus and bilateral putamen, respectively ( p FDR < 0.05). Structural covariance abnormalities were predominantly localized to connectivity between the default mode and limbic networks and within the limbic network in MDD, and they were classified into a hypoconnectivity subtype ( n = 49) and a hyperconnectivity subtype ( n = 73). The hypoconnectivity subtype exhibited greater anxiety and anhedonia symptoms, whereas the hyperconnectivity subtype showed broadly elevated inflammatory and immune state and achieved antidepressant response more rapidly during follow-up ( p = 0.032). Conclusions This study supports a bidirectional immune-brain framework in MDD and suggests that structure-derived subtypes classify different immune signaling heterogeneity, which may provide a biologically informed basis for stratification and prognosis in MDD.

title: Bilateral vs unilateral pleural drains in tetralogy of Fallot repair.
abstract: Objectives To compare postoperative outcomes after tetralogy of Fallot repair in patients managed with unilateral versus bilateral pleural drains. Methods In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing complete tetralogy of Fallot repair between 2020 and 2025 were included. Patients with previous complete repair, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, delayed sternal closure, or chylothorax were excluded. The primary outcome was undrained postoperative pleural effusion on routine chest radiographs. Secondary outcomes were postoperative pleural drain insertion, duration of invasive mechanical ventilation, diuretic score, ICU length of stay, and pleural drain-related complications. Multivariable regression adjusted for repair type, bypass duration, cross-clamp duration, and surgeon. Results Of 180 patients, 122 (68%) underwent unilateral pleural drain placement and 58 (32%) bilateral placement. Complex repairs were more common in the bilateral group. Undrained pleural effusion was more frequent after unilateral than bilateral pleural drain placement (42.6% vs 5.2%; p < 0.001). Postoperative pleural drain insertion was required in 9 patients (7.4%) in the unilateral group and in none in the bilateral group ( p = 0.06). Pleural drain-related complications were more frequent with bilateral pleural drains, with 4 pneumothoraces requiring intervention versus 1 self-resolving subcutaneous emphysema in the unilateral group ( p = 0.01). In multivariable analysis, bilateral pleural drain placement remained independently associated with lower odds of undrained pleural effusion, but not with duration of mechanical ventilation, diuretic score, or ICU length of stay. Conclusions Bilateral pleural drains were associated with fewer radiographic pleural effusions but no measurable short-term clinical advantage. Placement should therefore be individualised according to intraoperative findings and local practice.

title: Artificial intelligence in paediatric cardiac critical care: from predictive analytics to continuous physiologic intelligence.
abstract: Objective Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in paediatric cardiology and cardiac intensive care, where CHD, postoperative physiologic instability, and continuous bedside monitoring generate complex datasets. This review summarises current applications of artificial intelligence in paediatric cardiology and the cardiac ICU, focusing on cardiac imaging, electrocardiography, predictive analytics, waveform intelligence, and postoperative outcome prediction. Data sources A narrative review of PubMed, MEDLINE, and Scopus was performed for studies published from 2018 through 2026 evaluating artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in paediatric cardiology, CHD, congenital heart surgery, and cardiac critical care. Study selection Studies addressing paediatric or CHD-focused applications in echocardiography, cardiac MRI, electrocardiography, cardiac ICU monitoring, waveform analytics, or postoperative complication prediction were included, together with relevant reviews. Data extraction Information was extracted on study population, artificial intelligence method, clinical task, model inputs, outcomes, validation strategy, and major limitations. Data synthesis Artificial intelligence is most developed in imaging and electrocardiography, while paediatric and complex CHD evidence remains less mature. In cardiac ICU, models using electronic health record variables, high-frequency physiologic data, and risk indices have been evaluated for cardiac arrest, low cardiac output physiology, hyperlactatemia, extubation failure, and vasoactive de-escalation. External validation, prospective deployment, calibration, and workflow-safe implementation remain major gaps. Conclusions Artificial intelligence may improve diagnostic consistency, risk stratification, and early recognition of deterioration, but prospective validation and measurable clinical benefit are needed before autonomous use.

title: De Novo Design of a TROP-2-Targeting Peptide PET Tracer via AI-Guided Binding Interface Mimicry.
abstract: Trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP-2) is a transmembrane glycoprotein overexpressed across a range of epithelial malignancies, yet its clinical assessment still relies largely on invasive immunohistochemical analysis of biopsied tissues. In this study, we employed the PepMimic artificial intelligence platform to de novo design a TROP-2-targeting peptide, TR23, via binding interface mimicry, which was subsequently conjugated with DOTA and radiolabeled with 68Ga to yield the peptide-based PET probe [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TR23. The tracer bound TROP-2 with nanomolar affinity (KD = 26.8 nM), showed selective cellular uptake in TROP-2-positive cells, and exhibited high radiochemical purity (>95%) with excellent stability in saline and serum. Micro-PET/CT imaging in pancreatic (BxPC-3), prostate (PC3), and thyroid (BCPAP) xenograft models revealed rapid, specific tumor accumulation with high contrast and low background uptake, while competitive blocking studies with excess unlabeled TR23 substantially suppressed tumor uptake, confirming receptor-mediated specificity. Quantitative analysis further demonstrated strong positive correlations between SUVmax and TROP-2 expression levels verified by immunohistochemistry across all three tumor types. Collectively, these findings establish [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TR23 as a promising peptide-based PET tracer for rapid, specific, and quantitative imaging of TROP-2-positive tumors, and highlight the PepMimic-enabled strategy as a versatile platform for peptide-based probe discovery, supporting the translational potential of this tracer as a pan-cancer diagnostic agent for precision molecular imaging.

title: Preclinical Evaluation of 68Ga-Labeled Heterodimers for Dual Integrin αvβ3 and PARP1-Targeted Tumor Imaging.
abstract: Tumor heterogeneity limits the diagnostic performance of molecular imaging probes targeting a single biomarker. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and preclinical evaluation of 68Ga-labelled heterodimeric radiotracers co-targeting integrin αvβ3 and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) through a proposed "binding-anchoring" concept strategy. Conjugating the tumor-penetrating iRGD peptide with the PARP1 inhibitor niraparib and incorporating an albumin-binding moiety yielded the lead probe [68Ga] Ga-NY-Dual-IP. Molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance supported nanomolar target-binding capability of the corresponding non-radiolabeled precursors. In the 4T1 breast cancer model, [68Ga] Ga-NY-Dual-IP exhibited a tumor uptake of 7.29 ± 0.28% ID/g at 1 h, approximately 4-5-fold higher than that of the corresponding single-target probes. Cytotoxicity, haemolysis and histopathological analyses confirmed excellent biocompatibility. These findings established [68Ga] Ga-NY-Dual-IP as a promising PET probe for precise tumor imaging and potential clinical translation.

title: Mild, Fast, and General Biocatalytic Deprotection Strategies for Automated Fluorine-18 Positron Emission Tomography Radiotracer Synthesis.
abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) has become an essential tool in nuclear medicine, driving the continuous development of new radiotracers. Owing to the short half-life of fluorine-18 (110 min), radiotracer production requires fast, robust, and fully automated synthetic protocols. Reactive functional groups present on precursor molecules must be protected to prevent competition during radiofluorination, with deprotection typically achieved under harsh chemical conditions that may compromise automation and lead to partial molecular degradation. Herein, we report a general biocatalytic deprotection strategy based on porcine liver esterase (PLE) as a mild and efficient alternative to conventional chemical methods. Three protecting groups (valerate, pivaloyloxymethyl and pivaloyl ethylidene carbamate) were selected to enable the PLE-deprotection of a broad range of functional groups found in radiotracers and drugs (alcohols, phenols, carboxylic acids, amines, anilines, sulfonamides). The PivEC protective group of amines, anilines and sulfonamides was specifically developed for allowing an esterase deprotection. This approach was validated across a broad substrate scope and was successfully automated on ORA-Neptis modules for clinically relevant PET tracers, including [18F]FMISO, [18F]CABS13, and [18F]Nifene. This work establishes enzymatic deprotection as a versatile and practical strategy for PET scan application.

title: First-In-Human PET Imaging of Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A with [18F]BIBD-181: Automation, Biodistribution, Dosimetry, and Preliminary Application in Epilepsy.
abstract: We report the first-in-human evaluation of [18F]BIBD-181, a novel SV2A tracer designed with a fluoropropyl side chain to enable mild, automated radiosynthesis. A fully automated cGMP-compliant production process was developed on a commercial synthesizer, yielding the tracer with >95% radiochemical purity and molar activity >130 GBq/μmol. In eight healthy volunteers, [18F]BIBD-181 demonstrated excellent safety, rapid brain penetration peaking at 15 s post-injection, and a regional uptake pattern consistent with known synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) distribution (pallidum SUV = 2.01 ± 0.57 at 30 min). The effective dose was 2.7 μSv/MBq, with predominant renal clearance and no detectable defluorination. In pilot epilepsy patients, [18F]BIBD-181 positron emission tomography (PET) results revealed focal SV2A reductions that were confined to the epileptogenic lesionsa sclerotic hippocampus in one patient and a focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) in anotherwhereas [18F]FDG showed either extensive ipsilateral temporal hypometabolism or concordant focal hypometabolism, suggesting that SV2A imaging may offer more precise lesion delineation, particularly when [18F]FDG abnormalities extend beyond the true epileptogenic zone. These findings establish [18F]BIBD-181 as a clinically practical SV2A PET tracer with favorable dosimetry, simplified production, and promising utility for epilepsy surgical planning, warranting further validation in larger cohorts.

title: Manganese-Doped Fluorinated Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-90 for Activatable 1H/19F MRI and Metalloimmunotherapy of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: In the immunotherapy of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is substantially limited by the complex and highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Therefore, developing approaches to effectively reverse the immunosuppressive TME while enabling accurate HCC imaging poses a major unmet challenge. To tackle this critical challenge, we rationally designed and constructed a hyaluronic acid (HA)-functionalized manganese-doped fluorinated zeolitic imidazolate framework-90 (ZIF-90) nanosystem (ZM-F6@HA NPs) for integrated theranostic applications in HCC. This nanosystem not only enabled noninvasive and precise visualization of HCC lesions through GSH-activatable 1H/19F MRI for diagnostic purposes, but also induced robust tumor-associated inflammation and promoted potent antitumor adaptive immunity through synergistic mechanisms, including cGAS-STING pathway activation, immunogenic cell death (ICD) induction, and pyroptosis induction in HCC cells. The activated antitumor immune response effectively remodeled the immunosuppressive TME, and its combination with ICIs results in significant tumor regression and substantial inhibition of lung metastasis. This responsive ZIF-90-based multifunctional nanosystem provides a promising and rational strategy for integrated diagnosis and combinatorial immunotherapy of HCC.

title: Chemically Informed Artificial Intelligence Decoding of Full-Spectrum SERS Fingerprints for pH-Guided Intraoperative Assessment of Freshly Excised Melanoma Specimens.
abstract: Precise intraoperative delineation of melanoma margins remains a clinical challenge; incomplete resection causes recurrence, whereas over-excision compromises aesthetic and functional outcomes. While surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) provides chemically rich vibrational fingerprints, accurate intraoperative quantification is hindered by complex, coupled full-spectrum responses. Herein, we report a chemistry-informed artificial intelligence (AI)-SERS platform designed to support melanoma margin assessment via the detection of tumor-associated metabolic acidification. A pH-responsive HemS-SERS microarray was developed to translate the phenolic protonation/deprotonation of a hemicyanine-xanthene reporter into coordinated intensity redistributions across multiple Raman bands. Guided by this acid-base chemistry, our AI model (CIMPA-pH) encodes these pH-responsive vibrational anchors as learnable directional chemical priors, integrating full-spectrum attention with Henderson-Hasselbalch-guided prediction. This global decoding strategy accurately captures coupled pH responses, reducing prediction errors by approximately 85% and 54-78% compared to manual peak-ratio features and conventional deep-learning baselines, respectively, while a quality-control risk metric further reduces high-error readouts by 29.1%. Providing rapid (10 s) pointwise pH measurements, the platform distinguishes melanomas from normal skin with distinct pigmentation phenotypes in animal models and shows preliminary applicability for assessing melanoma-associated regions, including grossly atypical areas, in human resection specimens. Ultimately, this chemical-prior-guided SERS decoding strategy provides an interpretable framework with potential for metabolism-guided intraoperative margin assessment.

title: Optical Fiber Needle Probes for In Situ-Distributed Biosensing Based on Optical Frequency Domain Reflectometry.
abstract: In situ detection is crucial for diagnosing lesions during surgery, endoscopy, or biopsy but has always been a challenge in medical diagnostics. Optical fiber biosensing needle probes, with their small size, can be nearly noninvasively guided to the lesion site for in situ detection. However, existing optical fiber biosensing probes are single-point sensors, unable to precisely locate lesions. We propose an optical fiber needle probe for in situ distributed sensing of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) biomarker GPC3 in soft matter based on optical frequency domain reflectometry (OFDR). The needle type probe is fabricated by integrating a polydopamine (PDA)-assisted anti-GPC3 antibody-functionalized micro/nano fiber into a metal needle with a lateral opening near the distal tip. Through differential-phase demodulation, calibration experiments with varying GPC3 concentrations reveal that the needle probe exhibits an 8 mm sensing length with a sensitivity of 0.0031 rad/(ng/mL). More importantly, the proposed needle probe achieves the precise spatial localization of both independent and simultaneous multiple 250-μm mimic lesions loaded by GPC3 in an agarose-glycerol hydrogel soft matter phantom with a spatial resolution of 25 μm and a limit of detection (LOD) of 3.23 ng/mL, which offers unparalleled advantages compared with existing biosensors. The proposed method provides a potential for in situ detection and localization of HCC or other lesions.

title: Retrieval-induced forgetting and facilitation across the Alzheimer's disease continuum: Behavioral and neuroanatomical evidence from a recognition-based paradigm.
abstract: Objective The aim of the present study was to investigate facilitation (FAC) and retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF) during episodic memory retrieval across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum and to examine their gray matter correlates in verbal and visual recognition tasks. Method One hundred participants (28 AD, 29 amnestic mild cognitive impairment, 23 subjective cognitive decline [SCD], 20 healthy subjects) completed a modified retrieval-practice paradigm (mRPP) involving verbal and visual recognition tasks, a comprehensive neuropsychological battery, and 3T magnetic resonance imaging. FAC and RIF were computed at the group level and via individual proxy scores, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess the association between mRPP indices and regional gray matter volumes. Results The verbal mRPP showed reduced overall recognition in AD compared with healthy subjects ( p = .003 - η p ² = 0.23). A robust FAC effect in AD, amnestic mild cognitive impairment, and SCD was observed, whereas RIF emerged only in SCD, suggesting intact inhibitory control at the earliest stage and its disruption with disease progression ( p < .001 - η p ² = 0.48). The visual mRPP showed a strong FAC effect across all groups, with no RIF, indicating modality-specific reliance on recognition-based retrieval ( p < .001 - η p ² = 0.63). Voxel-based morphometry analyses revealed distinct gray matter correlates across groups and tasks: Verbal RIF was negatively associated with frontotemporal regions in AD patients and parieto-occipital regions in healthy subjects, while visual indices showed widespread associations with temporal, subcortical, cerebellar, and sensorimotor regions, particularly in amnestic mild cognitive impairment and SCD groups. Conclusions This study shows shared and modality-specific brain mechanisms of retrieval practice across AD stages. Preserved compensatory processes in SCD individuals give way to progressive regional disruption, supporting early, modality-tailored, and multimodal cognitive interventions to enhance cognition and delay cognitive decline. One hundred participants (28 AD, 29 amnestic mild cognitive impairment, 23 subjective cognitive decline [SCD], 20 healthy subjects) completed a modified retrieval-practice paradigm (mRPP) involving verbal and visual recognition tasks, a comprehensive neuropsychological battery, and 3T magnetic resonance imaging. FAC and RIF were computed at the group level and via individual proxy scores, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess the association between mRPP indices and regional gray matter volumes.

Results

The verbal mRPP showed reduced overall recognition in AD compared with healthy subjects (p = .003 - ηp² = 0.23). A robust FAC effect in AD, amnestic mild cognitive impairment, and SCD was observed, whereas RIF emerged only in SCD, suggesting intact inhibitory control at the earliest stage and its disruption with disease progression (p < .001 - ηp² = 0.48). title: PET imaging enables direct evaluation of ferroptosis in HCC synergistically induced by anti-PD-L1 and Olaparib.
abstract: The efficacy of PET image-guided immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) management is limited by the lack of direct monitoring of therapeutic response. A key challenge is the mismatch between the therapeutic pathway and the imaging target, which hinders the accurate assessment of treatment outcomes. We addressed this challenge by combining anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy with Olaparib, a strategy that promotes ferroptosis in BRCA wild-type HCC by suppressing SLC7A11, thus allowing for therapeutic response evaluation via [ 18 F]FASu PET imaging of SLC7A11 expression. The combination treatment resulted in a 57% reduction in tumor volume, accompanied by decreased Ki-67 expression and increased levels of γ-H2AX and 8-OHdG. [ 18 F]FASu PET imaging revealed significantly lower SUVmax and tumor-to-background ratios in the combination group, correlating with SLC7A11 downregulation. Mechanistically, GPX4 downregulation, glutathione (GSH) depletion and elevated malondialdehyde (MDA) levels confirmed the activation of ferroptosis. Notably, no therapeutic or imaging response was observed in immunodeficient models. Thus, the SLC7A11-targeted PET tracer [ 18 F]FASu offers a clinically translatable biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy, establishing a novel theragnostic paradigm that directly evaluates treatment response via PET imaging.

title: Applications of lung ultrasound in preterm infants: implications for respiratory distress syndrome and bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
abstract: Lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a promising bedside imaging modality in neonatal intensive care units, offering real-time assessment of lung aeration without exposure to ionizing radiation. These advantages are particularly relevant for preterm infants, who are vulnerable to cumulative radiation exposure and evolving pulmonary disease. In this narrative review, we synthesize current evidence on the functional clinical applications of lung ultrasound in preterm infants. We focus on how LUS has been studied to guide early respiratory management, predict the need for surfactant and escalation of respiratory support, assess extubation readiness, identify infants at increased risk for bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and monitor disease trajectory and response to therapy throughout the NICU course, including emerging data on longer-term respiratory outcomes. While available studies demonstrate promising diagnostic and prognostic value, interpretation is limited by heterogeneity in acquisition protocols, scoring systems, timing of assessment, and operator dependence. Further multicenter studies with standardized protocols are needed to define the role of LUS in routine neonatal respiratory care.

title: Artificial intelligence and digital technologies transforming neonatal respiratory assessment: a scoping review.
abstract: Digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) have been increasingly incorporated into neonatal care, particularly in respiratory assessment. However, structured evidence regarding their clinical applications, performance, and limitations remains limited. This scoping review analyzed 35 studies published between 2019 and 2026 to map the use of digital technologies and AI in neonatal respiratory assessment. The findings showed that these approaches are mainly applied to predictive models, medical image analysis, and continuous physiological monitoring. Overall, the studies demonstrated potential for early diagnosis, prediction of respiratory outcomes, and clinical decision support. Nevertheless, the available evidence remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, lack of robust external validation, small sample sizes, and absence of protocol standardization. These findings suggest that, although promising, AI-based technologies are not yet ready for widespread clinical implementation, requiring prospective, multicenter, and standardized studies to validate their effectiveness and safety in neonatal care. IMPACT: This review synthesizes the use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence in neonatal respiratory assessment, highlighting their expanding role in neonatal respiratory research and clinical decision support. AI-based predictive models demonstrate potential for early identification of critical respiratory outcomes, including bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the need for mechanical ventilation. Imaging-based approaches, such as chest radiography and lung ultrasound combined with deep learning, may improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce interobserver variability. Digital monitoring technologies enable continuous, noninvasive, and real-time assessment of neonatal respiratory parameters. The lack of external validation, methodological standardization, and evidence of clinical impact limits their application, reinforcing the need for multicenter studies and structured integration of these technologies into clinical workflows.

title: Differentiated skeletal myotubes coupled with bimodal biosensing for dynamic functional evaluation of inflammatory myotube dysfunction.
abstract: Inflammatory skeletal muscle atrophy is a growing clinical challenge, driven by chronic inflammatory conditions and life-threatening illnesses that cause progressive muscle loss. This condition leads to premature muscle fatigue and a decline in muscle function, highlighting the necessity for highly sensitive diagnostic methods to detect impairment prior to the occurrence of structural damage. Conventional diagnostic methods, including electromyography, serum biomarker assays, and medical imaging, often fail to detect early and subtle alterations in myotube electrophysiological responsiveness because of limited temporal accuracy and insufficient target specificity. Furthermore, these techniques are limited in resolving dynamic electrophysiological fluctuations as well as characterizing the coupling between electrical signaling and intracellular calcium dynamics. Herein, we have developed an integrated bimodal biosensing platform that combines microelectrode array (MEA)-based electrophysiological recording with high-resolution, fluorescence-based calcium imaging. This platform performs coordinated and real-time tracking of extracellular field potentials and intracellular calcium transients across networks of differentiated C2C12 myotubes. Using an in vitro model of LPS-induced inflammatory skeletal muscle atrophy, LPS exposure progressively disrupted spontaneous electrical firing, field potential amplitude, and intracellular calcium transients in a concentration- and time-dependent manner. Diclofenac, a clinically applied anti-inflammatory agent, effectively maintained both electrophysiological function and calcium homeostasis in myotubes under inflammatory stress. Therefore, our bimodal platform functions as a robust, real-time preclinical tool for the detection of incipient inflammatory myopathy. Its integrated capabilities enable the precise quantification of drug responses and the scalable screening of therapeutic candidates, thereby establishing a versatile, translationally-oriented platform for the investigation of skeletal muscle atrophy mechanisms and interventions.

title: Shared cortical morphometry and molecular signatures across depression and physical diseases.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is highly comorbid with physical diseases, suggesting shared neurobiological mechanisms. However, the common structural and molecular substrates underlying this comorbidity remain poorly understood. We analyzed multimodal MRI data from 577 patients (MDD, asthma, fibromyalgia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, type 2 diabetes) and 275 healthy controls, constructed individual morphometric similarity networks (MSN) to identify shared cortical alterations, and applied principal component analysis with multiscale molecular annotation (transcriptomic, cell-type, neurotransmitter, and cognitive mapping) to characterize underlying mechanisms. All patient groups exhibited regional MSN abnormalities. A shared MSN pattern emerged, featuring increased similarity in visual and somatomotor regions and decreased similarity in ventral attention, limbic, and default mode networks, and was replicated in independent cohorts. This pattern was significantly associated with spatial gene expression enriched for synaptic signaling, membrane potential regulation, and neuronal architecture, with predominant expression in excitatory/inhibitory neurons and astrocytes. It further mapped onto specific neurotransmitter systems, with exploratory cognitive decoding suggesting possible relevance to emotion and social cognition. Related genes overlapped with known risk loci for Alzheimer's disease and bipolar disorder. These findings identify a robust across diseases cortical MSN phenotype linked to convergent molecular and neurochemical correlates, offering a framework for studying shared vulnerability and transdiagnostic mechanisms across depression and physical diseases.

title: Prenatal exposure to hypertensive disorders and adolescent brain white matter development.
abstract: Background Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are associated with altered in utero neurodevelopment, yet long-term impact on adolescent white matter architecture remains unclear, particularly by HDP subtype and sex. While preeclampsia/eclampsia (P/E) is clinically more severe, pregnancy-related hypertension (PR-HTN) may involve longer in-utero exposure to hemodynamic stress. This study examined how distinct HDP exposures influence longitudinal white matter measures in adolescents. Methods Using a longitudinal cohort with two MRI timepoints (baseline ages 9-11 years; 2-year follow-up ages 11-13.8 years), we modeled fiber volume (FV) and fractional anisotropy (FA) using linear mixed-effects models. Analyses were sex-stratified and adjusted for prenatal exposures, maternal age, race/ethnicity, and income. False discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied. Results In female adolescents, PR-HTN was significantly associated with lower FV across bilateral association, projection, and limbic pathways, alongside reduced FV and FA in the corpus callosum and forceps major/minor (q < 0.05). Conversely, P/E exposure showed no FDR-significant associations. No significant associations were observed in males for either HDP subtype. Conclusion Chronic in-utero exposure to PR-HTN, rather than acute P/E, is associated with widespread reductions in white matter structural integrity in females. These findings support subtype-specific and developmentally sensitive associations between HDP exposure and offspring brain development. Impact This study demonstrates that pregnancy-related hypertension, a traditionally "milder" disorder, has more pronounced long-term impacts on adolescent white matter scaffolding than preeclampsia/eclampsia. The results highlight a female-specific vulnerability to chronic prenatal hypertensive stress, manifesting as reduced volumetric and microstructural integrity in critical commissural and association white matter tracts. These findings shift the clinical focus toward the neurodevelopmental risks of chronic gestational hypertension, suggesting that maternal cardiovascular health throughout the entire pregnancy is a vital determinant of offspring brain development.

title: Cardiometabolic health's influence on the efficacy of pre-operative hormone therapy for men with localized high-risk prostate cancer.
abstract: Background Altered lipid metabolism, adiposity, and androgens have been linked to cardiac disease and prostate cancer. Adiposity increases risk of recurrence for prostate cancer and may enhance response to androgen receptor pathway inhibition (ARPI). We evaluated whether adiposity and circulating lipid metabolites are associated with response to pre-operative ADT + /- ARPI in localized high-risk prostate cancer (HRPCa). Methods We performed a post hoc analysis of 104 men with localized HRPCa treated with 3-6 months of preoperative ADT + /- ARPI across three trials. Body composition was quantified from L3 CT imaging at baseline and at radical prostatectomy (RP; end-of-treatment [EOT] n = 56). Plasma lipid metabolites were profiled by UPLC-MS at baseline (n = 60) and in paired baseline/EOT samples (n = 59). Pathologic response was defined as ≤ T2N0 at RP. PSA progression-free survival (PFS) was defined as time from RP to PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL or initiation of radiotherapy. Results Median age was 63 years, 76.9% had Gleason grade group 4-5, and 43.7% had clinical T3-4 disease. At RP, lower visceral (VATi, p = 0.002) and subcutaneous adiposity (SATi, p = 0.004) were associated with pathologic response. Increasing adiposity at RP was associated with PSA progression (per 10-unit increase: VATi HR 1.09, p = 0.04; SATi HR 1.14, p = 0.03). In paired analyses (n = 59), pathologic responders demonstrated decreases (p < 0.05) in diacylglycerols and polyunsaturated fatty acyl chain-containing triacylglycerols (PUFA-TAGs) and elevations in ceramide species. Non-responders exhibited increases (p < 0.05) in PUFA-TAGs and glycerophospholipids with reductions in lysophosphatidylcholine species, long-chain acylcarnitine, and cholesterol. Conclusions Higher post-treatment adiposity and intrapatient changes in lipid metabolite pathways were associated with inferior outcomes after pre-operative hormone therapy, supporting a stage-dependent link between cardiometabolic health and prostate cancer that warrants further elucidation.

title: Pulmonary nodules: classification, biomarkers, signaling pathways, diseases, early diagnosis and management.
abstract: Pulmonary nodules are increasingly detected by thoracic imaging and low-dose computed tomography-based lung cancer screening, but most are benign, transient, or indolent. Clinically, the key task is to distinguish nodules that require timely cancer-directed evaluation from those that can be safely observed. This review summarizes the classification, disease spectrum, risk assessment, early diagnosis, biomarkers, signaling mechanisms, translational models, and management of pulmonary nodules. We first distinguish imaging phenotypes and disease entities, then differentiate the individual-level models used to select candidates for lung cancer screening from the nodule-level models and structured reporting systems used after nodule detection. Low-dose computed tomography remains the foundation of screening and surveillance approaches, whereas magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography, nonsurgical biopsy, surgical diagnosis, and local therapies play more selective roles depending on the probability of malignancy and patient fitness. Noninvasive biomarkers, including circulating cellular, nucleic acid, methylation, protein, autoantibody, extracellular vesicle, and metabolic analytes, are most likely to serve as adjuncts to imaging and clinical risk assessment rather than as stand-alone diagnostic tests. Artificial intelligence may support detection, workflow efficiency, malignancy risk reclassification, invasiveness assessment, and multimodal integration, but its value depends on external validation, calibration, implementation, and prospective evidence of management benefit. Mechanistic studies of adenocarcinoma spectrum subsolid nodules have implicated the involvement of early oncogenic signaling, genomic instability, immune escape, stromal and vascular remodeling, and adaptive survival pathways. Translational models can support mechanistic and procedural research, but do not replicate real-world nodule management in patients. Overall, care for pulmonary nodules should be risk-adapted, longitudinal, multidisciplinary, and patient-centered.

title: Surgery to treat autonomic dysreflexia due to cubital tunnel syndrome in cervical spinal cord injury: a case report.
abstract: Introduction Autonomic dysreflexia (AD) is a potentially fatal syndrome in people with spinal cord injury (SCI) marked by episodic hypertension with flushing, diaphoresis, and bradycardia. Common etiologies include bladder distension and bowel impaction. Compressive neuropathies lack attention as a potential precipitant of AD. This report describes an individual with cervical SCI and with recurrent AD treated with ulnar nerve decompression surgery. Case presentation A 74-year-old woman with a remote history of C6 SCI (American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale Grade B) presented to clinic with recurrent episodes of AD that had been refractory to standard treatment measures. History and clinical examination were suggestive of ulnar nerve compressive neuropathy at the elbow - cubital tunnel syndrome. The diagnosis was confirmed with electrodiagnostic studies and neuromuscular ultrasound. Treatment with surgery successfully resolved her episodes of AD. Discussion This case identifies compressive neuropathy as a treatable cause of AD in individuals with cervical SCI. When more common etiologies of AD are excluded, clinicians should consider compressive peripheral neuropathies as potential causes of AD. Surgical decompression may alleviate symptoms of AD in select cases. Further research should investigate the prevalence and optimal management of compressive neuropathy in people with SCI.

Introduction

Autonomic dysreflexia (AD) is a potentially fatal syndrome in people with spinal cord injury (SCI) marked by episodic hypertension with flushing, diaphoresis, and bradycardia. Common etiologies include bladder distension and bowel impaction. Compressive neuropathies lack attention as a potential precipitant of AD. This report describes an individual with cervical SCI and with recurrent AD treated with ulnar nerve decompression surgery.

Case presentation

A 74-year-old woman with a remote history of C6 SCI (American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale Grade B) presented to clinic with recurrent episodes of AD that had been refractory to standard treatment measures. History and clinical examination were suggestive of ulnar nerve compressive neuropathy at the elbow - cubital tunnel syndrome. The diagnosis was confirmed with electrodiagnostic studies and neuromuscular ultrasound. Treatment with surgery successfully resolved her episodes of AD.

Discussion

This case identifies compressive neuropathy as a treatable cause of AD in individuals with cervical SCI. When more common etiologies of AD are excluded, clinicians should consider compressive peripheral neuropathies as potential causes of AD. Surgical decompression may alleviate symptoms of AD in select cases. Further research should investigate the prevalence and optimal management of compressive neuropathy in people with SCI.

title: MD2-IN-1 restores microglial lysosomal function and attenuates amyloid pathology through TREM2-associated signaling in 5×FAD mice.
abstract: Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) is a central regulator of microglial adaptation during Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the development of small-molecule modulators associated with TREM2 signaling remains limited. Here, through a consensus pharmacophore-guided virtual screening strategy, MD2-IN-1 was identified as a candidate small molecule associated with TREM2 signaling. Biolayer interferometry and cellular thermal shift assays supported cellular target engagement related to TREM2 (K D = 13.85 μM). In Aβ-stimulated BV2 microglia, MD2-IN-1 increased SYK phosphorylation, promoted Aβ uptake, and shifted microglial responses toward a less proinflammatory phenotype. These effects were markedly attenuated following Trem2 knockdown, indicating the involvement of the TREM2-SYK signaling pathway. Mechanistically, MD2-IN-1 restored lysosomal acidification and increased the expression of the V-ATPase subunits ATP6v0c and ATP6v0a1, accompanied by increased intracellular Aβ degradation. In 5×FAD mice, chronic MD2-IN-1 administration improved cognitive performance without detectable behavioral abnormalities compared with WT animals. Multimodal PET imaging demonstrated reduced amyloid deposition and attenuated neuroinflammatory signals, which were further supported by histological analyses showing decreased plaque burden, reduced inflammatory microglial responses, and preserved neuronal integrity. In addition, MD2-IN-1 reduced P62 accumulation and restored ATP6v0c expression in vivo, whereas these effects were partially attenuated by pharmacological inhibition of TREM2. Collectively, these findings identify MD2-IN-1 as a small-molecule modulator associated with TREM2 signaling that restores microglial lysosomal degradative function and promotes Aβ clearance in AD models, providing pharmacological support for targeting adaptive microglial responses in AD.

title: Dens invaginatus: a review and case series.
abstract: Dens invaginatus is a dental anomaly resulting in an abnormal tooth morphology, most commonly affecting the permanent dentition. An associated infolding of the outer enamel organ results in structural pocketing and increased susceptibility to dental disease. Clinical sequalae of affected teeth may include dental caries, pulpal pathology, devitalisation, discolouration, localised periodontal pocketing or increased tooth mobility. Early diagnosis is therefore essential in the delivery of effective prevention and informed treatment planning. Clinicians should be aware of the diverse clinical and radiographic presentations of dens invaginatus. Treatment principles may range from conservative approaches to multidisciplinary input within tertiary care services for anatomically challenging presentations. We present six clinical cases referred to the paediatric dentistry department at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, demonstrating a range of management approaches.

title: Uterine leiomyomas in HLRCC: a scoping review of presentation, histopathology, treatment patterns, and reproductive implications.
abstract: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC) is a rare cancer predisposition syndrome in which uterine leiomyomas (ULs) are common, morbid, and often precede renal cancer diagnosis. We synthetized evidence on the clinical presentation, pathology, management, and reproductive outcomes of HLRCC-associated ULs. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for peer-reviewed studies reporting original data on ULs in HLRCC. Two reviewers independently screened articles and extracted data. Individual patient data from 410 patients and aggregate data from 27 observational studies were included. Mean age at UL diagnosis was 32.4 years. Most patients (89.1%) had multiple fibroids, were symptomatic (88.1%), and commonly reported abnormal uterine bleeding (80.6%) or pelvic pain (41.2%). Average maximum fibroid size was 7.5 cm. Fumarate hydratase (FH) and/or S-(2-succino)cysteine (2SC) immunohistochemistry studies showed abnormal staining in >85% of tumors. Surgical intervention was required in 94.4% of patients; hysterectomy was most common (67.0%), at a mean age of 35.2 years, whereas myomectomy was performed in 27% at 27.7 years. Despite a family history of HLRCC-related features in 88.8% of patients, only 0.6% underwent germline FH testing before gynecologic diagnosis. Fertility and obstetric outcomes were sparsely reported. Uterine leiomyosarcoma was rare, with an uncertain syndromic association. HLRCC-associated ULs are genetically, morphologically, and clinically distinct from sporadic fibroids, yet remain under-recognized. Integrating age, multiplicity, symptoms, family history, and pathology-triggered FH/2SC immunohistochemistry into gynecologic practice would enable earlier germline testing, renal surveillance, and reproductive counseling. Prospective registries are needed to define genotype-phenotype relationships, fertility outcomes, and leiomyosarcoma risk.

title: Deep learning-based prediction of one-year functional and structural outcomes in treatment-naïve DMO after anti-VEGF therapy.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether baseline structural optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans contain prognostic information that can be used by deep learning models to predict one-year functional and anatomical outcomes in treatment-naïve diabetic macular oedema (DMO). Design Retrospective cohort study. Participants Eighty-seven eyes (74 patients) with treatment-naïve DMO receiving intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy. Methods Baseline OCT volumes were analysed using a deep learning regression model. The images were homogenised - preprocessed and transformed into a common reference frame - to streamline the learning task. The model predicted 12-month changes in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central subfield thickness (CST). Main outcome measures Performance was assessed using 5-fold cross-validation and compared between original and preprocessed datasets. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated classification of responders versus non-responders, while occlusion sensitivity analysis identified image regions contributing most to predictions. Results Mean BCVA improved from 0.40 ± 0.40 to 0.33 ± 0.30 logMAR, and CST decreased from 390.2 ± 77.1 µm to 342.2 ± 76.3 µm (both p < 0.001). Prediction of BCVA change achieved an R² of 0.575, improving to 0.661 after preprocessing. CST prediction improved from R² = 0.447-0.633. Classification performance increased from AUC 0.65 to 0.71 for BCVA response and from 0.93 to 0.97 for CST response. Key predictive regions included the outer retina and retinal pigment epithelium. Conclusions Deep learning analysis of baseline OCT can predict one-year outcomes in DMO. Image homogenisation enhances performance, and responder identification suggests the potential utility of this approach for prognostic assessment and risk stratification, warranting further validation before clinical implementation.

To evaluate whether baseline structural optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans contain prognostic information that can be used by deep learning models to predict one-year functional and anatomical outcomes in treatment-naïve diabetic macular oedema (DMO).

Design

Retrospective cohort study.

Participants

Eighty-seven eyes (74 patients) with treatment-naïve DMO receiving intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy.

Methods

Baseline OCT volumes were analysed using a deep learning regression model. The images were homogenised - preprocessed and transformed into a common reference frame - to streamline the learning task. The model predicted 12-month changes in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central subfield thickness (CST).

Main outcome measures

Performance was assessed using 5-fold cross-validation and compared between original and preprocessed datasets. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated classification of responders versus non-responders, while occlusion sensitivity analysis identified image regions contributing most to predictions.

Results

Mean BCVA improved from 0.40 ± 0.40 to 0.33 ± 0.30 logMAR, and CST decreased from 390.2 ± 77.1 µm to 342.2 ± 76.3 µm (both p < 0.001). Classification performance increased from AUC 0.65 to 0.71 for BCVA response and from 0.93 to 0.97 for CST response. Key predictive regions included the outer retina and retinal pigment epithelium.

title: Restorative and regenerative therapies for vision loss.
abstract: Reversing blindness and restoring functional vision remains a central challenge in biomedical engineering. Advances in ocular prosthetics have enabled limited recovery of light perception, motion detection, and coarse object recognition through anterior segment devices such as keratoprostheses and through posterior segment interfaces including retinal, suprachoroidal, optic nerve, and cortical implants. Parallel progress in organ-on-a-chip systems and retinal organoids is providing increasingly sophisticated platforms for disease modelling and therapeutic development. Despite these advances, issues of long-term biocompatibility, signal fidelity, and surgical complexity continue to constrain clinical performance. Emerging approaches that combine stem cell-derived tissues, biofabrication, and hybrid bioelectronic constructs offer promising avenues for next-generation vision restoration, although current production remains limited to early-stage or small-scale systems. Effective integration of these technologies also requires structured vision-rehabilitation strategies to harness neuroplasticity and support functional adaptation. This review synthesises recent progress across prosthetic, rehabilitative, and regenerative domains and outlines key opportunities for future translational development.

title: Ultrasound renal denervation for treatment-resistant hypertension with severe left ventricular hypertrophy.
abstract: Resistant hypertension with left ventricular hypertrophy requires aggressive treatment to reduce cardiovascular risk. Ultrasound renal denervation safely attenuates sympathetic activity and lowers blood pressure. We performed step-by-step image-guided renal denervation, demonstrating procedural feasibility, safety, and early blood pressure reduction with potential benefits for left ventricular remodeling.

title: Integrated morphological and transcriptomic analysis of bone disorders in aldosterone-salt hypertension.
abstract: Although excessive dietary sodium intake is a well-recognized risk factor for hypertension, accumulating evidence indicates that it leads to broader metabolic consequences. Here, we investigated the renal and skeletal consequences of high salt loading and the protective effects of esaxerenone, a selective nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) antagonist. Male Sprague-Dawley rats were infused with aldosterone and fed an 8% sodium chloride diet for 4 weeks (Aldo-HS), with or without esaxerenone. Trabecular bone architecture was assessed by micro-computed tomography, three-dimensional morphometry, and histomorphometry. Kidney and bone transcriptomes were analyzed using RNA sequencing and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Aldo-HS rats developed marked renal calcium wasting without changes in serum calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone, or fibroblast growth factor 23 levels. Fractional calcium excretion was strongly inversely correlated with trabecular bone volume (r = -0.74, p < 0.001). Aldosterone-salt loading induced substantial trabecular bone loss, which was prevented by esaxerenone. title: A soft bioelectronic system with a responsive hydrogel neural interface for direct force quantification and real-time intraoperative craniocerebral injury monitoring.
abstract: In craniotomies, the surgical manipulation of instruments inherently involves applying mechanical forces to brain tissues, potentially causing brain damage. Currently, there is no direct method to quantitatively monitor craniocerebral injuries. Here we report a soft neural interface bioelectronic system (SNIBS) for real-time monitoring of craniocerebral injury throughout neurosurgery. On the basis of the thermally triggered swelling/deswelling of hydrogel microspheres, the hydrogel interface achieves seamless integration with the brain cortex for recording high-fidelity signals during surgery while ensuring benign detachment to prevent brain damage after surgery. The SNIBS enables the monitoring of contact pressure, somatosensory evoked potentials, electrocorticography and temperature, providing a direct method of assessing neural status. The correlation between somatosensory evoked potential and cortical neural pathway damage caused by pressure is revealed by SNIBS. Evans blue staining and magnetic resonance imaging confirm that contact pressure higher than 80 kPa causes irreversible craniocerebral injury. Validated in rabbit brain tumour excision models, the SNIBS enables surgeons to quantify forces to avoid craniocerebral injury. The presented technology holds strong potential for establishing safety evaluation standards for neurosurgery.

title: The β-cells in type 1 diabetes mellitus: findings from human pancreas studies.
abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by long-term and dynamic interactions between the immune system and pancreatic β-cells, ultimately leading to severe insulin deficiency. A paradigm shift in T1DM research has occurred in the past few years, with research now focusing on the human disease because of access to human pancreatic tissue and pancreas-draining lymph nodes. Advances in high-resolution imaging, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and histopathology based on artificial intelligence have profoundly reshaped our understanding of disease initiation and progression. These studies revealed that β-cell loss and/or dysfunction might begin earlier than previously appreciated, preferentially affecting small β-cell-rich islets and insulin-positive cell clusters, with larger islets showing transient resistance. Substantial β-cell mass often persists at diagnosis, accompanied by functional impairment rather than immediate cell death. Across disease stages, β-cells exhibit conserved molecular signatures dominated by interferon signalling, enhanced antigen presentation and adaptive immune-evasion programmes, with evidence of heterogeneity linked to age, disease duration and immune context. Parallel analyses of pancreatic lymph nodes show early immune dysregulation, including altered regulatory T cell signatures and expansion of stem-like cytotoxic T cell populations, even before overt hyperglycaemia. Together, these findings support an integrated model of T1DM progression that enables alignment of clinical staging with evolving β-cell and immune phenotypes.

title: Single-component imaging and ultrasound-based tools for the assessment of fracture risk.
abstract: Emerging imaging and computational technologies are reshaping how osteoporosis and low bone mass are assessed. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is key for the operational definition of osteoporosis, but advances in single-component tools such as finite element analysis, trabecular bone score, DXA-based 3D shape modelling, quantitative ultrasound, radiofrequency echographic multi-spectrometry and artificial-intelligence-driven interpretation of routine radiology offer complementary insights into bone strength, microarchitecture and fracture risk. Some of these approaches provide additional fracture-risk measures beyond areal bone mineral density, whereas others enable opportunistic identification of people with low bone density in populations who would otherwise be missed. Strong pre-clinical and encouraging observational data support the use of these technologies and, although their current use in clinical practice varies with the age of the technology, they all have a potential role in the assessment of fracture risk at a variety of points in the patient journey (from screening to monitoring response to therapy). As their use becomes more widespread, monitoring performance, assessing the equitability of implementation and evaluating the health-service benefits of these tools in clinical practice will be key.

title: Rare prostate cancer histologies: detection, characteristics and treatment.
abstract: Relatively rare histologies of prostate cancer collectively account for <5% of all prostate cancers and comprise mucinous adenocarcinoma, intraductal carcinoma, ductal adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine prostate cancer (including treatment-emergent small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma), sarcomatoid carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma. These histologies have distinct morphological, molecular and clinical features from each other and the most common histological type, acinar adenocarcinoma. The perceived rarity of these histologies often reflects sampling limitations rather than biological prevalence, as many treatment-emergent phenotypes are seldom encountered in routine practice owing to the infrequent use of metastatic biopsies. These histologies demonstrate aggressive behaviour, atypical metastatic patterns and reduced responsiveness to conventional therapies. Despite their clinical importance, these entities remain under-represented in standard guidelines and clinical trials. Histological types and subtypes, such as ductal, mucinous, intraductal, neuroendocrine and sarcomatoid carcinomas, pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, and conventional screening with PSA exhibits limitations, so they are often diagnosed at advanced stages. Multiparametric MRI, immunohistochemistry and genomic profiling are crucial tools for accurate recognition and risk stratification. Histological type-specific genomic alterations, including DNA repair deficiencies, RB1 and TP53 loss, and mismatch repair mutations, provide potential therapeutic opportunities, but treatment recommendations are still largely extrapolated from acinar adenocarcinoma. Limited retrospective data suggest worse outcomes for patients with a rare histology than those with typical acinar adenocarcinoma, highlighting the urgent need for prospective registries and dedicated clinical trials. Rare histologies of prostate cancer are an under-recognized source of morbidity and mortality. Improved diagnostic precision, incorporation of molecular profiling and collaborative data collection efforts are essential to develop evidence-based strategies.

title: A preinvasive regulatory T cell axis for lung cancer interception.
abstract: Late-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is rarely curable 1 , underscoring a need to intervene earlier in the disease process. Growing evidence suggests that antitumour T cell responses are mounted but become progressively dysregulated during early tumorigenesis 2,3 . Tracking and targeting preinvasive T cell regulation may inform new approaches to detect and intercept lung cancer development. Here we explore how the T cell network is remodelled during NSCLC development via multi-omic, cross-tissue immune profiling in patients with preinvasive lung lesions surveilled by autofluorescence bronchoscopy and computed tomography (CT) imaging. Effector regulatory CD4 + T cells (eT reg cells) expressing basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) accumulated in high-grade premalignant airway lesions and were clonally related to circulating eT reg cells. Circulating eT reg cells were increasingly elevated during preinvasive progression, enabling lung tumorigenesis to be tracked through analysis of peripheral blood. Emergence of this clonally coordinated eT reg cell circuit defined rapid progression in patients with early-stage NSCLC detected during CT screening. In mice, carcinogen-driven lung tumorigenesis triggered an analogous preinvasive eT reg cell axis across the blood, airways and draining lymph nodes (dLNs). This culminated in an expansion of lung BATF + T reg cells and T reg cell-rich peribronchial immature tertiary lymphoid structures (iTLSs). Immune interception via phosphoinositide 3-kinase-δ (PI3Kδ) inhibition abrogated formation of T reg cell-rich iTLSs, reduced circulating and pulmonary T reg cells, increased local conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s) and reduced lung tumour incidence and size. These data reveal a conserved eT reg cell network that emerges across tissues during early pulmonary tumorigenesis and provide a theranostic framework to track and target preinvasive immune regulation for lung cancer interception.

title: Multimodal precision diagnostics in clinical xenotransplantation.
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in pig-to-human xenotransplantation have successfully prevented hyperacute rejection of kidney, heart, liver and lung xenografts, marking a milestone long considered a critical barrier. However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date. Detection and management of these injuries remain a critical bottleneck, as conventional histopathology and standard clinical monitoring lack the sensitivity required to identify subclinical injury early enough to guide timely intervention. This diagnostic gap underscores an urgent need for the development of advanced, multimodal precision diagnostic frameworks to enhance immune surveillance, which will be essential for standardizing clinical protocols and enabling pathogenesis-driven therapeutic intervention. This approach will inform both immunosuppressive regimens and future gene editing strategies aimed at engineering rejection-resistant porcine organs, ultimately prolonging graft survival. Broad adoption of such an integrative strategy will be essential to transition xenotransplantation from an experimental intervention into a safe, scalable and patient-centred clinical therapy. In this Review, we synthesize recent progress in xenotransplantation and position multimodal precision diagnostics as a pivotal strategy to address the remaining immunological and clinical barriers to widespread clinical implementation.

title: An open vision-language model for diverse medical applications.
abstract: Artificial intelligence has high potential for impact in healthcare applications, but its training and deployment are challenging due to diverse data, a complex spectrum of possible tasks and important privacy needs. High-performing foundation models that enable data-efficient fine-tuning for diverse downstream tasks can meaningfully accelerate development in this domain. We introduce MedGemma, a collection of medical vision-language foundation models based on Gemma 3. MedGemma demonstrates advanced medical understanding and reasoning across images and text and multiple medical imaging domains, exceeding the performance of similarly sized generative models while maintaining the general capabilities of the Gemma base models. For out-of-distribution tasks, MedGemma achieves improvements of 2.6-10% in medical image question answering, 15.5-18.1% in chest X-ray finding classification and 10.8% in agentic evaluations compared with the base models. Our results show that fine-tuning MedGemma can be more effective than fine-tuning the base Gemma 3 model for medical tasks, particularly in the setting of limited training data. We additionally introduce MedSigLIP, a medically tuned vision encoder derived from SigLIP. MedSigLIP powers the visual understanding capabilities of MedGemma and, as an encoder, achieves performance comparable to or better than that of many specialized medical image encoders. Taken together, the MedGemma collection provides a strong foundation of medical image and text capabilities, with the potential to accelerate medical research and the development of downstream applications.

Taken together, the MedGemma collection provides a strong foundation of medical image and text capabilities, with the potential to accelerate medical research and the development of downstream applications.

title: AEGIS: an operational infrastructure for post-market governance of adaptive medical AI under US and EU regulatory frameworks.
abstract: Medical AI requires governance preserving safety during continuous improvement. FDA Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) and EU post-market surveillance address iterative updates but lack operational tooling. We present AEGIS, an internal governance and post-market-monitoring infrastructure designed to support the documentation of predetermined governance pathways for PCCP and Medical Devices Regulation alignment. AEGIS comprises dataset assimilation and retraining, model monitoring, and conditional decision-making modules. It utilizes a four-category taxonomy (APPROVE, CONDITIONAL APPROVAL, CLINICAL REVIEW, REJECT) and an independent ALARM signal. Instantiating AEGIS for sepsis prediction (PhysioNet) and brain-tumor segmentation (BraTS) exercised all decision categories, successfully routing failures to the critical REJECT + ALARM state (no deployable model; released model at risk). On real cross-site data, drift detection ROC-AUC rose from 0.82 to 1.00, reliably triggering near 500-patient batches with zero false alarms. This proof-of-concept utilizes illustrative clinical models; drift scoring quantifies covariate shift only, leaving concept drift for future work.

title: Towards reliable morphological subtyping and cancer detection on Barrett's esophagus pathology through ensembling foundation models.
abstract: The reliability of emergent histopathology foundation models (Histo-FMs) for real-world diagnostic tasks remains unproven. Given the complexity of diagnostic tasks and the challenges inherent in real-world data, we utilized Histo-FMs to investigate their utility for morphological subtyping of Barrett's esophagus (BE) and detecting esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) across the BE progression spectrum. We benchmarked Histo-FMs on the BarrettNet cohort, spanning diagnostic categories ranging from normal to EAC (N2EAC). The dataset comprised 3528 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) from 790 patients. A multi-magnification, multi-backbone aggregation of the five most expert-consistent single-scale models yielded incremental performance gains (AUROC of 0.907, F1-score of 0.696, accuracy of 0.795, and κ of 0.651 for morphological subtyping; AUROC of 0.909, F1-score of 0.836, accuracy of 0.959, and κ of 0.673 for EAC detection), with non-uniform gains across single-model comparisons and limited benefit for dysplasia. The findings support the capability of Histo-FMs for BE morphological subtyping and EAC detection in a multicenter clinical cohort, while highlighting persistent challenges in dysplasia assessment and the need for external validation. This study provides a foundation for future clinical validation.

title: Perivascular spaces are associated with T cell trafficking and may have prognostic relevance in brain metastases.
abstract: Background Perivascular structures, in particular, perivascular spaces (PVS) are emerging key immune modulators in the tumor microenvironment. However, their relationship with immune infiltration, vascular remodeling, and clinical outcomes in brain metastases is unclear. Methods In this retrospective two-center study, we analyzed 56 brain metastases. Perivascular spaces were graded on preoperatively T2-weighted MRI in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale. Tumor immune infiltration, vascular features, and immune cell phenotypes were assessed by immunohistochemistry and spectral flow cytometry and correlated with clinical outcome. Results Here we show that high PVS burden in the centrum semiovale region, but not in the basal ganglia, were significantly associated with improved overall survival. High PVS are linked to increased presence of tumor-infiltrating cytotoxic T cells-most of which exhibited an activated/exhausted phenotype, indicated by PD-1- and Fas-positivity-was likewise prognostically favorable. Moreover, these cells showed elevated expression of the migration marker CXCR3, as well as Granzyme B/IFNγ consistent with effector polarization. High PVS were additionally associated with a higher M1/M2-like macrophage ratio, which showed similar prognostic relevance as high vascular density, suggesting enhanced blood supply and immune cell recruitment. Conclusion These findings could establish PVS as a non-invasive imaging marker of anti-tumor immunity and prognosis in patients with brain metastasis, underscoring their potential as biomarkers for immune activity and therapeutic monitoring.

Background

Perivascular structures, in particular, perivascular spaces (PVS) are emerging key immune modulators in the tumor microenvironment. However, their relationship with immune infiltration, vascular remodeling, and clinical outcomes in brain metastases is unclear.

Methods

In this retrospective two-center study, we analyzed 56 brain metastases. Perivascular spaces were graded on preoperatively T2-weighted MRI in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale. Tumor immune infiltration, vascular features, and immune cell phenotypes were assessed by immunohistochemistry and spectral flow cytometry and correlated with clinical outcome.

Results

Here we show that high PVS burden in the centrum semiovale region, but not in the basal ganglia, were significantly associated with improved overall survival. High PVS are linked to increased presence of tumor-infiltrating cytotoxic T cells-most of which exhibited an activated/exhausted phenotype, indicated by PD-1- and Fas-positivity-was likewise prognostically favorable. Moreover, these cells showed elevated expression of the migration marker CXCR3, as well as Granzyme B/IFNγ consistent with effector polarization. High PVS were additionally associated with a higher M1/M2-like macrophage ratio, which showed similar prognostic relevance as high vascular density, suggesting enhanced blood supply and immune cell recruitment.

Conclusion

These findings could establish PVS as a non-invasive imaging marker of anti-tumor immunity and prognosis in patients with brain metastasis, underscoring their potential as biomarkers for immune activity and therapeutic monitoring.

title: Recent advances in spectral CT contrast agents for gastrointestinal tract imaging.
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) represents one of the most widely utilized and clinically effective imaging techniques for gastrointestinal diseases. Specifically, spectral CT, as an advanced evolution of conventional CT, has significantly improved diagnostic accuracy. The creation of high-performance and biocompatible contrast agents is essential for achieving superior visualization of the gastrointestinal tract and facilitating accurate disease identification. Recent studies reveal that small molecule- and nanoparticle-based contrast agents with high atomic number elements demonstrate significant promise in gastrointestinal diagnostics via spectral CT imaging. Therefore, this review systematically discusses the synthesis, characteristics and advantages of small molecule- and nanoparticle-based contrast agents, with emphasis on their utility in gastrointestinal imaging, disease diagnosis, and therapeutic interventions. Furthermore, the limitations and future directions of current contrast agents are also evaluated, offering a foundation for the design of novel gastrointestinal spectral CT contrast agents.
