title: A homologous cell membrane-camouflaged iridium-doped carbon dot nanozyme for multimodal imaging-guided radiosensitization.
abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) is a mainstay of cancer treatment, yet its efficacy is limited by tumor hypoxia, elevated glutathione (GSH) levels, and a lack of tumor-specific radiosensitizers. Herein, we synthesized iridium-doped carbon dots (Ir-CDs) and further camouflaged them with 4T1 cancer cell membranes to construct a biomimetic nanoplatform (Ir-CDs@CM) integrating homologous targeting, multimodal imaging, and nanozyme-mediated properties for enhanced radiosensitization. The synthesized Ir-CDs exhibited a uniform size of ∼2.25 nm and good water dispersibility. After encapsulation with 4T1 cell membranes, Ir-CDs@CM showed an average hydrodynamic diameter of ∼181.9 nm and a zeta potential of -17.0 mV, along with excellent colloidal stability, low cytotoxicity, favorable biocompatibility, and homologous targeting capability. Functionally, Ir-CDs@CM enabled dual-mode fluorescence (FL) and computed tomography (CT) imaging. Moreover, Ir-CDs displayed three nanozyme activities: GSH-depletion activity (47.13% GSH depletion), catalase-like activity (O 2 generation up to 11.9 mg L -1 ), and peroxidase-like activity (a 5.17-fold increase in reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation under X-ray irradiation). This nanozyme-mediated oxygen evolution and ROS generation reduced 4T1 cell viability from 83% to 45.69% under 6 Gy irradiation. In vivo , the nanoplatform achieved excellent tumor accumulation and therapeutic efficacy in subcutaneous tumor-bearing mice, suppressing tumor growth within 14 days. Body weight fluctuations remained below 5% with no hepatorenal toxicity or tissue damage, confirming excellent biosafety. This strategy integrates membrane camouflage with iridium-based nanozyme technology for targeted imaging, microenvironment modulation, and radiosensitization, opening new avenues for integrated tumor therapy and diagnosis.

title: US/ROS-responsive ALN-modified polymer nanoparticles enhance the efficacy of infiltration anesthesia through improved bone targeting and permeation.
abstract: Complex maxillofacial bone anatomy compromises the efficacy of local anesthetics. This study develops an ultrasound (US)/reactive oxygen species (ROS) cascade-responsive polylactic-coglycolic acid (PLGA) nanoparticle system for enhanced dental infiltration anesthesia and perioperative pain management. The nanoparticles, which were surface-modified with alendronate (ALN) via an ROS-cleavable thioketal (TK) linker and coloaded with bupivacaine (BUPI) and perfluorohexane (PFH), enabled enhanced bone targeting and penetration. Under US stimulation, PFH undergoes a liquid-gas phase transition, generating ROS that cleave TK linkers, switching the system from a "bone-targeting" to a "bone-penetration" state. This cascade mechanism facilitates deep tissue penetration of local anesthetics for enhanced anesthesia while enabling a dual-phase release profile: rapid US-triggered BUPI release for intraoperative analgesia and sustained diffusion for postoperative pain management. In rat models of tooth extraction and pulp injury, the system demonstrated superior efficacy over conventional BUPI, significantly increasing drug concentrations in the mandibular bone and improving pain-related outcomes. Biocompatibility was confirmed via histology and serum biomarkers. By overcoming maxillofacial bone barriers and enabling responsive, biphasic drug release, this platform represents a promising strategy to address the limitations of current local anesthetics in dentistry, reducing local anesthesia failure rates and improving perioperative pain control.

title: Responsive accumulation of ultrasmall DNA@WO3-x nanodots for suppressing tumor progression and metastasis via single-nanodot triple-therapeutic effects.
abstract: Effective treatment for malignant tumors continues to represent an urgent unmet clinical need. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) constitutes a therapeutic challenge on account of its aggressive nature and limited response to conventional therapies. Radiotherapy serves as a cornerstone for cervical cancer treatment. Nevertheless, radioresistance frequently gives rise to therapeutic failure in cervical cancer. We developed ultrasmall, pH-responsive DNA@WO 3- x nanodots to enhance the accumulation of nanodots within tumors, thereby improving therapeutic efficacy. The nanodots undergo intelligent self-assembly within the acidic tumor microenvironment, leading to enhanced accumulation and retention. DNA@WO 3- x functions dually as an effective computed tomography (CT) contrast agent for tumor visualization and a potent radiosensitizer. The high- Z element tungsten and remarkable photothermal conversion capability in the NIR-II window enable synergistic radio-photothermal therapy (RT-PTT). In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that the combined treatment via single-nanodot triple-therapeutic effects potently suppresses the growth of tumor cells. Consequently, this synergistic strategy achieved remarkable inhibition of primary tumor growth and suppression of distant metastasis in orthotopic TNBC models, with no significant systemic toxicity observed. Furthermore, in vitro validation experiments verified that the developed nanodots can effectively sensitize cervical cancer cells to radiotherapy, thereby achieving prominent anti-tumor therapeutic effects. This work presents a versatile and integrated theranostic strategy that realizes potent tumor suppression via single-nanodot triple-therapeutic effects, offering a promising approach for the precise and effective treatment of aggressive solid tumors.

title: Nanomedicines for prostate cancer therapy: stimuli-responsive design and disease-specific applications.
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) remains a major malignancy among men and is clinically complicated by biological heterogeneity, treatment resistance and frequent bone metastasis. Current therapeutic strategies, including radical local treatment, androgen deprivation therapy, androgen receptor (AR) pathway inhibitors, chemotherapy and radioligand therapy, have improved disease control, but their efficacy is often limited by systemic toxicity, functional burden and insufficient tumour selectivity. Chemistry-enabled nanomedicines offer a versatile route to improve drug solubility, circulation, tumour accumulation and controlled therapeutic activation. In this review, we summarise recent advances in nanomedicines for PCa therapy with an emphasis on two closely related aspects: stimuli-responsive design and disease-specific applications. First, endogenous stimuli-responsive drug delivery systems are discussed, including platforms activated by acidic pH, hypoxia, redox imbalance and aberrant enzyme activity. Exogenous systems regulated by light, ultrasound and magnetic fields are then reviewed, with attention to how carrier architecture, responsive linkers, surface transformation and externally triggered activation influence payload release and therapeutic output. Second, PCa-specific nanoplatforms are highlighted, focusing on prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-directed delivery, AR axis- and castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC)-oriented intervention, and bone metastasis-adapted design. Nanomedicine-enabled combinations with immunotherapy or radiotherapy are also considered. Finally, we discuss key challenges related to tumour delivery efficiency, structural complexity, manufacturing reproducibility, biosafety and patient stratification. Overall, this review highlights how rational chemical design can be integrated with prostate cancer biology to develop more precise and clinically translatable nanotherapy strategies.

title: Melanin-like nanoparticles for nanomedicine and drug delivery.
abstract: Melanin plays important roles in coloration and photoprotection in living organisms. Because of its intrinsic biocompatibility, melanin and its biomimetic replicates find important applications in nanomedicine. Thanks to their unique optical and electronic properties, melanin-based materials could be used for both diagnostics and therapeutics. Modes of detection include photoacoustic imaging (PAI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Therapeutic activities include photothermal therapy (PTT), antioxidant (AOX) therapy, and drug delivery. In this review paper, we summarize and discuss the most recent applications of melanin-like nanoparticles (NPs) as multifunctional agents in nanomedicine and drug delivery. Although most of these applications involve the most popular biomimetic form of melanin, polydopamine (PDA, resulting from the oxidative polymerization of dopamine), in the last part of the review, we show that alternative forms of melanin are becoming more and more important for nanomedicine.

title: Carbon nanotube-induced magnetic shielding effects on <sup>129</sup>Xe NMR from equivariant neural networks.
abstract: Equivariant graph neural networks (EGNNs) have been successfully used in building efficient and accurate machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for molecular dynamics (MD) and to predict nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) parameters in complex systems. In this work, EGNNs are used to fine-tune an atomistic foundation model, which serves as an MLIP for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of xenon in carbon nanotubes. In addition, EGNNs are employed to develop a machine-learning model for the 129 Xe NMR magnetic shielding tensor, σ , enabling its direct prediction from the MLMD snapshots. Both models are data-efficient and remain accurate well beyond their training data. Using this dual-model framework, we show that xenon encapsulated in carbon nanotubes experiences a nanotube-induced, negative 129 Xe isotropic chemical shift that varies non-monotonically with nanotube diameter and depends further on temperature and Xe loading, establishing this dual-model approach as an efficient route to interpret confinement-driven 129 Xe NMR response.

title: An RGD peptide actively targeting nanoprobe with enhanced tumor accumulation for complementary magnetic resonance imaging/NIR-II fluorescence imaging.
abstract: Accurate visualization of tumor lesions with high contrast and well-defined margins remains a major challenge for preoperative evaluation and intraoperative navigation. Conventional single-modal contrast agents mainly rely on passive accumulation, which often suffers from limitations in terms of sensitivity, specificity and tumor uptake, as well as short circulation time in vivo . Therefore, it is necessary to develop high-performance multi-modal nanoprobes with active-targeting ability. Here, we develop an RGD-mediated active-targeted imaging nanoprobe based on lanthanide nanoparticles with a core-shell structure (NaGdF 4 :Er,Yb@NaGdF 4 :Yb,Nd), followed by in situ growth of a mesoporous SiO 2 shell and surface functionalization with DSPE-PEG 2000 -RGD to form the nanoprobe (abbreviated as DSR) for achieving molecular targeting of integrin αvβ 3 on tumor vascular endothelial cells. Under 808 nm excitation, DSR exhibits intense near-infrared IIb (NIR-IIb) emission at 1525 nm, markedly improving the contrast and margin delineation of in vivo tumor imaging. Importantly, the presence of Gd 3+ further endows the nanoprobe with T 1 -weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast, providing complementary anatomical information for tumor localization. With good biocompatibility, DSR can be used for actively targeted NIR-II fluorescence/ T 1 -MRI dual-modal imaging of breast cancer, providing a promising tool for image-guided surgery.

title: Thermosensitive RGD-modified liposomes co-loading Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> and sorafenib for synergistic photothermal-chemotherapy of hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Sorafenib (SRF) therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by dose-limiting toxicities, inadequate tumor exposure, and the inability to confine drug action spatiotemporally, leading to suboptimal efficacy and a narrow therapeutic window. Here we report an RGD-functionalized DPPC-based thermosensitive liposomal theranostic system co-encapsulating Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles and SRF (RGD-Fe 3 O 4 /SRF@TSL) to enable MRI-guided window selection and near-infrared (NIR)-triggered, on-demand chemotherapy potentiation. The nanosystem is colloidally stable (208 nm) and exhibits a phase transition at 41 °C. Accordingly, SRF release is sharply temperature-gated, reaching 88% at 45 °C but only 26% at 37 °C within 18 h (3.4-fold enhancement). Fe 3 O 4 confers strong T 2 MRI contrast ( r 2 = 136.4 mM -1 s -1 ) and photothermal conversion ( η = 24.73%), enabling noninvasive tracking of tumor accumulation and controllable local heating that elevates tumor-surface temperature to 56 °C within 5 min under 808 nm irradiation. Dynamic MRI identifies a pronounced tumor signal drop at ∼12 h post-injection, providing an imaging-defined irradiation window. RGD decoration improves cellular internalization (DiO-positive cells 80.6% vs . 55.8% at 3 h) and, together with NIR activation, increases ROS-associated signals, mitochondrial depolarization, and apoptosis (up to 46.4%) in vitro . In Hepa1-6 tumor-bearing mice, the image-guided combined regimen markedly suppresses tumor growth, reducing endpoint tumor weight from 1.1 g (PBS) to 0.1 g (91% reduction) without obvious acute toxicity under the tested conditions. This work establishes an operational "MRI-defined window → mild hyperthermia → thermosensitive release" paradigm to localize SRF action and improve the efficacy-toxicity balance for HCC therapy.

title: Green and sustainable synthesis of nanostructured metal phosphates: structure-property relationships and catalytic applications.
abstract: The sustainable design of effective catalysts necessitates synthetic methods that reduce resource usage while ensuring precise control over the composition, structure, and accessibility of active sites. Metal phosphates represent a versatile category of materials, as phosphate groups can directly engage in framework construction, influence the coordination and electronic environment of metal centers, and enhance acid-base, adsorption, and redox characteristics. This review thoroughly evaluates environmentally friendly and sustainable methods for synthesizing nanostructured metal phosphates, including hydrothermal, microwave-assisted, precipitation and co-precipitation, ultrasound-assisted, template-directed, mechanochemical, and solvent-free techniques. Instead of viewing individual studies as separate instances, the review analyzes how synthesis conditions affect nucleation, crystallization, morphology, porosity, defect formation, and multimetallic interactions, as well as how these structural attributes influence catalytic performance. Particular attention is devoted to the mechanistic role of phosphate species in material formation and catalysis, encompassing M-O-P bond formation, framework charge balance, template interactions, stabilization of metal centers, and modulation of Brønsted/Lewis acidity and redox behavior. The review critically assesses the advantages and limitations of nanoparticle, nanoporous, and hybrid architectures concerning active-site accessibility, mass transport, stability, leaching, and scalability. Finally, it highlights significant knowledge gaps, such as the identification of genuine active sites, operando structural evolution, quantitative structure-activity relationships, defect control, multimetallic synergy, and standardized sustainability evaluation. Thus, the review establishes a structure-mechanism-performance framework for the rational development of scalable and truly sustainable phosphate-based nanocatalysts.

title: X-ray µ-CT contrast agents employing highly-concentrated low-viscosity layered double hydroxide nanoparticles for high-resolution imaging of vasculature.
abstract: Contrast agents capable of being injected and cured in situ within the vasculature are required for angiography based on X-ray microcomputed tomography (µ-CT) for pathophysiology of biopsies or postmortem. In this study, we developed a contrast agent based on highly-concentrated methanolic dispersion of NiAl-type layered double hydroxide nanoparticles (NiAl-LDH NPs) for X-ray µ-CT imaging of vasculature. We optimized the synthesis conditions of the constituent NiAl-LDH NPs, with particular attention to drying conditions and dispersion media selection. The formulated contrast agent achieved a particle concentration >30 wt%, a curing time of ∼30 min, and low viscosity (<100 mPa s). These properties enabled successful perfusion into small vessels and capillaries giving excellent X-ray attenuation following setting without tissue maceration. Consequently, this enabled reliable vessel identification and segmentation using simple intensity-based approaches giving a robust approach to accelerated tissue screening.

title: Comparative Assessment of Orofacial Myofunction, Strength, and Quality of Life in Children With and Without Anterior Open Bite: The OMBIT Study.
abstract: Purpose Anterior open bite (AOB) is a multifactorial malocclusion frequently associated with nonnutritive sucking habits (NNSHs) and orofacial dysfunctions. However, little is known about the specific orofacial strength and endurance profile in affected children. This study evaluated myofunctional history, orofacial myofunctional status, orofacial strength, and oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) in children in the mixed dentition stage with AOB, compared to controls without AOB. Method Sixteen children with AOB in the mixed dentition stage ( M age = 8.2 years) and 16 age- and gender-matched controls participated in this cross-sectional study. Dental and orofacial histories were collected through parental questionnaires. Palatal and occlusal morphologies were assessed using intraoral scans. Orofacial function was examined using the Orofacial Myofunctional Evaluation with Scores (OMES) protocol and ultrasound imaging. Maximum isometric pressure and endurance of the tongue and lips were measured using the Iowa Oral Performance Instrument (IOPI). OHRQoL was assessed using the Child Oral Health Impact Profile-Ortho (COHIP-Ortho). Results Oral habits (e.g., nail biting, lip licking) were more frequently observed in the AOB group, and parental reports indicated that persistent open mouth behavior was reported more often in children with AOB. Two thirds of the participants had a history of NNSH, with similar prevalence across groups; however, AOB was associated with NNSH cessation at an older age. AOB was associated with higher anterior tongue endurance. No other significant differences were found in tongue or lip strength or endurance, OMES scores, or COHIP-Ortho scores. Conclusions The absence of group differences in orofacial strength and most endurance measures suggests that, in this sample, mixed-dentition AOB was not accompanied by generalized orofacial strength deficits. These findings support early functional screening and suggest that function-focused orofacial myofunctional therapy, rather than strength-based training, may be a relevant approach in children with AOB.

title: Clinical Interpretation and Structured Reporting of Velopharyngeal Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Framework for Multidisciplinary Decision Making.
abstract: Purpose Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enables direct visualization of the velopharyngeal (VP) mechanism, including the soft palate, pharyngeal walls, adenoid tissue, and levator veli palatini (LVP) musculature. As VP MRI becomes more integrated into multidisciplinary craniofacial care, speech-language pathologists (SLPs) are increasingly involved in image interpretation. However, structured guidance for translating MRI findings into clinically relevant multidisciplinary decision making remains limited. This study presents a clinically oriented framework for interpretation of VP MRI and introduces a structured reporting approach to support consistent documentation and interdisciplinary communication. Method A literature-informed, consensus-based framework for interpreting VP MRI was developed. Scoping review first identified MRI-derived anatomic variables relevant to VP function. These variables were organized into interpretive domains through multidisciplinary discussion among SLPs, surgeons, and radiologists. The framework was operationalized into structured reporting templates for speech-language pathology and radiology documentation and prospectively piloted in clinical VP MRI cases. Results The resulting framework organizes interpretation across five domains: VP proportional relationships, LVP morphology and function, VP closure dynamics, additional structural contributors, and articulatory context. Structured templates integrate quantitative measurements, qualitative observations, and clinical synthesis. The framework was successfully applied across pilot cases, supporting consistent interpretation and documentation. Conclusion This framework provides clinicians with a practical method for integrating VP MRI observations with speech assessment to enhance clinical reasoning and inform multidisciplinary treatment planning for individuals with VP dysfunction. title: Current classification systems in slipped capital femoral epiphysis: Clinical relevance, limitations, and future directions.
abstract: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) is the most common adolescent hip disorder and remains a significant cause of pain, gait disturbance, proximal femoral deformity, and early degenerative hip disease. Accurate classification of SCFE is essential for diagnosis, prognostication, treatment planning, and communication among orthopedic surgeons. Over the past several decades, multiple classification systems have been proposed based on symptom duration, physeal stability, radiographic severity, and deformity morphology. However, substantial variability exists regarding their reliability, prognostic value, and clinical applicability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the currently available classification systems in SCFE, including temporal, Loder, Southwick, Wilson, epiphyseal tubercle (Maranho), MRI-based, and three-dimensional/statistical shape modeling classifications. Particular emphasis is placed on their historical evolution, clinical relevance, prognostic implications, limitations, and emerging role in modern hip preservation strategies. Among existing systems, the Loder classification remains the most clinically influential because of its strong association with avascular necrosis risk, while the Southwick classification continues to play a central role in quantifying deformity severity and guiding surgical decision-making. Emerging imaging-based and three-dimensional classifications have improved understanding of the rotational and multiplanar nature of SCFE and may facilitate earlier diagnosis, improved deformity characterization, and individualized treatment planning. Nevertheless, no single classification system comprehensively integrates physeal stability, deformity severity, vascular compromise, cartilage injury, and long-term functional prognosis. Current SCFE classification systems remain valuable tools in contemporary clinical practice; however, important limitations persist regarding reproducibility, prognostic accuracy, and integration with modern biomechanical concepts. Future classification frameworks may benefit from a multidomain approach integrating physeal stability, deformity morphology, vascular and biological status, cartilage involvement, and patient-specific prognostic factors, with prospective multicentre validation required before clinical adoption.
originalAbstract: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) is the most common adolescent hip disorder and remains a significant cause of pain, gait disturbance, proximal femoral deformity, and early degenerative hip disease. Accurate classification of SCFE is essential for diagnosis, prognostication, treatment planning, and communication among orthopedic surgeons. Over the past several decades, multiple classification systems have been proposed based on symptom duration, physeal stability, radiographic severity, and deformity morphology. However, substantial variability exists regarding their reliability, prognostic value, and clinical applicability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the currently available classification systems in SCFE, including temporal, Loder, Southwick, Wilson, epiphyseal tubercle (Maranho), MRI-based, and three-dimensional/statistical shape modeling classifications. Particular emphasis is placed on their historical evolution, clinical relevance, prognostic implications, limitations, and emerging role in modern hip preservation strategies. Among existing systems, the Loder classification remains the most clinically influential because of its strong association with avascular necrosis risk, while the Southwick classification continues to play a central role in quantifying deformity severity and guiding surgical decision-making. Emerging imaging-based and three-dimensional classifications have improved understanding of the rotational and multiplanar nature of SCFE and may facilitate earlier diagnosis, improved deformity characterization, and individualized treatment planning. Nevertheless, no single classification system comprehensively integrates physeal stability, deformity severity, vascular compromise, cartilage injury, and long-term functional prognosis. Current SCFE classification systems remain valuable tools in contemporary clinical practice; however, important limitations persist regarding reproducibility, prognostic accuracy, and integration with modern biomechanical concepts. Future classification frameworks may benefit from a multidomain approach integrating physeal stability, deformity morphology, vascular and biological status, cartilage involvement, and patient-specific prognostic factors, with prospective multicentre validation required before clinical adoption.

title: Outcomes of mini-screw fixation following dorsal closing wedge osteotomy for treatment of freiberg's disease.
abstract: Background Freiberg's disease is an osteochondrosis of the lesser metatarsal heads, most commonly the 2 nd , that predominantly affects adolescent females and causes pain and limited motion; early cases are treated conservatively, while advanced or refractory ones may need dorsal closing wedge osteotomy. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical and radiological outcomes of dorsal closing wedge osteotomy fixed with a single mini-screw in patients aged 13 to 30 years. Methods This prospective observational case series included 48 consecutive patients with Freiberg's disease, Smillie stage II, III, or IV, who underwent dorsal closing wedge osteotomy with mini-screw fixation after failed conservative treatment. Pain was assessed with a 0-10 visual analogue scale (VAS) preoperatively and at the final 6-month follow-up, radiographs were reviewed for osteotomy union, and complications were recorded. Results There was a substantial reduction in pain, with the mean VAS score improving from 8.67 ± 0.88 to 1.33 ± 2.01 (P<0.001). Radiographic union was achieved in all patients at a mean of 7.31 ± 1.22 weeks. Intraoperative fragmentation of the metatarsal head occurred in 3 patients (6.25%) and superficial wound infection in 3 (6.25%), and all patients had some loss of metatarsophalangeal joint plantarflexion (mean 11°). Conclusions In this case series, dorsal closing wedge osteotomy with mini-screw fixation for Freiberg's disease was associated with a substantial reduction in pain and a low complication rate, although some loss of metatarsophalangeal joint motion occurred in all patients.

title: Impact of CT-based posterior malleolar fracture classifications on clinical outcomes in bimalleolar ankle fractures involving the posterior and lateral malleoli.
abstract: Background The prognostic value of computed tomography (CT)-based posterior malleolar fracture classifications in uniformly treated fractures remains uncertain. Purpose To examine associations of the Haraguchi, Bartoníček/Rammelt, and Mason-Molloy classifications with 1-year functional and early radiographic outcomes. Study design Retrospective cohort study. Methods Fifty-eight patients with posterior malleolar and Weber B lateral malleolar fractures underwent fixation of both malleoli through a posterolateral approach. Outcomes were the 1-year American Orthopedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) score and Kellgren-Lawrence grade. Classification subgroups were compared using Kruskal-Wallis tests; fragment dimensions were assessed using Spearman correlations. Results Mean AOFAS score was 92.97 ± 5.28 (95% confidence interval [CI], 91.58-94.35); 10 patients (17%) scored 100 and 24 (41%) scored ≥95. Subgroup mean scores were 91.0-93.3 for Haraguchi (p = 0.994), 84.0-96.5 for Bartoníček/Rammelt (p = 0.130), and 87.0-93.3 for Mason-Molloy (p = 0.836). Kellgren-Lawrence grades did not differ across Haraguchi, Bartoníček/Rammelt, or Mason-Molloy subgroups (p = 0.449, p = 0.277, and p = 0.608, respectively). AOFAS correlations with axial and sagittal fragment lengths were ρ = 0.001 (95% CI, -0.273 to 0.285; p = 0.992) and ρ = 0.049 (95% CI, -0.242 to 0.342; p = 0.717), respectively. Conclusions No significant associations with 1-year outcomes were detected. Small, uneven subgroups and upper-end AOFAS clustering limited precision; potentially meaningful prognostic associations cannot be excluded.

title: [Atlantoaxial luxation in a neonatal Warmblood foal].
abstract: Abstract Atlantoaxial luxation represents a rare but clinically relevant differential diagnosis in neonatal foals presenting with neurological abnormalities or dysphagia. This case report describes a newborn filly without apparent ataxia, but presenting with a stiff head-neck posture and milky nasal discharge. Clinical examination revealed a compromised general condition and abnormal swelling in the region of the fossa retromandibularis. Radiographic examination confirmed the diagnosis of an atlantoaxial luxation. Due to the poor prognosis the foal was euthanized. This case highlights the diagnostic approach to atlantoaxial luxation and emphasizes the importance of imaging modalities both for ruling out differential diagnoses and for assessing therapeutic options.

title: Coxofemoral luxation in 112 cattle - a retrospective analysis.
abstract: Objective Coxofemoral luxation ( luxatio ossis femoris ) requires special consideration among orthopedic conditions of the pelvic area in cattle. The disease has a guarded prognosis, and affected cattle are often recumbent and therefore must not be shipped to a slaughter facility. Our study aimed to compile epidemiologically relevant aspects of coxofemoral luxation and facilitate the diagnosis in the field and at referral clinics. Material and methods This retrospective study analyzed 116 cases of coxofemoral luxation and subluxation in 112 cattle in relation to the housing system used and the breeds affected. The different directions of luxation, clinical findings, diagnostic imaging, treatment, and prognosis were also investigated. Results Holstein Friesian cows (93/116; 83.0%) and free-stall barns (80/87; 92.0%) were overrepresented, and 96 of the 112 animals (85.7%) were recumbent at referral. The general health status was impaired in 87 of 102 cattle (81.8%). Caudoventral luxation occurred in 87/116 cases (75.0%), subluxation in 17/116 (14.6%), craniodorsal luxation in 6/116 (5.2%), caudodorsal luxation in 3/116 (2.6%), and cranioventral luxation in 3/116 (2.6%) cases. Bilateral coxofemoral luxation occurred in 16/116 cases (13.8%,) and accompanying fractures of the greater trochanter or the femoral head in 14/112 (12.5%) of the cattle; 93/112 cattle (83.0 %) were slaughtered or subjected to euthanasia after the diagnosis. Of 19/112 cattle (17.0 %) that underwent treatment, only 4 (21.1%) remained productive in the long term. In 13 cows in advanced pregnancy, the prognosis for a viable calf was guarded to favorable after a gestation length of 248 days. Conclusions and clinical relevance Dairy cows that fall in a free-stall barn and incur splaying of the hind legs ("doing the splits") usually sustain subluxation or caudoventral luxation of the femoral head, particularly when the fall is sudden. The diagnosis often required ultrasonographic and radiographic confirmation, highlighting the diagnostic difficulty in the field. The prognosis for caudoventral coxofemoral luxation is especially grave. Prevention of the disease by barn construction measures is therefore essential.

title: High rate of neoplasia diagnosis at endoscopic reassessment and incidence of progression in patients with ultra-long Barrett esophagus referred to expert centers.
abstract: Background Surveillance recommendations for Barrett esophagus (BE) are based on BE length, since the risk of progression to dysplasia or esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) has been shown to increase with greater BE length. The 2023 European Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Guideline on BE advises referral to Barrett expert centers (BECs) for surveillance of ultra-long ( ≥ 10 cm) BE. This study evaluated the outcomes of expert care for patients with ultra-long BE in the Netherlands. Methods This retrospective, nationwide cohort study including patients referred with ultra-long nondysplastic BE (NDBE) to Dutch BECs. Outcome parameters were number of cases upgraded to dysplasia/esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) at expert endoscopic reassessment, and number of cases with progression to high-grade dysplasia (HGD)/EAC during surveillance after a confirmed diagnosis of NDBE at expert endoscopic reassessment. Results 168 patients were referred with ultra-long NDBE, namely with Barrett length (median and interquartile range [IQR]), circumference (C) 11 cm (9-12), maximum (M) 12 cm (10-14). Upon expert endoscopic reassessment, 28 /168 (17 %) patients were diagnosed with dysplasia/EAC, among whom 5 /168 (3 %) had HGD/EAC in a visible lesion. In 11 patients no Seattle protocol biopsies were obtained, thus 129 patients had an NDBE diagnosis based on Seattle protocol biopsies. Of these, 95 /129 (74 %) had > 1 surveillance endoscopy at the BEC. During surveillance 20 patients progressed to LGD (n = 11, 12 %), HGD (n = 4, 4 %) or EAC (n = 5, 5 %); all progressors underwent endoscopic therapy. Conclusion Expert care with dedicated BE endoscopy programs and experienced endoscopists may be beneficial for patients with ultra-long BE.

title: Apple Vision Pro-Enabled Endoscopic Endonasal Approach for Pituitary Adenoma Resection: First In-Human Spatial Computing Skull Base Neurosurgery Case Report.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to report the first in-human skull base neurosurgery case using Apple Vision Pro (AVP). Main Outcome Measures Endoscopic stream with the AVP in an endoscopic endonasal transsellar and left transcavernous approach for resection of a pituitary adenoma. Results Endoscopic endonasal approach was performed using the AVP for resection of a pituitary adenoma. The procedure was completed without complication. A postoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed no convincing residual pituitary mass. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 2. Conclusion Endoscopic streaming to the AVP is safe in skull base surgery. We described the first case report of an AVP-specific spatial computing technology successfully used to display endoscopic feed to the skull base neurosurgeon during skull base neurosurgery with no intraoperative complications. Continued integration of intraoperative navigation platforms, patient vitals, preoperative imaging, and electronic medical records with endoscopic streams serves as an important step in optimizing surgeon experience and developing a virtual operating room.

title: Acute Enlargement of a Frontal Calvarial Lesion in Polyostotic Fibrous Dysplasia Associated with McCune-Albright Syndrome: A Case Report.
abstract: Background McCune-Albright syndrome is a rare mosaic disorder caused by postzygotic activating mutations in GNAS , classically presenting with fibrous dysplasia (FD), hyperpigmented macules, and endocrinopathies. Craniofacial FD is common and typically follows a benign course. However, acute symptomatic changes with aggressive imaging features may mimic malignant transformation or secondary lesions such as aneurysmal bone cysts (ABCs), creating significant diagnostic uncertainty. Case Description We report a 20-year-old woman with known MAS and polyostotic FD who presented with a 4-week history of progressive left frontal swelling, headache, and tenderness. Interval imaging revealed a rapidly enlarging erosive lytic lesion of the left frontal calvarium with peripheral enhancement and an internal fluid-fluid level, raising concern for secondary pathology or malignancy. Given rapid growth and cortical erosion, the patient underwent surgical resection with cranioplasty. Intraoperatively, the lesion contained serosanguinous fluid. Histopathology demonstrated bland spindle cell proliferation with curvilinear woven bone trabeculae and hemosiderin-laden macrophages, without cytologic atypia, necrosis, or features of ABC. Molecular testing confirmed a GNAS p.(R201C) mutation, consistent with FD. The patient had an uncomplicated postoperative course with complete symptom resolution. Conclusion This case highlights that fluid-fluid levels, rapid interval growth, and erosive changes can occur in craniofacial FD without ABC formation or malignant transformation. Imaging findings alone are insufficient to distinguish benign changes from aggressive pathology. Accurate diagnosis requires a multimodal approach integrating clinical context, advanced imaging, histopathology, and pathologic analysis. Surgical intervention is justified in some cases to establish diagnosis and provide symptomatic relief.

title: Recurrent Dedifferentiated Clival Chondrosarcoma Presenting 32 Years after Initial Treatment: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Skull base chondrosarcomas are rare and locally aggressive tumors with heterogeneous biology accounting for 0.1-0.2% of all intracranial tumors. Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma is an exceptionally uncommon and aggressive variant, seldom seen at the skull base. We report a recurrent clival chondrosarcoma with a small, dedifferentiated component, and an unusually long latency after initial treatment. Case Report A 66-year-old woman was referred with a recurrent progressive clival lesion, initially suspected to be a chordoma. She had undergone subtotal resection followed by single-fraction radiosurgery (25 Gy) 32 years earlier. Surveillance imaging demonstrated interval growth compared with imaging 5 years earlier, prompting repeat subtotal resection. Histopathology revealed a conventional chondrosarcoma with a dedifferentiated component comprising <5% of tumor area and an isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) R132 mutation. The patient declined adjuvant radiotherapy. Three years later, she developed worsening diplopia, new right oculomotor palsy, and headache with radiologic progression, prompting repeat subtotal resection. She currently awaits postoperative proton beam radiotherapy. Conclusion This case highlights a key diagnostic challenge of distinguishing chondrosarcoma from chordoma, and underscores the importance of meticulous histologic sampling to detect small dedifferentiated foci that may otherwise result in undergrading and undertreatment. The heterogeneity in clinical behavior observed across histopathological subtypes further underscores the necessity for grade/subtype-driven treatment regimens. Therefore, accurate subtype classification and molecular annotation may better inform treatment strategy and follow-up. Lastly, the rarity of dedifferentiated skull base chondrosarcoma reinforces the need for multicenter registries to further understand the behavior and vulnerabilities of this rare disease.

title: Tenosynovitis caused by Mycobacterium malmoense.
abstract: Background Mycobacterium malmoense is a slow-growing nontuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) increasingly recognized as a cause of extrapulmonary infections. Tenosynovitis due to M. malmoense is rare and diagnostically challenging because of its indolent course and nonspecific clinical presentation. Case presentation We report a 65-year-old immunocompetent woman presenting with progressive wrist pain, swelling, and impaired hand function without prior trauma. Symptoms developed after exposure to fresh fish and shellfish. Surgical exploration revealed extensive tenosynovitis with median nerve compression. Histopathology showed granulomatous synovitis suggestive of mycobacterial infection. Molecular testing detected Mycobacterium genus DNA, while PCR for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex was negative. After prolonged incubation, culture identified M. malmoense . Drug susceptibility testing demonstrated susceptibility to standard antimycobacterial agents except doxycycline. Initial empiric therapy targeting M. marinum was adapted following species identification. After 8 months of treatment, significant clinical and radiological improvement was observed, with no evidence of relapse at 6-month follow-up. Discussion M. malmoense tenosynovitis is extremely rare, with only few cases reported. Diagnosis is frequently delayed due to low sensitivity of microscopy, slow growth in culture, and nonspecific findings. Molecular diagnostics and prolonged incubation are essential. Management requires a combination of surgery and prolonged antimycobacterial therapy. Conclusion NTM infections, including M. malmoense , should be considered in chronic tenosynovitis unresponsive to standard treatment. Early diagnostic suspicion and interdisciplinary management are crucial for favorable outcomes.

NTM infections, including M. malmoense, should be considered in chronic tenosynovitis unresponsive to standard treatment. Early diagnostic suspicion and interdisciplinary management are crucial for favorable outcomes.

title: Ultrasound in fetal growth restriction.
abstract: Abstract Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with increased perinatal morbidity and mortality. Its recognition requires differentiation from a constitutionally small-for-gestational-age (SGA) fetus. Based on the current AWMF S2k guideline, this CME review summarizes the ultrasound assessment and clinical management of suspected FGR. Accurate first-trimester dating, standardized fetal biometry, assessment of amniotic fluid volume, and detailed anatomical evaluation form the basis of diagnosis. Consensus-based criteria distinguish early FGR before 32 + 0 weeks' gestation from late FGR at or beyond 32 + 0 weeks' gestation. Multivessel Doppler assessment of the umbilical artery, middle cerebral artery, cerebroplacental ratio, and ductus venosus provides complementary information on placental resistance, fetal redistribution, and cardiovascular decompensation. Cardiotocography, including computerized analysis of short-term variation in early FGR, is used as part of multimodal surveillance and should not be interpreted in isolation. The review discusses appropriate monitoring intervals, indications for inpatient care, antenatal corticosteroids and fetal neuroprotection when preterm birth is anticipated, as well as gestational-age- and finding-dependent timing and mode of delivery. A practical clinical case illustrates the diagnostic pathway from abnormal fetal biometry to delivery planning.

title: Practice Variability in Anorectal Malformations Management across Europe: A TEPS-EUPSA Survey with Analysis of Center Volume Effects.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate management strategies for anorectal malformations (ARMs) across Europe and assess the impact of institutional case volume on clinical decision-making.A cross-sectional online survey developed within the Trainees in European Pediatric Surgery (TEPS) and endorsed by the European Paediatric Surgeons' Association (EUPSA) Network Office was distributed among pediatric surgeons involved in ARM care. The questionnaire addressed diagnostic workup, surgical management, perioperative care, and long-term follow-up. European responses were analyzed and compared by institutional case volume.A total of 94 responses from 21 countries were analyzed. Substantial variability was observed across all domains of care. Ultrasound-based screening and invertogram were widely used, whereas high-pressure distal colostography was variably applied. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and vaginoscopy were used more selectively. Primary neonatal repair in cases with the rectum located <1 cm from the perineal skin was commonly performed, and staged reconstruction was most frequently undertaken at 3 to 6 months. Non-divided stomas were more frequently used in high-volume centers ( p = 0.002), with increasing center volume associated with higher odds of their use (odds ratio [OR] 2.98, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.51-5.87, p = 0.002). Routine anal dilations were reported by 44.7% of respondents and were less common in high-volume centers ( p = 0.005); increasing volume was associated with lower odds of routine dilation (OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.20-0.72, p = 0.003).ARM management across Europe remains highly variable. Institutional case volume is associated with practice differences, particularly in stoma configuration and postoperative dilation strategies.

title: Mesenteric Vein Thrombosis and Its Interventional-Radiological Management.
abstract: Objective and background Mesenteric venous thrombosis (MVT) is a rare but clinically important cause of mesenteric ischemia. It most often affects the superior mesenteric vein and is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Nonspecific symptoms often delay diagnosis. Severe disease courses may occur in the presence of intestinal infarction. Objective and background The aim of this article is to provide a structured overview of the etiopathogenesis, imaging findings, and interventional radiological treatment options for MVT. Materials and methods Narrative, literature-based review taking into consideration current guidelines, radiological imaging protocols, and endovascular techniques. Results The pathogenesis of MVT can be classified according to Virchow's triad, including hypercoagulability, stasis, and endothelial injury. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is the method of choice for diagnosis. It demonstrates thrombosis as a contrast filling defect within the portomesenteric venous system and allows assessment of bowel viability. Important CT findings include bowel wall thickening, mesenteric edema, ascites, and the halo or target sign. Pneumatosis intestinalis and portomesenteric venous gas suggest transmural ischemia and indicate the need for immediate surgical management. Systemic anticoagulation is the cornerstone of treatment. Mechanical thrombectomy, local thrombolysis, stent angioplasty, and, where appropriate, TIPS placement may be considered in complex or prolonged clinical courses. Conclusion Early interdisciplinary, imaging-guided management is crucial for diagnosis and treatment planning. CT guides further management by detecting thrombosis and assessing bowel viability. Interventional radiological recanalization is not a first-line treatment, but it may represent an important escalation strategy in selected patients. Key points · Mesenteric venous thrombosis is an uncommon but clinically relevant cause of mesenteric ischemia.. · Early interdisciplinary diagnostic work-up is essential to prevent irreversible intestinal ischemic injury.. · Contrast-enhanced CT represents the key imaging modality, enabling both detection of venous thrombosis and assessment of bowel viability.. · In the absence of contraindications, systemic anticoagulation constitutes the cornerstone of treatment.. · Surgical management is indicated in the presence of suspected transmural bowel necrosis or clinical signs of peritonitis.. · Interventional radiological recanalization techniques may be considered as an escalation strategy in selected patients.. Citation format · Camp LC, Weber M, Arndt H. Mesenteric Vein Thrombosis and Its Interventional-Radiological Management. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2965-8425.

title: A Comprehensive Approach to Flexion-Varus Tibial Plateau Fractures: Principles of Systematic Management.
abstract: Abstract Tibial plateau fractures (TPFs) are complex intra-articular injuries frequently accompanied by significant soft tissue injury. Existing medical literature has shown that TPFs resulting from a flexion-varus injury mechanism, affecting the posteromedial column primarily, are associated with worse clinical outcome scores and a higher risk of conversion to total knee arthroplasty. This narrative review aims to explain why this specific subgroup has a poorer prognosis compared with other TPFs subtypes. Four key factors are examined in this review: fracture morphology, biomechanics, soft tissue involvement, and surgical management. The complex fracture morphology of flexion-varus TPFs can be most accurately assessed using three-dimensional computed tomography-based reconstructions. The mechanism of injury helps to better understand fracture morphology and potential soft tissue injury. Soft tissue injuries are frequent in these type of fractures, such as anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) avulsion fracture, lateral meniscus tears, and entrapment. These three elements are important for better understanding TPFs and adequately planning surgical strategy. The severity of the fracture and the involvement of the posterolateral depression complicate surgical treatment. Visualization of the posteromedial compartment is essential but remains challenging. Anatomical reduction and stable fixation of the posteromedial and posterolaterocentral tibial plateau, with consideration of any meniscal injury, should be performed with care. An ACL avulsion fracture should ideally be fixed. Although preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides valuable information about the soft tissue involved, this examination is not yet routinely performed. Given the high incidence of ACL and (lateral) meniscal injury, an MRI is highly recommended.

title: Interstitial Lung Abnormalities: A Multidisciplinary Narrative Review.
abstract: Abstract Interstitial lung abnormalities (ILAs) is an umbrella term used to describe a spectrum of computed tomography (CT)-detected lung abnormalities that may reflect interstitial lung disease (ILD). Initially perceived as a niche topic-and often underreported in clinical practice-ILAs have gained increasing attention in recent years, given growing evidence of their association with several adverse outcomes, including increased all-cause, respiratory, and cancer-related mortality. Over time, efforts have been made to standardize the definition, classification, and management of ILAs. The recent American Thoracic Society clinical statement has reshaped the definition of ILAs proposed by the Fleischner Society in 2020, introducing substantial changes to the populations in whom ILAs may be identified and proposing new boundaries to distinguish ILAs from ILD. Nevertheless, several key aspects remain debated, and growing efforts are being made to balance the opportunity for early ILD diagnosis against the risk of unnecessary burden on patients and healthcare systems. This is particularly relevant given the increasing number of CT examinations performed in the general population, as well as in patients at increased risk of ILD, such as those with connective tissue disease, and considering the substantial number of examinations related to expanding implementation of lung cancer screening. In this narrative review, we focus on the definition, implications, and management of ILAs, integrating pulmonology, radiology, and pathology perspectives on the strengths and limitations of current approaches.

title: [Molecular-Based Diagnostics and Therapy of Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer (mHSPC)].
abstract: Abstract Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) represents a biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease entity. While traditional clinical parameters such as metastatic burden and timing of metastasis remain prognostically relevant, molecular biomarkers are increasingly gaining importance for individualized treatment planning. Genetic alterations in tumor suppressor genes and DNA repair pathways, particularly BRCA, PTEN, and TP53 aberrations, are associated with more aggressive disease courses and poorer prognosis. At the same time, these molecular alterations provide novel therapeutic opportunities, including the use of PARP inhibitors and AKT inhibitors.In addition to genetic alterations, transcriptomic characteristics also play an important role. In particular, androgen receptor (AR) pathway activity influences prognosis and treatment response. Low AR activity and reduced PSMA expression have been associated with reduced sensitivity to hormonal therapies and increased biological heterogeneity. Conversely, high PSMA expression appears to correlate with improved responses to androgen deprivation therapy as well as PSMA-targeted radioligand therapies.Advanced imaging modalities such as PSMA PET imaging further contribute to a refined understanding of metastatic disease biology and increasingly challenge traditional disease classifications. Moreover, biomarkers including PSA nadir or circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) may help identify progression patterns and guide future treatment intensification or de-escalation strategies.Overall, current evidence suggests that integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and imaging biomarkers may substantially improve the biological characterization of mHSPC. In the future, these approaches could enable a more accurate prognostic stratification and support the development of personalized therapeutic concepts.

title: Ultra-Low-Dose Computed Tomography of the Lung: Evidence and Prospects of a New Method.
abstract: Abstract The introduction of state-of-the-art tube, detector, and image reconstruction techniques has made ultra-low-dose CT (ULD-CT) of the lungs technologically feasible, resulting in radiation exposure comparable to that of chest X-rays. Due to its high-contrast structures, the lung as target organ is generally well suited for reducing radiation exposure while maintaining diagnostic accuracy, which could already be shown for the earlier development of low-dose CT (LDCT). The current state of the literature already demonstrates significant benefits of ULD-CT for the diagnosis of respiratory diseases, including COPD, pneumonia, interstitial lung disease, pediatric lung disease, as well as in interventional procedures. It is expected that ULD-CT will significantly expand the range of indications for CT and, in certain areas, will be able to replace chest X-rays as the initial imaging modality once its availability in institutions increases. Limitations currently arise from the known dependencies of quantitative methods on radiation exposure and image noise, and the fact that in-depth validation has not yet taken place. Key points · Ultra-low-dose computed tomography (ULD-CT) reduces radiation exposure to the level of a conventional chest X-ray through the latest tube, detector, and reconstruction technologies.. · ULD-CT can already be used for the diagnosis of solid pulmonary nodules, pneumonia, and chronic inflammatory airway diseases.. · Especially in children and immunosuppressed patients, ULD-CT should be considered for monitoring the progression of inflammatory lung diseases.. · There is insufficient evidence for the use of ULD-CT in interstitial lung diseases.. · In the future, ULD-CT could replace conventional chest X-ray for many indications in thoracic imaging.. Citation format · Wielpütz MO, Stiller W, Bayerl N et al. Ultra-Low-Dose Computed Tomography of the Lung: Evidence and Prospects of a New Method. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2977-0644.

title: Temporal Bone Osteosarcoma in Pregnancy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: Introduction Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor; however, involvement of the temporal bone is exceptionally rare, particularly during pregnancy. The coexistence of malignancy and pregnancy presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges requiring multidisciplinary management. Case Presentation A 23-year-old woman presented with persistent right otalgia and an external auditory canal lesion initially diagnosed as cholesteatoma. Following surgical resection, final histopathology revealed temporal bone osteosarcoma with early locoregional recurrence and intracranial extension. Pregnancy was incidentally diagnosed during oncologic evaluation at 24 weeks of gestation. Given the aggressive nature of the tumor, pregnancy termination followed by palliative chemotherapy was initially recommended; however, the patient elected to continue the pregnancy after multidisciplinary counseling. She received chemoradiotherapy with ifosfamide/mesna and 40 Gy radiotherapy. Subsequently, severe anhydramnios and early fetal growth restriction developed, likely secondary to fetal nephrotoxicity associated with ifosfamide exposure. A cesarean section was performed after antenatal corticosteroid administration, resulting in the delivery of a live preterm neonate admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit, and discharged after 58 days of hospitalization. Conclusion Temporal bone osteosarcoma during pregnancy is exceedingly rare and requires complex multidisciplinary management balancing maternal oncologic treatment and fetal risks.

title: Giant Multiloculated Cystic Trochlear Nerve Schwannoma Between the Tentorial Leaflets: Case Report and Systematic Review.
abstract: Background Trochlear nerve schwannomas (TNSs) are exceptionally rare benign tumors, accounting for a very small fraction of intracranial schwannomas. Due to their deep locations and slow growth, they often reach a considerable size before diagnosis. Giant or multiloculated cystic variants are exceptionally uncommon and present significant diagnostic and surgical challenges. Methods A 32-year-old female presented with headache and dizziness but no diplopia. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a giant multiloculated cystic lesion extending from the posterior fossa to the right temporal lobe, causing obstructive hydrocephalus. The mass was removed through a right paramedian supracerebellar transtentorial approach under intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. The tumor was confined between the two tentorium leaflets with the trochlear nerve entering and exiting the lesion. Gross total resection was achieved with an uneventful postoperative course. Histopathology confirmed a World Health Organization Grade I schwannoma with Antoni A-B architecture and diffuse S-100 positivity. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines, identifying forty-six surgically treated cases, analyzed together with the present case (n = 46). Results Mean age was 44.7 years with an approximately equal sex distribution. Most tumors (76.1%) were located in the ambient or crural cisterns, followed by the quadrigeminal cistern (10.8%) and cisterno-cavernous region (8.7%). Diplopia and trochlear nerve palsy were the most common presenting symptoms. Gross total resection was achieved in 80.4% of patients, while postoperative trochlear palsy occurred in 60.8%. No malignant transformation or early recurrence was reported. Conclusion This case represents one of the largest TNSs described and the second known lesion arising between the tentorial leaflets. Awareness of this unique anatomic configuration is essential for accurate preoperative diagnosis and surgical planning. A meticulous, anatomy-guided microsurgical approach enables complete resection while preserving neurological function in select cases.

title: Neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest: evidence review and institutional protocol proposal.
abstract: Background Cardiac arrest (CA) is associated with high mortality and neurological morbidity, mainly due to hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Accurate neurological prognostication in CA survivors is essential to guide therapeutic decisions and provide appropriate care. Objective To review the current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA and to propose an institutional protocol adapted to the resources of Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre (HCPA). Methods The current narrative review was conducted in two stages: a literature review and the development of an institutional protocol. Articles were selected according to their clinical relevance and their contribution to current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA. The PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and SciELO databases were searched. The protocol was developed considering the clinical tools available at HCPA, including neurological examination, electroencephalography (EEG), and neuroimaging. Results Brain injury after CA occurs in three stages: intra-arrest ischemia, immediate reperfusion, and delayed postreperfusion injury. Prognostic modalities include neurological examination, EEG, somatosensory-evoked potentials (SSEPs), serum biomarkers, and neuroimaging. Reliable predictors of poor outcome include absent brainstem reflexes at 72 hours, persistent EEG suppression, bilateral absence of cortical N20 potentials, and diffuse abnormalities on magnetic resonance imaging. The proposed protocol organizes assessments from admission to the Intensive Care Unit through day 5 after the return of spontaneous circulation. Conclusion A standardized post-CA neurological prognostication protocol at HCPA may improve care quality, enhance communication with families, and support ethically-sound decision-making.

title: Automated Detection and Segmentation of Dental Caries in Panoramic Radiographs Using YOLOv8-Based Deep Learning Model.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to develop an automated dental caries localization system through detection and classification using a deep learning (DL) approach based on You Only Look Once Version 8 (YOLOv8). Materials and methods YOLOv8 models were developed using 750 panoramic radiographs, which were divided into training, validation, and test sets at a ratio of 80%:10%:10%. The training and validation data were cropped into six regions to enhance the detection model performance. Confusion matrices were utilized to assess performance metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 score. Statistical analysis Fleiss's kappa was used to evaluate overall agreement among the YOLOv8 predictions and the expert evaluations, followed by Cohen's kappa for each comparison category. Results For caries detection, the YOLOv8-M model achieved an optimal accuracy of 95.22%, a sensitivity of 84.07%, a specificity of 98.18%, a precision of 92.46%, and an F1 score of 88.06%. For segmentation, the YOLOv8-X model achieved an optimal accuracy of 93.92%, a sensitivity of 78.30%, a specificity of 98.01%, a precision of 91.15%, and an F1 score of 84.24%. Fleiss's kappa analysis indicated substantial agreement of 0.766 ( p < 0.001) between model predictions and expert evaluations. Conclusion The YOLOv8 models demonstrated strong performance in detecting and segmenting dental caries in panoramic radiographs. They also showed substantial agreement with expert assessments, highlighting their potential as a reliable tool for automated caries identification. Further development is recommended to enhance performance, particularly by reducing false positive and false negative cases.

title: Legal and Regulatory Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Use in Medical and Radiology Research.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical imaging and radiology research, improving image acquisition, interpretation, workflow efficiency, and decision support. However, its rapid adoption has introduced complex legal and regulatory challenges involving patient privacy, data governance, algorithm validation, liability, intellectual property, transparency, cybersecurity, and ethical oversight. A comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal landscape is essential for the safe, effective, and legally compliant implementation of AI in radiology. A narrative review of the published literature and current regulatory guidance was conducted. Relevant international legal and regulatory frameworks governing AI in medical imaging were evaluated, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, General Data Protection Regulation, U.S. Food and Drug Administration guidance on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, World Health Organization recommendations, International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, and selected national regulations. Key topics reviewed included data protection, informed consent, AI validation, regulatory approval pathways, post-market surveillance, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, and medico-legal responsibility. Current regulatory frameworks increasingly classify AI-enabled radiology software as SaMD, requiring risk-based evaluation, clinical validation, quality management systems, and continuous post-market performance monitoring. Regulatory authorities emphasize transparency, human oversight, data security, and lifecycle governance of AI systems. Nevertheless, important legal challenges remain, including liability for AI-assisted diagnostic errors, ownership of AI-generated outputs, secondary use of imaging data, cross-border data sharing, algorithmic bias, and regulation of adaptive or continuously learning AI models. The legal framework governing AI in radiology is evolving in parallel with technological innovation. Responsible integration of AI into clinical practice and research requires harmonized international regulations, robust data governance, standardized validation protocols, transparent algorithm development, and clearly defined legal accountability. Continued collaboration among radiologists, researchers, regulators, policymakers, industry, and legal experts will be essential to ensure that AI technologies remain safe, ethical, equitable, and trustworthy while maximizing their potential to improve patient care.

title: The role of thoracic interventional radiologists in the management of chest infections: a pictorial review.
abstract: Thoracic infections remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, requiring accurate and timely diagnosis to guide appropriate treatment. This pictorial review illustrates the role of the interventional thoracic radiologist in the management of infectious processes involving the lung, pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall. We describe a range of non-vascular image-guided percutaneous diagnostic and therapeutic techniques. These include targeted sampling for microbiological identification in complicated pneumonias and cavitary lesions, as well as image-guided drainage of pulmonary, pleural, mediastinal, and thoracic wall infectious collections. The advantages of these minimally invasive percutaneous techniques, especially in peripheral/subpleural lung lesions, are highlighted. In addition, we present practical technical considerations and diagnostic "tips and tricks," aimed at improving diagnostic yield. By integrating imaging findings with interventional strategies, this review underscores the growing clinical impact of interventional radiology in thoracic infections.

title: Vestibular manifestations as the initial presentation of multiple sclerosis: a case series.
abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that can initially present with diverse neurological symptoms. Vestibular dysfunction may be an early manifestation, and can mimic common peripheral vestibular disorders, creating a diagnostic challenge. Objectives To characterize vestibular symptoms and clinical signs in patients with MS presenting initially with vestibular dysfunction. Materials and methods This retrospective observational case series included ten patients evaluated between 2019 and 2024 whose first clinical manifestation of MS was vestibular dysfunction. Clinical and neuro-otologic assessment, vHIT, and VNG were performed, and brain MRI was obtained when central vestibular involvement was suspected. Results Four main presentations were identified: acute vestibular syndrome ( n = 2), imbalance ( n = 4), recurrent vertigo ( n = 2), and positional vertigo ( n = 2). Nine of ten patients had at least one finding suggestive of central vestibular involvement, whereas one patient had a normal vestibular examination. Brain MRI demonstrated lesions fulfilling the radiological criteria for MS in all ten patients. Conclusions Central vestibular signs in young adults presenting with vestibular symptoms should raise suspicion of an underlying central lesion and possible MS. Recognition of these signs, together with appropriate neuroimaging when clinically indicated, may facilitate earlier diagnosis during the clinically isolated syndrome stage.

title: Multimodal based Brain Tumor Classification using Clustered Federated Learning in Edge based IoT Network.
abstract: A brain tumor is characterized by the uncontrolled growth of cells that causes a severe impact on the quality of life. Nowadays, various methods based on multimodal medical images are used to identify brain tumors. Meanwhile, these methods require extensive amounts of labeled information to identify disease tissues and often encounter various challenges based on privacy and accuracy. This paper establishes a Taylor-based Focal Log-cosh Entropy Network (TFLE-Net) to classify brain tumors from demographic data and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images by utilizing clustered federated learning in an edge-based Internet of Things (IoT) network. The detection process is executed in clustered federated learning concerning two entities: server and nodes. In a local training model, an input MRI scan is pre-processed, further brain tumor areas are segmented, and then, the mining of various features is performed. Simultaneously, the normalization of input demographic data is done, and the suitable features are selected using information gain. title: Benchmarking 3D U-Net variants for volumetric segmentation of the substantia nigra and brain ageing related analysis using 7T MRI.
abstract: Objective: Accurate segmentation of the substantia nigra (SN) is essential for assessing its structural integrity and volumetric changes in Parkinson's disease and brain aging. However, it remains challenging due to SN's small size, deep location, and low contrast on conventional MRI. This study benchmarked six U-Net variants baseline 3D U-Net, ResU-Net, SE-U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and U-Net 3+ for SN segmentation using ultra-high-field 7 T MRI. Methods T1-weighted MP2RAGE images from the ATAG dataset (53 healthy subjects: 31 train, 7 validation and 15 test). Six architectures were evaluated: 3D U-Net, ResU-Net, SE-U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and U-Net 3+.Performance was evalauted with Dice score, IoU, 95% HD95, ASSD, and also age-stratified analysis was considered for analysing the robustness of model across young, middle-aged, and elderly cohorts. Results While ResU-Net achieved the highest overlap metrics (Dice = 0.763, IoU = 0.618), where the baseline 3D U-Net outperformed all variants in boundary accuracy (HD95 = 13.85 mm, ASSD = 20.15 mm). The U-Net 3+ and SE-U-Net complex models relatively underperformed, indicated that architectural complexity does not enhance the segmentation performance of small subcortical structures. Descriptive Age-stratified analysis shows, ResU-Net maintained consistent performance across different age groups and 3D U-Net revealed strong age-invariance, however no statistically significant age-group differences were exhibited. Conclusions This study findings demonstrates architecture selection influences overlap, boundary detection and volume estimation small-structure segmentation and highlights the importance of evaluating model robustness to demographic variability. The findings offer a methodological benchmark for developing reliable SN volumetry tools for neurodegenerative research.

title: Long-segment posterior spinal instrumentation with intracanal bone fragment compaction for indirect anterior column support: a single-arm feasibility study in high load-sharing classification score thoracolumbar burst fractures.
abstract: Background Thoracolumbar burst fractures with high Load Sharing Classification (LSC) scores are mechanically unstable and associated with severe vertebral comminution and failure risk after short-segment fixation. This study evaluated outcomes of long-segment posterior fixation combined with intracanal bone fragment compaction as an indirect means of supporting the anterior column. Methods This retrospective study analyzed prospectively collected data from 121 consecutive patients with unstable thoracolumbar burst fractures (T10-L2) and LSC scores >6. All patients underwent open long-segment posterior instrumentation, decompression, and compaction of retropulsed intracanal bone fragments. Radiological outcomes included Cobb angle, percentage of anterior height compression (PAHC), vertebral body compression ratio (VBCR), and spinal canal compromise. Neurological recovery was assessed using the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) scale, and functional outcomes using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Results The cohort included 70 men and 51 women, with a mean age of 37.2 years and follow-up of 23.2 months. At final follow-up, 58.7% (95% CI 49.8-67.1%) achieved ASIA grade E. Significant improvements were observed in VBCR, PAHC, Cobb angle (15.6° to 7.9°; p = 0.008), and spinal canal compromise (65.2% to 8.7%; p < 0.001). Mean ODI improved from 59.4 to 8.4 ( p < 0.001). Conclusion Long-segment posterior fixation with intracanal bone fragment compaction was associated with favorable short- to mid-term neurological, functional, and radiological outcomes. Prospective comparative studies with CT-based fusion assessment, standardized safety reporting, and longer follow-up are required to confirm effectiveness and durability.

title: Impact of cerebral venous outflow on futile recanalization despite complete reperfusion following mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Background A substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke remain functionally dependent despite complete angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 3) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 420 adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent MT between 2015-2025 and achieved mTICI 3 reperfusion. Venous outflow was graded on baseline computed tomography angiography using COVES. Futile recanalization was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Independent associations with futile recanalization were evaluated using multivariable binary logistic regression. Results Futile recanalization occurred in 191 patients (45.5%). After adjustment for age, admission NIHSS, ASPECTS, total passes, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, previous stroke, and arterial collateral status, higher COVES remained independently associated with lower odds of futile recanalization (OR per 1-point increase, 0.649; 95% CI, 0.537-0.784; p < 0.001). Age (OR, 1.031; p = 0.005), admission NIHSS (OR, 1.091; p = 0.001), and total passes (OR, 1.538; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds of futile recanalization. Arterial collateral status was not independently associated with outcome. COVES showed greater discrimination than admission NIHSS (AUC, 0.742 vs 0.624). Conclusions Baseline COVES was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome among patients achieving complete reperfusion after MT. COVES may serve as a complementary prognostic imaging marker rather than a treatment-selection tool. Prospective external validation is required.

title: Deep learning-based segmentation of non-perfused volume after magnetic resonance guided high-intensity focused ultrasound therapies: a retrospective evaluation on clinical patient data.
abstract: Introduction Non-perfused volume (NPV) is a key imaging biomarker for treatment efficacy in MR -guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (MR-HIFU). In uterine fibroids therapies, the NPV ratio is strongly associated with clinical outcomes and long-term efficacy. We developed and clinically evaluated a deep learning-based automatic NPV segmentation model to facilitate standardized and efficient post-treatment assessment. Materials and methods Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MR images from 79 patients treated with MR-HIFU were retrospectively analyzed, with NPVs manually delineated as the reference. A 2D U-Net convolutional neural network was optimized using a Tversky loss function (α = 0.7) to prioritize volumetric robustness. Performance was evaluated using similarity metrics (Dice coefficient [DC], 95th percentile Hausdorff distance [HD95]) and clinically relevant measures, including Bland-Altman analysis of volumetric quantification error, precision, recall, slice-level missing rate, and processing time. Results In the independent test cohort ( n = 12), the model achieved a median DC of 0.900 (IQR: 0.841-0.920) and a median HD95 of 0.42 (IQR: 0.32-0.60) mm. Median absolute NPV quantification error was 4.3 mL (IQR: 2.6-8.4 mL), corresponding to a median relative error of 2.3% (IQR: -2.4% - 10.5%). Precision and recall were 0.909 (IQR: 0.843-0.940) and 0.912 (IQR: 0.881-0.931), respectively, with 2.8% of ground truth-positive slices missed. Average processing time per patient (∼384 slices) was 1-2 min. Conclusion The proposed 2D U-Net provides accurate and time-efficient automatic NPV segmentation. Quantitative and clinically oriented evaluation demonstrates reliable volumetric assessment with minimal slice-level omission, supporting integration into routine MR-HIFU treatment workflows.
